purpose: Read-only reference of the HelixSkill Robotics Atlas for the subject build-out campaign. Reuse these ids rather than adding duplicates, and link new skills to them by id. Answers, positions and lesson text are deliberately left out.

edgeTypes.supports: optional preparation; does not raise level
edgeTypes.related: context only; does not raise level

flags.onI05Path: the I05 milestone depends on it
flags.inCore: some core robotics skill depends on it (scope: robotics outside the extension pathways)

milestones.name: Integrate and verify a controlled joint
Integrate and verify a robot arm
Integrate and verify an autonomous wheeled robot
Verify a repeatable robotic work system

branches.name: Number and algebra foundations
branches.boundary: Number, fractions, ratios and percentages, units-free algebra, equations and inequalities, functions, exponents and logarithms, polynomials, sequences, complex numbers, logic.
branches.excludes: Number theory, proof-based algebra and contest techniques with no robotics use.

branches.name: Calculus and linear algebra
branches.boundary: Limits, derivatives and integrals, differential equations and transforms, multivariable calculus, vectors, matrices and the numerical methods robots use with them.
branches.excludes: Real-analysis proofs; abstract algebra beyond matrices.

branches.name: Geometry, trigonometry, probability and statistics
branches.boundary: Geometry, trigonometry, conic and polar forms, probability, statistics and the estimation mathematics used by sensing and control.
branches.excludes: Euclidean proof; probability theory beyond what estimation and evaluation need.

branches.name: Measurement and uncertainty
branches.boundary: Measuring, units and prefixes, random and systematic error, calibration, uncertainty propagation.

branches.name: Kinematics and forces
branches.boundary: Motion description and graphs, frames of observation, Newtonian forces, free-body models, friction and contact.

branches.name: Work, energy and momentum
branches.boundary: Work, power, energy balances, dissipation, momentum and impulse.

branches.name: Rotation and vibration
branches.boundary: Torque, moments, rotational dynamics, rolling, oscillation, damping and resonance.

branches.name: Fluids and thermal systems
branches.boundary: Pressure, flow and losses, heat transfer basics, thermal energy balances.

branches.name: Fields, induction and waves
branches.boundary: Electric and magnetic fields, induction and back EMF, waves, phase and delay.

branches.name: Optics and modern physics
branches.boundary: Image formation, resolution and sampling for cameras; modern physics only where a sensor needs it.
branches.excludes: Modern physics with no stated robotics application.

branches.name: DC circuit analysis
branches.boundary: Circuits, sources, Ohm and Kirchhoff, networks and equivalents, dividers, DC power and measurement, DC diagnosis.

branches.name: Transient and AC response
branches.boundary: RC and RL transients, phasors, AC power, filters, resonance, inductive current paths.

branches.name: Semiconductors and switching
branches.boundary: Diodes, transistors as switches, device limits, conduction and switching loss.

branches.name: Analog sensing and amplification
branches.boundary: Op-amp circuits, gain and range, comparators and hysteresis, active filters, sensor signal conditioning.

branches.name: Digital timing and conversion
branches.boundary: Logic and timing, sampling and aliasing, ADC and DAC conversion, digital buses and interfaces.

branches.name: Power and motor drives
branches.boundary: PWM, H-bridges and drivers, gate drive and dead time, regulators and converters, batteries, power budgets, protection and thermal operation.

branches.name: Instrumentation and sensor interfaces
branches.boundary: Meters and oscilloscopes, calibration, encoders, IMUs, Hall and bridge sensors, wiring harnesses.

branches.name: PCB layout and interference
branches.boundary: Board layout, grounding and return paths, decoupling and shielding, test points and board diagnosis.

branches.name: Statics and load transfer
branches.boundary: Load paths, free-body diagrams of structures, distributed loads, joints and two-force members, trusses.

branches.name: Stress, strain and material response
branches.boundary: Normal and shear stress and strain, elastic and plastic response, Poisson effects, tensile testing, creep.

branches.name: Members, deformation and stability
branches.boundary: Torsion, bending, section properties, deflection, buckling, finite-element use and checks.

branches.name: Failure and durability
branches.boundary: Failure criteria, stress concentration, fracture, fatigue, wear, safety factors and design margins.

branches.name: Material families and processing
branches.boundary: Metals, polymers, ceramics and composites, structure and bonding, processing routes and their effect on properties.

branches.name: Joints, manufacturing and tolerances
branches.boundary: Fasteners and preload, welding and adhesives, fits, datums, tolerance stacks.

branches.name: Thermal and environmental behavior
branches.boundary: Thermal expansion and resistance, lumped thermal models, conduction and convection, corrosion and coatings, materials thermodynamics.

branches.name: Mechanical design, CAD and fabrication
branches.boundary: Reading and making CAD parts, assemblies and drawings, workholding and tools, fabrication, inspection, material and process selection for robot parts.
branches.excludes: Training in a particular CAD product (inside lessons only).

branches.name: Programming and development practice
branches.boundary: Files and text, first programs, algorithms, functions and contracts, testing, debugging, version control, reproducible builds.

branches.name: Algorithms and numerical computing
branches.boundary: Data structures, graphs, cost and latency, floating point and numerical error.

branches.name: Systems, memory and concurrency
branches.boundary: Computer architecture, memory and ownership, processes and threads, races and deadlock.

branches.name: Networking, embedded and real time
branches.boundary: Microcontroller I/O, interrupts, timed acquisition, device communication, real-time scheduling, message framing, secure remote access.

branches.name: Robot software and integration
branches.boundary: Robot programs, messages and coordinate conventions, state machines, logging and replay, simulation, software integration.
branches.excludes: A particular robot framework as a skill (inside lessons only).

branches.name: Machine learning for robots
branches.boundary: Evaluation and leakage, metrics, overfitting, deploying models under robot constraints.

branches.name: Frames and rigid motion
branches.boundary: Frames and conventions, rotations and their representations, points versus directions, composing and inverting rigid transforms.

branches.name: Configuration and kinematics
branches.boundary: Degrees of freedom, configuration, task and joint space, forward and inverse kinematics, joint limits.

branches.name: Jacobians, statics and dynamics
branches.boundary: Velocity Jacobians, singularities, mapping loads to joint torques, spatial motion and force, dynamic model terms.

branches.name: Actuation and transmissions
branches.boundary: Transmissions and ratios, torque and losses, reflected inertia, encoders on joints, actuator and driver selection, backlash and compliance.

branches.name: Trajectories and feedback
branches.boundary: Timed trajectories, feedback and PID in practice, saturation and windup, sampled control, feedforward, state feedback and observers.

branches.name: Estimation and sensor fusion
branches.boundary: Sensor calibration, noise and covariance, timing alignment, inertial orientation, state estimation and fusion, innovation checks.

branches.name: Perception, localization and navigation
branches.boundary: Camera models and calibration, depth and pose estimation, differential drive, odometry, maps, localization, route planning, path tracking, obstacles, SLAM evaluation.

branches.name: Planning and manipulation
branches.boundary: Collision geometry, motion planning and timing, contact and grasp, grippers, pick-and-place, mobile manipulation.

branches.name: System integration and validation
branches.boundary: Requirements, interfaces and budgets, staged commissioning, verification and fault injection, diagnosis, reliability trials, configuration control, handover.

branches.name: Robot fault handling and safety
branches.boundary: Hazard identification and protective functions, bounded fault response, lost-sensor detection and recovery, stop and restart, holding and power-loss behavior.

branches.name: Calibration and identification
branches.boundary: Robot parameter identification versus sensor calibration, identifying actuator models, designing identification experiments.

branches.name: Mechanical machine elements
branches.boundary: Bearings and shaft supports, couplings and misalignment, joint modules.

branches.name: Integration milestones (I01–I05)
branches.boundary: The five physical build-and-verify milestones that define "done" (docs/SCOPE.md §3.1).

branches.name: Advanced pathways (X01–X09)
branches.boundary: Labelled extensions beyond the core (docs/SCOPE.md §3.2); X10 is a roadmap note and out of scope.

skills.name: Counting and place value
skills.description: Count objects and read a numeral by the value each digit carries in its position.

skills.name: Addition and subtraction
skills.description: Combine quantities or find their difference while keeping units consistent.

skills.name: Multiplication and division
skills.description: Interpret equal groups, scale factors, and the inverse operation of division.

skills.name: Signed numbers
skills.description: Represent positive and negative values on a number line and calculate with their signs.

skills.name: Factors and multiples
skills.description: Find divisors, common factors, and common multiples of integers.

skills.name: Prime factorization
skills.description: Express an integer as a product of primes and use that representation to compare divisibility.

skills.name: Fractions and equivalence
skills.description: Represent a part-to-whole ratio and reduce or expand it without changing its value.

skills.name: Adding unlike fractions
skills.description: Rewrite fractions over a common denominator before adding or subtracting them.

skills.name: Fraction products and quotients
skills.description: Multiply fractional scale factors and divide by multiplying by a nonzero reciprocal.

skills.name: Decimals and rounding
skills.description: Convert between fractions and decimal representations and round to a stated precision.

skills.name: Percentages
skills.description: Express a ratio per hundred and calculate a part, a percentage, or a whole.

skills.name: Relative and percentage change
skills.description: Compare a change with its reference value while distinguishing the reference from the result.

skills.name: Ratios and unit rates
skills.description: Compare quantities multiplicatively and express a rate for one unit of input.

skills.name: Direct and inverse proportion
skills.description: Distinguish constant-ratio (direct) relationships from constant-product (inverse) relationships.

skills.name: Integer powers
skills.description: Evaluate repeated multiplication, zero powers, and negative powers for nonzero bases.

skills.name: Exponent rules
skills.description: Simplify products, quotients, and powers of powers using compatible bases.

skills.name: Scientific notation
skills.description: Write numbers as a coefficient times a power of ten and compare orders of magnitude.

skills.name: Roots and radicals
skills.description: Find values whose integer powers give a specified quantity and identify real-domain restrictions.

skills.name: Simplifying radicals
skills.description: Extract perfect-power factors from radicals and combine like radicals.

skills.name: Fractional exponents
skills.description: Relate rational powers to roots and respect restrictions for real-valued bases.

skills.name: Order of operations for basic arithmetic
skills.description: Evaluate grouped arithmetic expressions using a consistent precedence convention.

skills.name: Absolute value and distance
skills.description: Interpret magnitude independently of sign and measure the distance between numbers on a number line.

skills.name: Variables and expressions
skills.description: Use symbols for changeable quantities and evaluate an expression at assigned values.

skills.name: Collecting terms and distribution
skills.description: Expand grouped sums and combine terms representing the same symbolic quantity.

skills.name: Linear equations in one unknown
skills.description: Preserve equality while isolating an unknown through inverse operations.

skills.name: Rearranging formulas
skills.description: Isolate a chosen variable in a formula containing several symbolic quantities.

skills.name: Linear inequalities and intervals
skills.description: Represent a permitted range and reverse an inequality when multiplying by a negative value.

skills.name: Cartesian coordinates
skills.description: Locate points using independently signed axes and maintain a stated axis convention.

skills.name: Slope and intercept
skills.description: Calculate rise per run and connect a straight-line graph to its equation.

skills.name: Two-variable linear systems
skills.description: Solve simultaneous linear constraints by elimination or substitution and recognize inconsistent systems.

skills.name: Polynomial arithmetic
skills.description: Add, multiply, and collect expressions with nonnegative integer powers.

skills.name: Factoring polynomials
skills.description: Rewrite a polynomial as a product using common factors and standard identities.

skills.name: Solving quadratic equations
skills.description: Find roots using factoring or the quadratic formula and interpret the discriminant.

skills.name: Completing the square
skills.description: Rewrite a quadratic as a shifted square plus a constant.

skills.name: Polynomial division
skills.description: Divide polynomials with a quotient and remainder and connect a zero remainder to a factor.

skills.name: Rational expressions and restrictions
skills.description: Simplify ratios of polynomials while retaining excluded denominator zeros.

skills.name: Rational equations
skills.description: Clear valid denominators and reject candidates outside the original domain.

skills.name: Radical equations
skills.description: Isolate a radical, raise to a power, and check candidates in the original equation.

skills.name: Functions, domains, and ranges
skills.description: Treat a function as a rule assigning one output to each allowed input.

skills.name: Function composition
skills.description: Apply one function to the output of another in a stated order.

skills.name: Inverse functions
skills.description: Reverse a one-to-one mapping and restrict the domain when needed.

skills.name: Transforming function graphs
skills.description: Predict shifts, scaling, and reflections caused by changing a function's input or output.

skills.name: Piecewise functions
skills.description: Define different formulas on different input intervals and handle the boundaries explicitly.

skills.name: Exponential models
skills.description: Model constant multiplicative change and distinguish it from constant additive change.

skills.name: Logarithms
skills.description: Interpret a logarithm as an exponent and apply product, quotient, and power rules.

skills.name: Exponential and logarithmic equations
skills.description: Solve for an unknown in an exponent or logarithm while checking the allowed domain.

skills.name: Polynomial roots and graph shape
skills.description: Relate root multiplicity and leading terms to crossings and end behavior.

skills.name: Rational graphs and asymptotes
skills.description: Identify poles, removable holes, and limiting behavior of rational functions.

skills.name: Angles and geometric relationships
skills.description: Measure turns and use parallel-line, triangle, and polygon angle relationships.

skills.name: Perimeter and planar area
skills.description: Calculate boundary length and enclosed area for elementary shapes.

skills.name: Surface area and volume
skills.description: Calculate the exposed area and enclosed volume of common solids.

skills.name: Similarity and scale drawings
skills.description: Use equal angles and proportional lengths to transfer measurements between similar shapes.

skills.name: Right-triangle distances
skills.description: Relate the legs and hypotenuse of a right triangle and choose the correct side to solve for.

skills.name: Right-triangle trigonometry
skills.description: Use sine, cosine, and tangent as side ratios with a clearly identified angle.

skills.name: Radians and arc length
skills.description: Measure angle as arc length divided by radius and convert between radians and degrees.

skills.name: Unit-circle trigonometry
skills.description: Extend sine and cosine to all angles using coordinates on a unit circle.

skills.name: Periodic functions and phase
skills.description: Describe amplitude, period, frequency, and phase in a sinusoidal graph.

skills.name: Inverse trigonometry and quadrants
skills.description: Recover angles from ratios and resolve the quadrant ambiguity using both components.

skills.name: Trigonometric identities
skills.description: Transform trigonometric expressions using angle and Pythagorean identities.

skills.name: Trigonometric equations
skills.description: Find all relevant angle solutions in a specified interval rather than only a principal value.

skills.name: General triangle solutions
skills.description: Use sine and cosine laws for triangles that are not right triangles.

skills.name: Circles and conic curves
skills.description: Interpret equations of circles, ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas in terms of their geometry.

skills.name: Parametric curves
skills.description: Represent each coordinate as a function of a shared parameter.

skills.name: Polar coordinates
skills.description: Locate points by distance from the origin and angle, and convert between polar and Cartesian coordinates.

skills.name: Limits of functions
skills.description: Describe the value a function approaches near an input using graphs, tables, and algebra.

skills.name: Continuity and discontinuities
skills.description: Check whether a function's value and its limiting behaviour agree at a point, and classify any breaks.

skills.name: Derivative as local rate
skills.description: Define a derivative through a shrinking difference quotient and interpret it as an instantaneous rate with units.

skills.name: Power, product, and quotient differentiation
skills.description: Differentiate powers, sums, products, and quotients of algebraic functions with the appropriate rules.

skills.name: Chain rule
skills.description: Differentiate a composite function by multiplying the outer derivative by the derivative of the inner function.

skills.name: Trigonometric and exponential derivatives
skills.description: Differentiate exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions, keeping angles in radians.

skills.name: Implicit differentiation
skills.description: Differentiate a relation between x and y without first solving explicitly for one variable.

skills.name: Higher derivatives
skills.description: Differentiate repeatedly and interpret second and higher derivatives as rates of change of rates.

skills.name: Local linear approximation
skills.description: Approximate a smooth function near a chosen point by its tangent line, L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x − a).

skills.name: Single-variable optimization
skills.description: Find maximum or minimum values by locating critical points and comparing them with boundary values.

skills.name: Related rates
skills.description: Connect the time derivatives of quantities that are linked by a common equation.

skills.name: Antiderivatives
skills.description: Recover a family of functions from its derivative and use an initial condition to fix the integration constant.

skills.name: Definite integrals and accumulation
skills.description: Interpret a definite integral as signed accumulation, built as the limit of increasingly fine Riemann sums.

skills.name: Fundamental theorem of calculus
skills.description: Connect accumulation with differentiation and evaluate definite integrals as F(b) − F(a) using antiderivatives.

skills.name: Integration by substitution
skills.description: Change variables to reverse a chain-rule pattern, converting bounds consistently for definite integrals.

skills.name: Integration by parts
skills.description: Reverse the product rule, ∫ u dv = uv − ∫ v du, to trade one integral for an easier one.

skills.name: Partial-fraction integration
skills.description: Decompose a rational function into simpler fractions so that each piece can be integrated directly.

skills.name: Improper integrals
skills.description: Evaluate integrals over unbounded intervals or with unbounded integrands by taking limits.

skills.name: Numerical quadrature
skills.description: Approximate a definite integral from function values or samples using rectangle, trapezoid, or Simpson rules.

skills.name: Arc length and surface of revolution
skills.description: Find the length of a curve or the area of a surface of revolution by accumulating small straight pieces.

skills.name: Sequences and finite sums
skills.description: Define indexed values explicitly or recursively and use summation notation to add them.

skills.name: Geometric series
skills.description: Sum terms with a constant ratio and determine when an infinite geometric sum converges.

skills.name: Convergence of series
skills.description: Decide whether an infinite series converges or diverges using partial sums, comparison, and standard tests.

skills.name: Taylor approximation
skills.description: Build a polynomial approximation from a function's derivatives at an expansion point, and judge its accuracy.

skills.name: Vector components and arithmetic
skills.description: Represent a vector by ordered components and combine vectors component by component.

skills.name: Vector length and normalization
skills.description: Compute a vector's Euclidean length and divide by it to form a unit vector in the same direction, when the vector is nonzero.

skills.name: Dot products and projection
skills.description: Compute the dot product of two vectors and use it to find angles, test perpendicularity, and project one vector onto another.

skills.name: Cross products
skills.description: Form the vector perpendicular to two 3D vectors, with length equal to their parallelogram area and direction set by the right-hand rule.

skills.name: Matrix arithmetic
skills.description: Add, scale, transpose, and multiply matrices while tracking dimensions and the order of multiplication.

skills.name: Gaussian elimination
skills.description: Use row operations to reduce a linear system to echelon form, then identify pivot and free variables and solve.

skills.name: Determinants
skills.description: Compute the determinant of a square matrix and interpret it as a signed volume scale factor, with zero meaning the matrix is singular.

skills.name: Matrix inverses
skills.description: Find the inverse of a square matrix when its determinant is nonzero and use it to undo a transformation or solve a system.

skills.name: Span and linear independence
skills.description: Determine which vectors can be built from linear combinations of a set, and whether any vector in the set is redundant.

skills.name: Bases and dimension
skills.description: Choose an independent spanning set as a basis, express vectors by their coordinates in it, and count dimension.

skills.name: Rank and null spaces
skills.description: Find a matrix's rank, the number of independent output directions, and its null space, the inputs sent to zero.

skills.name: Linear transformations
skills.description: Represent maps that preserve addition and scaling as matrices, and identify their image and kernel.

skills.name: Changing basis
skills.description: Convert a vector's coordinates, or a transformation's matrix, from one basis to another without changing the underlying object.

skills.name: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
skills.description: Find the special directions a matrix only stretches or flips, and the scale factors (eigenvalues) along them.

skills.name: Diagonalization
skills.description: Rewrite a matrix as PDP⁻¹ using a basis of eigenvectors, so it acts as independent scalings along those directions.

skills.name: Orthogonality and orthonormal bases
skills.description: Build sets of mutually perpendicular unit vectors, use them as bases, and recognize orthogonal matrices that preserve lengths and angles.

skills.name: Gram-Schmidt and QR
skills.description: Turn independent vectors into an orthonormal basis with Gram-Schmidt, and factor a matrix as A = QR.

skills.name: Linear least-squares fitting
skills.description: Choose parameters that minimize the sum of squared residuals when a linear model has more equations than unknowns.

skills.name: Symmetric matrices and quadratic forms
skills.description: Write quadratic expressions as xᵀAx with a symmetric matrix A and classify them as positive definite, negative definite, or indefinite.

skills.name: Singular value decomposition
skills.description: Factor any matrix as UΣVᵀ, revealing orthogonal input and output directions and the nonnegative scale factors between them.

skills.name: Pseudoinverses
skills.description: Generalize the inverse to rectangular or singular matrices, giving least-squares and minimum-norm solutions to linear systems.

skills.name: LU factorization
skills.description: Factor a matrix into lower- and upper-triangular parts, with row pivoting when needed, to solve repeated linear systems efficiently.

skills.name: Matrix exponentials
skills.description: Define e^A for a square matrix through its power series and use it to solve linear systems of differential equations.

skills.name: Functions of several variables
skills.description: Describe scalar or vector outputs depending on several independent inputs.

skills.name: Partial derivatives
skills.description: Differentiate with respect to one input while holding the others fixed.

skills.name: Gradients and directional derivatives
skills.description: Collect partial derivatives into a vector and use it to find the rate of change in any direction.

skills.name: Jacobian matrices
skills.description: Collect first derivatives of a vector mapping into the matrix of its local linear transformation.

skills.name: Multivariable chain rule
skills.description: Differentiate compositions of multivariable functions by adding the contributions through each intermediate variable.

skills.name: Hessians and local curvature
skills.description: Collect second partial derivatives into a matrix and use it to classify critical points by local curvature.

skills.name: Constrained extrema
skills.description: Find maxima and minima of a function restricted by constraints, using Lagrange multipliers and boundary checks.

skills.name: Double and triple integration
skills.description: Accumulate a density over a two- or three-dimensional region using iterated integrals with valid bounds.

skills.name: Integration in transformed coordinates
skills.description: Change integration coordinates and include the Jacobian determinant as the area or volume scale factor.

skills.name: Vector fields
skills.description: Assign a vector to each point in a region, as with forces, velocities, or fluid flows.

skills.name: Divergence and curl
skills.description: Measure local spreading and circulation of a vector field through spatial derivatives.

skills.name: Line integrals
skills.description: Accumulate a scalar density or the tangential part of a vector field along a curved path.

skills.name: Conservative fields and potentials
skills.description: Recognize when a vector field is a gradient, so its line integrals depend only on the endpoints.

skills.name: Surface integrals and flux
skills.description: Accumulate a quantity over a surface, or the flow of a field through it, using a consistently oriented normal.

skills.name: Green, Stokes, and divergence theorems
skills.description: Relate integrals over a boundary to integrals of derivatives, such as curl or divergence, over the interior.

skills.name: Differential equations and initial values
skills.description: State a relationship between an unknown function and its derivatives, together with the initial data needed to fix a unique solution.

skills.name: Separable differential equations
skills.description: Separate variable factors, integrate, and account for equilibrium solutions and initial conditions.

skills.name: First-order linear equations
skills.description: Use an integrating factor to solve a linear first-order equation.

skills.name: Second-order linear equations
skills.description: Solve a·y'' + b·y' + c·y = g(t) using characteristic roots for the natural response plus a particular solution for the forcing.

skills.name: Phase portraits and equilibria
skills.description: Picture an autonomous system's states as points in phase space, sketch trajectories, and locate and classify equilibria.

skills.name: Linear systems of ODEs
skills.description: Write coupled first-order equations as a matrix equation x' = Ax and solve it with eigenvalues, eigenvectors, or the matrix exponential.

skills.name: Local linear stability
skills.description: Linearize near an equilibrium and interpret eigenvalues with attention to inconclusive cases.

skills.name: Laplace transforms
skills.description: Transform time functions and derivative equations into a complex-frequency representation.

skills.name: Inverse Laplace methods
skills.description: Recover time responses through decomposition and transform pairs.

skills.name: Fourier series
skills.description: Represent a periodic function as a sum of sines and cosines at a fundamental frequency and its whole-number multiples.

skills.name: Euler time stepping
skills.description: Advance a state with its local derivative and a chosen finite time step.

skills.name: Runge-Kutta integration
skills.description: Combine several derivative evaluations within a step to improve a numerical trajectory estimate.

skills.name: Numerical error and stability
skills.description: Separate truncation error, accumulated roundoff, and amplification caused by the integration scheme.

skills.name: Sets and event operations
skills.description: Describe set membership, union, intersection, and complement, and use these operations to represent events.

skills.name: Probability rules
skills.description: Assign consistent probabilities to events and combine disjoint alternatives.

skills.name: Permutations and combinations
skills.description: Count ordered or unordered selections without listing every possibility.

skills.name: Conditional probability and independence
skills.description: Update the sample space after an observation and distinguish independence from mutual exclusion.

skills.name: Bayesian updating
skills.description: Combine a prior probability and observation likelihood using a normalizing evidence term.

skills.name: Random variables and distributions
skills.description: Map outcomes to numerical values and describe their mass or cumulative distribution.

skills.name: Expectation and variance
skills.description: Compute a random variable's probability-weighted mean and its squared spread around that mean.

skills.name: Bernoulli and binomial models
skills.description: Model repeated binary trials under the stated independence and equal-probability assumptions.

skills.name: Poisson event counts
skills.description: Model counts over an interval when a constant-rate independent-event approximation is appropriate.

skills.name: Continuous probability densities
skills.description: Obtain interval probabilities by integrating a nonnegative density.

skills.name: Normal distributions and standard scores
skills.description: Represent a Gaussian distribution with a mean and standard deviation and standardize values.

skills.name: Joint and marginal distributions
skills.description: Describe several random variables together and recover marginal or conditional distributions.

skills.name: Covariance and correlation
skills.description: Measure joint variation and assemble covariance matrices without equating correlation with causation.

skills.name: Sampling and bias
skills.description: Distinguish a population from an observed sample and identify selection or measurement bias.

skills.name: Central limit behavior
skills.description: Explain when normalized sums approach a Gaussian distribution and where the approximation can fail.

skills.name: Confidence intervals
skills.description: Construct an interval procedure with a stated long-run coverage under a statistical model.

skills.name: Hypothesis tests and error types
skills.description: Compare evidence against a specified null model and distinguish false positives from false negatives.

skills.name: Regression and residual analysis
skills.description: Fit a relationship and inspect residual patterns rather than relying only on a fitted line.

skills.name: Maximum-likelihood estimation
skills.description: Choose parameters that make the observed data most likely within a stated model.

skills.name: Propositions and truth tables
skills.description: Combine statements using logical operators and evaluate truth under each input combination.

skills.name: Quantifiers and implications
skills.description: Distinguish claims about every case from claims about at least one case and interpret implication.

skills.name: Direct proof and counterexamples
skills.description: Justify a claim from assumptions or disprove a universal claim with a valid counterexample.

skills.name: Mathematical induction
skills.description: Prove a base case and an implication from one indexed case to the next.

skills.name: Binary and hexadecimal representation
skills.description: Represent integers in different bases and translate between binary and hexadecimal.

skills.name: Boolean algebra
skills.description: Simplify logical functions of 0/1 variables using Boolean identities such as absorption and De Morgan's laws.

skills.name: Modular arithmetic
skills.description: Calculate with remainders and interpret congruence classes.

skills.name: Recurrence relations
skills.description: Define a sequence from earlier values and analyze elementary recurrence models.

skills.name: Graphs, paths, and connectivity
skills.description: Represent entities and their pairwise connections as graphs, and distinguish directed from undirected paths and connectivity.

skills.name: Trees and spanning trees
skills.description: Recognize connected acyclic graphs and select a spanning tree of a connected graph.

skills.name: Directed acyclic graphs and ordering
skills.description: Identify directed cycles and form an ordering consistent with every dependency.

skills.name: Graph traversal and shortest paths
skills.description: Explore connectivity systematically and distinguish unweighted from weighted shortest paths.

skills.name: Algorithm growth rates
skills.description: Compare how computation grows with input size using asymptotic bounds.

skills.name: Complex-number arithmetic
skills.description: Extend real arithmetic with an imaginary unit whose square is minus one and use conjugates for division.

skills.name: Polar form and Euler's formula
skills.description: Represent a complex value through magnitude and angle and connect complex exponentials with rotation.

skills.name: Powers and roots of complex numbers
skills.description: Use magnitude and angle to find powers and all distinct roots of a nonzero complex value.

skills.name: Newton's method for roots
skills.description: Use a local tangent line to generate improved root estimates, and check convergence rather than assuming it.

skills.name: Finite-difference derivatives
skills.description: Estimate a derivative from nearby sampled values using forward, backward, or central differences with an explicit step size.

skills.name: Mean, median, and mode
skills.description: Compute common summaries of a data set's center and distinguish their sensitivity to unusual values.

skills.name: Sample variance and standard deviation
skills.description: Summarize squared deviations from a mean and distinguish sample from population conventions.

skills.name: Quartiles, percentiles, and outliers
skills.description: Locate ordered-data cutoffs and distinguish a flagged observation from a proven error.

skills.name: Histograms and distribution shape
skills.description: Group observations into intervals and examine shape while accounting for bin choice.

skills.name: Overlapping events and total probability
skills.description: Account for overlap when combining events and partition cases to compute an overall probability.

skills.name: Proof by contradiction
skills.description: Prove a claim by assuming it is false, keeping the original assumptions, and deriving a logical impossibility.

skills.name: Contrapositive reasoning
skills.description: Replace an implication with its logically equivalent contrapositive and distinguish it from the converse.

skills.name: Binomial expansion
skills.description: Expand a nonnegative integer power of a sum using combinatorial coefficients.

skills.name: Abstract vector spaces
skills.description: Recognize vector-space structure in objects such as polynomials, matrices, or functions that obey the vector-space axioms.

skills.name: Lines and planes in space
skills.description: Describe lines and planes in 3D using points, direction vectors, and normal vectors, and find intersections and distances.

skills.name: Cylindrical and spherical coordinates
skills.description: Represent a spatial point through radial and angular variables with an explicit convention.

skills.name: Conditioning and numerical sensitivity
skills.description: Distinguish how sensitive a problem is to small data changes from how stable the algorithm used to solve it is.

skills.name: Physical quantities and SI units
skills.description: Express a physical quantity as a number together with a unit, using the SI system as the common standard.

skills.name: Unit conversions
skills.description: Change a quantity to different units by multiplying by conversion factors equal to one, including for squared and cubed units.

skills.name: Dimensional consistency
skills.description: Check that terms added, subtracted, or equated in a formula have the same physical dimensions.

skills.name: Significant figures and resolution
skills.description: Report measurements with digits that match the instrument's resolution, and keep resolution distinct from accuracy.

skills.name: Measurement uncertainty
skills.description: Quantify the doubt in a measurement as a range and identify random and systematic contributions.

skills.name: Interpreting physical graphs
skills.description: Read axes, units, slopes, and areas of graphs as physical quantities in measurement and motion problems.

skills.name: Systems, assumptions, and models
skills.description: Choose what to include in a system and state which effects a physical model deliberately ignores.

skills.name: Position and displacement
skills.description: Describe an object's location and the signed change between two locations in a chosen frame.

skills.name: Speed and average velocity
skills.description: Distinguish distance per time from displacement per time.

skills.name: Acceleration
skills.description: Measure how velocity changes over time, including changes of direction.

skills.name: Constant-acceleration motion
skills.description: Use constant-acceleration relations only over intervals where the assumption is suitable.

skills.name: Free fall near Earth
skills.description: Model vertical motion under approximately constant gravitational acceleration when drag is negligible.

skills.name: Motion graphs and piecewise motion
skills.description: Translate between position, velocity, and acceleration graphs across successive time intervals.

skills.name: Two-dimensional motion components
skills.description: Resolve planar position, velocity, and acceleration into independent components.

skills.name: Projectile trajectories
skills.description: Combine horizontal and vertical motion with a shared time parameter.

skills.name: Relative motion and reference frames
skills.description: Relate observed velocities in frames moving at constant relative velocity.

skills.name: Mass, inertia, and net force
skills.description: Distinguish inertial mass from force and relate zero net force to constant velocity.

skills.name: Free-body diagrams
skills.description: Isolate one body and draw only external forces acting on that body.

skills.name: Newton's second law in components
skills.description: Relate the vector sum of external forces to mass times acceleration.

skills.name: Interaction pairs and multiple bodies
skills.description: Identify equal and opposite interaction forces acting on different bodies.

skills.name: Weight, normal force, and tension
skills.description: Model common contact and support forces without assuming the normal force always equals weight.

skills.name: Static and kinetic friction
skills.description: Distinguish a variable static-friction force up to a limit from a simplified sliding-friction model.

skills.name: Inclined-plane dynamics
skills.description: Resolve forces relative to a slope and solve for equilibrium or acceleration.

skills.name: Coupled masses and pulleys
skills.description: Use shared geometric constraints to solve interacting-body accelerations and forces.

skills.name: Uniform circular motion
skills.description: Relate radius and speed to inward acceleration even when speed is constant.

skills.name: Universal gravitation
skills.description: Model the inverse-square attraction between masses under the point-mass or spherical approximation.

skills.name: Circular orbits
skills.description: Balance the required inward acceleration with gravitational acceleration for a circular orbit.

skills.name: Work by a constant force
skills.description: Calculate energy transfer through the component of force along displacement.

skills.name: Kinetic energy and work-energy balance
skills.description: Relate net work to a change in translational kinetic energy.

skills.name: Gravitational and spring potential energy
skills.description: Represent recoverable energy associated with height or ideal spring deformation.

skills.name: Mechanical energy accounting
skills.description: Track energy transfers and losses across a chosen system boundary.

skills.name: Mechanical power and efficiency
skills.description: Calculate energy transfer per time and compare useful output with input.

skills.name: Linear momentum
skills.description: Represent mass times velocity as a vector property of motion.

skills.name: Impulse and momentum change
skills.description: Relate the area under a force-time curve to a change in momentum.

skills.name: Collision models
skills.description: Combine momentum conservation with the appropriate energy or restitution assumptions.

skills.name: Center of mass
skills.description: Compute the mass-weighted position of a system of particles.

skills.name: Angular position, speed, and acceleration
skills.description: Describe rotational motion with an angle and its rates of change, angular velocity and angular acceleration.

skills.name: Torque and lever arms
skills.description: Describe and calculate the turning effect of a force about a point or axis using lever arms and τ = r × F.

skills.name: Force and torque equilibrium
skills.description: Require both net force and net torque to vanish for static equilibrium, and use those conditions to solve for unknown forces.

skills.name: Mass moment of inertia
skills.description: Describe how a body's mass distribution resists angular acceleration about a specified axis.

skills.name: Parallel-axis theorem
skills.description: Transfer a mass moment of inertia from a center-of-mass axis to any parallel axis using I = I_cm + Md².

skills.name: Rotational dynamics about a fixed axis
skills.description: Relate net axial torque to angular acceleration, τ = Iα, for a rigid body with constant moment of inertia.

skills.name: Rotational kinetic energy and power
skills.description: Track rotational kinetic energy ½Iω² and relate torque times angular speed to power.

skills.name: Angular momentum conservation
skills.description: Track angular momentum L = Iω, which stays constant when the net external torque is zero and otherwise changes at the rate of that torque.

skills.name: Rolling without slipping
skills.description: Couple linear travel and angular rotation through the no-slip contact constraint.

skills.name: Ideal springs and restoring forces
skills.description: Model a spring's restoring force as F = −kx, proportional to displacement, within the range where the spring behaves linearly.

skills.name: Simple harmonic motion
skills.description: Relate sinusoidal motion to a restoring force proportional to displacement, x(t) = A cos(ωt + φ).

skills.name: Small-angle pendulum model
skills.description: Approximate a pendulum as a harmonic oscillator when its angular excursion is small.

skills.name: Motion through differentiation and integration
skills.description: Relate position, velocity, and acceleration as continuous-time derivatives and integrals.

skills.name: Work from a variable force
skills.description: Find work as the integral of the force component along a path, W = ∫ F · dr, when force or direction varies.

skills.name: Viscous damping and transient response
skills.description: Model velocity-proportional resistance and distinguish underdamped, critical, and overdamped response.

skills.name: Forced vibration and resonance
skills.description: Analyze how forcing frequency interacts with natural dynamics and damping to produce large vibration near resonance.

skills.name: Lagrangian mechanics
skills.description: Form equations of motion from kinetic and potential energy using generalized coordinates.

skills.name: Density and specific volume
skills.description: Relate mass to occupied volume and distinguish density from total mass.

skills.name: Pressure and hydrostatics
skills.description: Relate normal force to area and model pressure changes with depth in a static fluid.

skills.name: Hydraulic force transmission
skills.description: Use pressure transmission in an ideal confined fluid to relate piston forces and areas.

skills.name: Buoyancy
skills.description: Relate buoyant force to the weight of displaced fluid.

skills.name: Fluid continuity
skills.description: Use conservation of mass to relate flow rate, cross section, and velocity.

skills.name: Bernoulli energy relation
skills.description: Relate pressure, speed, and elevation along a suitable ideal-flow streamline.

skills.name: Temperature and thermal equilibrium
skills.description: Distinguish temperature from thermal energy and identify thermal equilibrium.

skills.name: Heat capacity and phase-change energy
skills.description: Calculate sensible or latent energy transfer using the appropriate material property.

skills.name: Ideal-gas relationships
skills.description: Relate pressure, volume, temperature, and amount under an ideal-gas approximation.

skills.name: First law of thermodynamics
skills.description: Track internal-energy changes using a clearly stated heat and work sign convention.

skills.name: Entropy and the second law
skills.description: Describe the direction and limitations of energy conversion and entropy generation.

skills.name: Thermodynamic cycles
skills.description: Track a system through a cycle and interpret work on a pressure-volume diagram.

skills.name: Electric charge and conservation
skills.description: Describe electric charge and its redistribution without treating charge as consumed by a circuit.

skills.name: Electric force and field
skills.description: Relate forces on charges to an electric field and use simple charge models.

skills.name: Electric potential and voltage
skills.description: Interpret potential difference as energy transfer per unit charge.

skills.name: Magnetic fields and forces
skills.description: Relate moving charges and currents to magnetic forces using consistent directions.

skills.name: Magnetic flux
skills.description: Measure the component of magnetic field passing through an area.

skills.name: Faraday and Lenz induction
skills.description: Relate changing magnetic flux to induced voltage and its opposing tendency.

skills.name: Wave speed, frequency, and wavelength
skills.description: Use v = fλ to link how fast a wave travels, how often it oscillates, and the spacing of its crests.

skills.name: Wave superposition and interference
skills.description: Add wave disturbances and distinguish constructive from destructive interference.

skills.name: Standing waves and modes
skills.description: Relate boundary conditions to standing-wave patterns and allowed resonances.

skills.name: Doppler shifts
skills.description: Relate relative source and observer motion to an observed frequency shift in an appropriate model.

skills.name: Reflection and ray diagrams
skills.description: Trace light rays off mirrors and surfaces, measuring angles from the normal so the reflection angle equals the incidence angle.

skills.name: Refraction and total internal reflection
skills.description: Relate propagation direction to refractive-index changes and identify a critical angle when applicable.

skills.name: Thin-lens image formation
skills.description: Relate object distance, image distance, and focal length with a stated sign convention.

skills.name: Diffraction and resolution
skills.description: Describe how waves spread through apertures and around edges, and how this limits the resolution of optical systems.

skills.name: Polarization of light
skills.description: Describe electric-field orientation and how polarizing elements affect transmitted intensity.

skills.name: Electromagnetic spectrum
skills.description: Relate wavelength and frequency across electromagnetic radiation bands.

skills.name: Photon energy and photoelectric response
skills.description: Relate photon energy to frequency and distinguish quantum energy thresholds from intensity.

skills.name: Current and charge flow
skills.description: Interpret electric current as charge transferred per unit time and choose consistent reference directions.

skills.name: Voltage references and ground
skills.description: Choose a voltage reference node and distinguish a circuit's signal ground from a physical earth connection.

skills.name: Resistance and Ohm's law
skills.description: Relate voltage, current, and resistance for an ohmic element and recognise when Ohm's law does not apply.

skills.name: Electrical power and dissipation
skills.description: Calculate electrical power and energy, including resistive heating, and check that parts can dissipate it safely.

skills.name: Reading schematics and connectivity
skills.description: Identify components, nodes, branches, and intended electrical connections when reading a schematic diagram.

skills.name: Series resistor networks
skills.description: Combine resistors that carry the same current by adding their values, and find how the voltage divides among them.

skills.name: Parallel resistor networks
skills.description: Combine resistors that share the same voltage, add their branch currents, and find the equivalent resistance.

skills.name: Voltage dividers and loading
skills.description: Calculate the output of a resistive voltage divider and account for how a connected load changes it.

skills.name: Kirchhoff current law
skills.description: Apply charge conservation so the currents entering a circuit node equal the currents leaving it.

skills.name: Kirchhoff voltage law
skills.description: Sum voltage rises and drops around a closed loop to zero using a consistent sign convention.

skills.name: Nodal analysis
skills.description: Solve for node voltages relative to a chosen reference by writing Kirchhoff current law at each node.

skills.name: Mesh-current analysis
skills.description: Assign circulating mesh currents in a planar circuit and solve the resulting KVL equations simultaneously.

skills.name: Thevenin and Norton equivalents
skills.description: Replace a linear two-terminal network with an equivalent voltage source and series resistance, or current source and parallel resistance.

skills.name: Circuit superposition
skills.description: Find a response in a linear circuit by adding the contributions of each independent source acting alone.

skills.name: Capacitance and stored energy
skills.description: Relate a capacitor's stored charge and energy to its voltage and distinguish capacitance from voltage rating.

skills.name: Inductance and stored energy
skills.description: Relate an inductor's voltage to its rate of current change and its magnetic energy storage to current.

skills.name: RC transient response

skills.name: Component tolerances and worst cases

skills.name: Phasors and impedance

skills.name: AC network analysis
skills.description: Apply Kirchhoff's laws and nodal or mesh methods with complex impedances at a specified frequency.

skills.name: Real, reactive, and apparent power

skills.name: RLC resonance and quality factor

skills.name: Passive low-pass filters

skills.name: Passive high-pass filters

skills.name: Band-pass and notch responses

skills.description: Describe electron and hole carriers, how doping creates n-type and p-type material, and how a pn junction forms.

skills.name: Diode behavior and limits
skills.description: Interpret forward conduction, reverse blocking, and the nonlinear current-voltage characteristic and ratings of a diode.

skills.name: Rectification and smoothing
skills.description: Convert alternating voltage into one polarity with diodes and estimate the ripple left after capacitor smoothing.

skills.name: Inverting and noninverting amplifiers

skills.name: Buffers and impedance loading
skills.description: Use a buffer stage so a source is not disturbed by the current its load draws.

skills.name: Differential and instrumentation amplification
skills.description: Amplify the small difference between two input voltages while rejecting the larger voltage common to both.

skills.name: Comparators and hysteresis

skills.name: Saturation and clipping models

skills.name: Active filters

skills.description: Distinguish guaranteed input voltage thresholds from output voltage guarantees and compute noise margins between logic devices.

skills.description: Provide a defined path for the energy stored in an inductive load when a switch turns off.

skills.description: Distinguish charge capacity, stored energy, terminal voltage, and load-dependent voltage sag in a battery.

skills.name: Grounding and interference paths
skills.description: Trace shared return impedance and distinguish differential-mode from common-mode interference.

skills.description: Choose time, voltage, and trigger settings on an oscilloscope and account for probe loading and ground connections.

skills.name: Sensor calibration curves

skills.name: Resistive bridge sensing

skills.name: Incremental and absolute encoders

skills.name: Hall-effect sensing

skills.name: Inertial measurement units
skills.description: Distinguish accelerometer and gyroscope outputs, their biases, and the reference frames they are expressed in.

skills.name: Local serial interfaces

skills.name: PCB connectivity and physical layout
skills.description: Translate logical connections into physical copper while accounting for current loops, spacing, and heat.

skills.name: Dielectric properties

skills.description: Recognize and estimate the local rise in stress near holes, notches, and sharp corners.

skills.name: Cracks and fracture toughness
skills.description: Explain why a crack can cause failure far below a material's nominal strength and how fracture toughness quantifies crack resistance.

skills.name: Fatigue under repeated loading
skills.description: Explain how repeated load cycles can grow cracks and cause failure at stresses well below a material's static strength.

skills.name: Viscoelastic response
skills.description: Describe materials whose response depends on loading time and rate, combining spring-like and fluid-like behaviour.

skills.name: Creep and stress relaxation
skills.description: Distinguish creep, where strain grows under constant stress, from stress relaxation, where stress falls under constant strain.

skills.name: Fiber composites and load sharing
skills.description: Estimate how fibers and matrix share load in a composite and why its stiffness and strength depend strongly on direction.

skills.name: Laminates and anisotropic stiffness
skills.description: Describe how stacked plies at different angles set a laminate's stiffness and create coupling between stretching, bending, and twisting.

skills.name: Finite-element model concepts
skills.description: Understand how finite-element analysis approximates a structure with elements, material laws, loads, and boundary conditions solved as a matrix system.

skills.name: Mesh convergence and model verification
skills.description: Check a finite-element result by refining the mesh, balancing reactions against loads, and comparing with hand calculations before trusting it.

skills.name: Engineering metals and alloy families
skills.description: Compare metallic material families through density, stiffness, strength, corrosion behavior, and ease of processing.

skills.name: Steels and their processing condition
skills.description: Distinguish major steel families and recognize that heat treatment and processing condition change properties.

skills.name: Aluminum alloys
skills.description: Weigh aluminum alloys' low density and easy machining against their lower stiffness, temperature limits, joining issues, and corrosion.

skills.name: Titanium and specialty alloys
skills.description: Compare titanium and other specialty alloys by specific performance, temperature and corrosion capability, and fabrication cost.

skills.name: Thermoplastics and thermosets
skills.description: Distinguish polymers that soften and can be remelted from those that cure into a permanently crosslinked network.

skills.name: Elastomers and large elastic strain
skills.description: Describe rubbery polymer networks that stretch far and recover, and understand why their stiffness is not constant.

skills.name: Ceramics and glasses
skills.description: Compare hard, often brittle ceramics and glasses and their uses as wear surfaces, insulators, and high-temperature materials.

skills.name: Carbon-fiber reinforced structures
skills.description: Relate fiber orientation, resin, joints, and damage sensitivity to how carbon-fiber composite structures carry load.

skills.name: Diffusion in materials
skills.description: Describe how atoms move through solids from high to low concentration and how temperature and time control how far they move.

skills.name: Strengthening mechanisms
skills.description: Explain how obstacles to dislocation motion raise a metal's yield strength, and what that costs in ductility.

skills.name: Heat treatment and microstructure
skills.description: Relate a controlled heating and cooling history to phase changes, microstructure, and the resulting mechanical properties.

skills.name: Casting and solidification
skills.description: Connect mold design and solidification behavior with shrinkage, internal defects, and the features a cast part can have.

skills.name: Metal forming
skills.description: Shape metal by controlled plastic deformation while accounting for springback, work hardening, and changes to material properties.

skills.name: Machining fundamentals
skills.description: Relate cutting forces, tool access, workholding, and material behavior to the geometry and accuracy a machined part can achieve.

skills.name: Additive manufacturing and build direction
skills.description: Distinguish 3D printing process families and recognize how build orientation, porosity, supports, and postprocessing affect parts.

skills.name: Welding and heat-affected zones
skills.description: Recognize local melting, residual stress, distortion, and weakened or embrittled heat-affected zones near welds.

skills.name: Adhesive joints
skills.description: Relate surface preparation, bond geometry, and loading mode to the strength and durability of bonded joints.

skills.name: Bolted joints and preload
skills.description: Distinguish bolt preload from service load and use joint stiffness to see how added load is shared, and when joints slip or separate.

skills.name: Fits, tolerances, and datum references
skills.description: Specify allowed size and geometric variation and reference it to datum features that reflect how parts function and assemble.

skills.name: Tolerance stack analysis
skills.description: Combine dimensional variations along a chain of parts using a clearly chosen worst-case or statistical model.

skills.name: Surface finish and contact behavior
skills.description: Distinguish overall geometric form from waviness and fine surface texture, and understand how each affects contact.

skills.name: Wear and lubrication
skills.description: Distinguish common wear mechanisms and the role of lubrication and contamination in sliding and rolling contacts.

skills.name: Corrosion and galvanic couples
skills.description: Explain corrosion as an electrochemical process and predict when electrically connected dissimilar metals will corrode.

skills.name: Protective coatings and surface treatments
skills.description: Match a coating or surface treatment to its purpose and recognize its limits in adhesion, wear, thickness, and coverage.

skills.name: Thermal expansion and mismatch
skills.description: Relate temperature change to dimensional change and predict the effects of joining materials that expand differently.

skills.name: Thermal conductivity and conduction
skills.description: Relate conductive heat flow to the temperature difference, path geometry, and a material's thermal conductivity.

skills.name: Thermal resistance networks
skills.description: Model steady heat paths as thermal resistances in series and parallel to estimate temperature rise from dissipated power.

skills.name: Convection and radiation concepts
skills.description: Distinguish heat carried away by a moving fluid from heat emitted as thermal radiation, and estimate each.

skills.name: Material selection under constraints
skills.description: Screen and rank candidate materials against stiffness, mass, environment, temperature, cost, and manufacturing requirements.

skills.name: Design margins and uncertain loads
skills.description: Compare estimated capacity with expected demand and apply an explicitly chosen margin for uncertainty in loads and materials.

skills.name: Kinematic singularities
skills.description: Identify arm configurations where the Jacobian loses rank, so some tool motions become impossible or demand huge joint speeds.

skills.name: Adding Fractions and Whole Numbers Using Models
skills.description: Use fraction strips, area pictures, or number lines to show adding a whole number and a fraction.

skills.name: Adding Fractions and Whole Numbers
skills.description: Add a whole number and a fraction or mixed number, writing the result as a mixed number or improper fraction.

skills.name: Subtracting Fractions and Whole Numbers Using Models
skills.description: Use bar models or number lines to show taking a fraction away from a whole number.

skills.name: Subtracting Fractions and Whole Numbers
skills.description: Subtract a fraction from a whole number, or a whole number from a mixed number, regrouping a whole when needed.

skills.name: Least Common Multiples
skills.description: Find the smallest positive number that two or more whole numbers all divide into evenly.

skills.name: Least Common Denominators
skills.description: Find the smallest shared denominator of two or more fractions by using the least common multiple of their denominators.

skills.name: Comparing Fraction Models Using Common Denominators
skills.description: Compare two fractions by redrawing their models with a common denominator so equal-sized pieces can be counted.

skills.name: Comparing Fractions Using Common Denominators
skills.description: Decide which of two fractions is larger by rewriting both over a common denominator and comparing numerators.

skills.name: Adding Fractions With Unlike Denominators Using Models
skills.description: Use fraction bars, area models, or number lines to add fractions with unlike denominators.

skills.name: Subtracting Fractions With Unlike Denominators Using Models
skills.description: Use fraction bars, area models, or number lines to subtract fractions with unlike denominators.

skills.name: Adding Fractions With Unlike Denominators
skills.description: Add fractions with different denominators by rewriting them over a common denominator, then adding numerators.

skills.name: Subtracting Fractions With Unlike Denominators
skills.description: Subtract fractions with different denominators by converting to a common denominator and subtracting numerators.

skills.name: Adding Mixed Numbers With Unlike Denominators
skills.description: Add mixed numbers whose fraction parts have different denominators, regrouping when the fraction sum exceeds one.

skills.name: Subtracting Mixed Numbers With Unlike Denominators
skills.description: Subtract mixed numbers with unlike denominators, borrowing from the whole number when the fraction part is too small.

skills.name: Subtracting Mixed Numbers With Unlike Denominators Using Improper Fractions
skills.description: Subtract mixed numbers with unlike denominators by converting them to improper fractions first.

skills.name: Multiplying Unit Fractions by Whole Numbers Using Models
skills.description: Use models to show a whole number times a unit fraction, such as 5 × 1/4, as repeated single pieces.

skills.name: Multiplying Fractions by Whole Numbers Using Models
skills.description: Use bar models or number lines to show a whole number times a fraction as repeated copies of that fraction.

skills.name: Multiplying Fractions by Whole Numbers
skills.description: Multiply a fraction by a whole number by multiplying the numerator, keeping the denominator, then simplifying.

skills.name: Multiplying Fractions by Whole Numbers: Word Problems
skills.description: Solve real-world problems that multiply a fraction by a whole number, such as repeated recipe amounts.

skills.name: Strategies to Simplify Whole Number and Fraction Multiplication
skills.description: Use shortcuts like cancelling common factors or dividing first to multiply whole numbers by fractions efficiently.

skills.name: Multiplying Mixed Numbers by Whole Numbers
skills.description: Multiply a mixed number by a whole number by distributing over its parts or converting to an improper fraction.

skills.name: Multiplying Fractions by Unit Fractions Using Models
skills.description: Use area models to show multiplying a fraction by a unit fraction as taking one equal share of it.

skills.name: Multiplying Fractions Using Models
skills.description: Use area models to show the product of two fractions as the overlap of two shaded regions.

skills.name: Multiplying Fractions
skills.description: Multiply fractions by multiplying numerators together and denominators together, simplifying common factors.

skills.name: Multiplying Fractions: Word Problems
skills.description: Solve real-world problems that require finding a fraction of a fractional amount.

skills.name: Multiplying Fractions by Swapping Denominators
skills.description: Trade the denominators of two fractions being multiplied to create easier fractions to simplify.

skills.name: Multiplying Mixed Numbers by Fractions
skills.description: Multiply a mixed number by a fraction, converting to an improper fraction or using the distributive property.

skills.name: Multiplying Mixed Numbers
skills.description: Multiply two mixed numbers by converting them to improper fractions, multiplying, and simplifying.

skills.name: Multiplying Mixed Numbers: Word Problems
skills.description: Solve measurement and rate problems that require multiplying mixed numbers.

skills.name: Dividing Whole Numbers by Unit Fractions Using Models
skills.description: Use bar models, area pictures, or number lines to show a whole number divided by a unit fraction.

skills.name: Dividing Whole Numbers by Unit Fractions
skills.description: Divide a whole number by a unit fraction such as 1/4 by multiplying by its denominator.

skills.name: Dividing Unit Fractions by Whole Numbers Using Models
skills.description: Use models to show a unit fraction shared among a whole number of groups, such as 1/2 ÷ 3 = 1/6.

skills.name: Dividing Unit Fractions by Whole Numbers
skills.description: Divide a unit fraction such as 1/3 by a whole number, producing a smaller unit fraction.

skills.name: Reciprocals
skills.description: Find the reciprocal of a number, the value that multiplies with it to give 1, by flipping the fraction.

skills.name: Dividing Whole Numbers by Fractions Using Models: Whole Number Results
skills.description: Use bar models or number lines to divide a whole number by a fraction when the groups fit exactly.

skills.name: Dividing Whole Numbers by Fractions Using Models: Fractional Results
skills.description: Use drawings or number lines to divide a whole number by a fraction when the answer includes a leftover part.

skills.name: Dividing Whole Numbers by Fractions
skills.description: Divide a whole number by any fraction by multiplying it by the reciprocal of that fraction.

skills.name: Dividing Fractions by Whole Numbers Using Models
skills.description: Use bar or area models to show dividing a fraction by a whole number as sharing it equally.

skills.name: Dividing Fractions by Whole Numbers
skills.description: Divide a fraction by a whole number by multiplying by the whole number's reciprocal.

skills.name: Dividing Fractions Using Models
skills.description: Use models to show dividing one fraction by another as asking how many copies of the divisor fit.

skills.name: Dividing Fractions
skills.description: Divide one fraction by another by multiplying the first fraction by the reciprocal of the second.

skills.name: Introduction to Ratios
skills.description: Use a ratio to compare two quantities, written as a : b, a to b, or a/b, with the order carrying meaning.

skills.name: Equivalent Ratios
skills.description: Create and recognize ratios that describe the same comparison by scaling both parts by the same factor.

skills.name: Writing Ratios Using Fractions
skills.description: Write a ratio as a fraction a/b, simplify it, and interpret correctly what the fraction form does and does not mean.

skills.name: Reasoning With Equivalent Ratios
skills.description: Use equivalent ratios to work out missing quantities and to judge whether two situations are in the same ratio.

skills.name: Further Reasoning With Equivalent Ratios
skills.description: Solve harder equivalent-ratio problems, including non-whole scale factors, shares of a total, and comparing two ratios.

skills.name: Ratio Tables
skills.description: Organise equivalent ratios in a table and use scaling, adding columns, or unit values to find missing entries.

skills.name: Graphing Ratios
skills.description: Plot pairs of equivalent ratios as points on a coordinate grid and see that they lie on a straight line through the origin.

skills.name: Unit Rates
skills.description: Find a rate per single unit, such as price per item or kilometres per litre, by dividing one quantity by the other.

skills.name: Solving Problems Using Unit Rates
skills.description: Use a unit rate to scale up or down in multi-step problems such as pricing, recipes, work rates, and best-buy comparisons.

skills.name: Speed as a Unit Rate
skills.description: Express speed as distance travelled per one unit of time, and use it to compare journeys or find distance and time.

skills.name: Understanding Proportional Relationships Using Tables
skills.description: Use a table of paired values to decide whether two quantities are proportional and find the constant of proportionality.

skills.name: Understanding Proportional Relationships Using Graphs
skills.description: Identify a proportional relationship from its graph as a straight line through the origin and read the constant of proportionality from it.

skills.name: Understanding Proportional Relationships From Descriptions
skills.description: Decide from a written description whether two quantities are proportional, and if so identify the constant of proportionality.

skills.name: Modeling with Direct Variation
skills.description: Build and use equations of the form y = kx to describe situations where one quantity is a constant multiple of another.

skills.name: Inverse Variation
skills.description: Recognise quantities that vary inversely, where their product stays constant and one halves as the other doubles: y = k/x.

skills.name: Modeling With Inverse Variation
skills.description: Write and apply y = k/x models for situations such as shared work, fixed-distance travel, or dividing a fixed amount.

skills.name: Units of Length
skills.description: Know common metric and imperial length units, estimate lengths sensibly, and pick an appropriate unit for a measurement.

skills.name: Units of Mass
skills.description: Understand mass as the amount of matter in an object and use units such as grams, kilograms, ounces, and pounds.

skills.name: Units of Time
skills.description: Understand the units used to measure time, from seconds to years, and use them with clock times and elapsed time.

skills.name: Units of Volume
skills.description: Measure the space an object occupies or a container holds using cubic units and capacity units such as litres and millilitres.

skills.name: Understanding Volume Using Unit Cubes
skills.description: Measure volume by counting how many unit cubes fill a solid, leading to the formula length × width × height.

skills.name: Units of Area and Volume
skills.description: Recognise square units for area and cubic units for volume, and understand why their conversion factors are squared or cubed.

skills.name: Unit Conversions Using Base Units of Mass
skills.description: Convert metric masses such as milligrams, grams, kilograms, and tonnes by relating each prefix to the gram.

skills.name: Two-Step Unit Conversions
skills.description: Convert between units that have no direct factor by chaining two conversion factors so the intermediate unit cancels.

skills.name: Unit Conversions Using Base Units of Length
skills.description: Convert metric lengths between prefixes such as mm, cm, m, and km by relating each one to the metre.

skills.name: Unit Conversions Using Units of Time
skills.description: Convert between seconds, minutes, hours, days, and weeks using the non-decimal factors 60, 24, and 7.

skills.name: Converting Units of Area to Smaller Units
skills.description: Change an area measurement to a smaller unit, such as m² to cm², by multiplying by the square of the length factor.

skills.name: Converting Units of Area to Larger Units
skills.description: Change an area measurement to a larger unit, such as cm² to m², by dividing by the square of the length factor.

skills.name: Converting Between Mixed Units
skills.description: Convert measurements written in two units, such as 5 ft 7 in or 2 h 45 min, to and from a single unit.

skills.name: Determining Units in Formulas
skills.description: Work out the units of a quantity by substituting units into a formula and simplifying them like algebra.

skills.name: Selecting Units for Rates of Change
skills.description: Choose and interpret appropriate units for a rate of change, such as dollars per hour or litres per minute, from its context.

skills.name: Degrees of Accuracy
skills.description: Round values to a stated degree of accuracy and find the upper and lower bounds that a rounded measurement implies.

skills.name: Understanding Percentages Using Models
skills.description: Picture percentages with hundred grids, bar models, and number lines to see a percent as a number of parts out of 100.

skills.name: Converting Between Percentages and Fractions
skills.description: Rewrite a percentage as a simplified fraction over 100, and turn a fraction into a percentage.

skills.name: Converting Between Percentages and Decimals
skills.description: Convert a percentage to a decimal by dividing by 100, and a decimal to a percentage by multiplying by 100.

skills.name: Comparing Fractions, Percents, and Decimals
skills.description: Order and compare values given as fractions, percents, and decimals by converting them to one common form.

skills.name: Finding Part of a Number Given a Whole and a Percentage
skills.description: Calculate a percentage of a given amount, such as 15% of 80, by converting the percent to a decimal or fraction.

skills.name: Finding Part of a Number Given a Whole and a Percentage: Word Problems
skills.description: Apply percent-of-a-number calculations to everyday situations such as discounts, tips, taxes, and survey results.

skills.name: Finding a Percentage Given Two Numbers
skills.description: Work out what percentage one number is of another by dividing the part by the whole and multiplying by 100.

skills.name: Finding a Percentage Given Two Numbers: Word Problems
skills.description: Work out what percent one quantity in a real situation is of another by identifying the part and the whole.

skills.name: Finding a Total Given a Part and a Percentage
skills.description: Work backwards from a known part and its percentage to find the whole amount it came from.

skills.name: Applying Percentages in Succession
skills.description: Apply one percentage change after another by multiplying the corresponding multipliers rather than adding percentages.

skills.name: Applying Percentage Increases
skills.description: Increase an amount by a given percentage using the multiplier 1 + r/100, as in price rises, sales tax, or growth.

skills.name: Applying Percentage Decreases
skills.description: Reduce an amount by a given percentage, either by subtracting the percentage part or by multiplying by a single decimal multiplier.

skills.name: Calculating Percentage Change
skills.description: Measure how much a quantity has grown or shrunk relative to its original value, expressed as a percentage.

skills.name: Finding Original Values From Percentage Increases
skills.description: Recover the value before a percentage increase by dividing the new amount by the increase multiplier.

skills.name: Finding Original Values From Percentage Decreases
skills.description: Work backwards from a reduced value to the amount before a percentage decrease by dividing by the decrease multiplier.

skills.name: Subtracting a Positive Number From a Smaller Positive Number
skills.description: Subtract a larger positive number from a smaller one, such as 3 − 8, and get a negative result.

skills.name: Subtracting a Positive Number From a Negative Number
skills.description: Subtract a positive number from a negative number by moving further left on the number line, making the result more negative.
