skills.name: Subtracting a Positive Fraction From a Smaller Fraction
skills.description: Subtract a larger fraction from a smaller one using a common denominator, giving a negative result.

skills.name: Subtracting a Positive Decimal From a Smaller Decimal
skills.description: Subtract a larger decimal from a smaller one by finding the difference of their sizes and giving the result a negative sign.

skills.name: Adding a Positive Number to a Negative Number
skills.description: Add a positive number to a negative one by moving right on the number line or subtracting sizes and keeping the larger's sign.

skills.name: Adding a Negative Number
skills.description: Add a negative number by moving left on the number line, which is equivalent to subtracting its positive counterpart.

skills.name: Subtracting a Negative Number
skills.description: Subtract a negative number by adding its opposite, so a − (−b) becomes a + b.

skills.name: Additive Inverses of Numbers
skills.description: Identify a number's opposite, the value that adds to it to give zero, including opposites of fractions and decimals.

skills.name: Interpreting Additive Opposites and Addition Using Absolute Value
skills.description: Interpret sums on the number line as moves of |q| units from p, and see opposites as equal distances that sum to zero.

skills.name: Solving Problems Using Addition and Subtraction of Rational Numbers
skills.description: Solve word problems about gains, losses, and changes by adding and subtracting signed fractions and decimals.

skills.name: Absolute Value
skills.description: Find a number's distance from zero on the number line, written |x|, which is never negative.

skills.name: Multiplying Positive Numbers With Negative Numbers
skills.description: Multiply a positive number by a negative number, giving a negative product whose size is the product of the sizes.

skills.name: Multiplying Negative Numbers
skills.description: Multiply two or more negative numbers, using the fact that an even number of negative factors gives a positive product.

skills.name: Dividing With Negative Numbers
skills.description: Divide integers with signs, giving a positive quotient for like signs and a negative quotient for unlike signs.

skills.name: Equivalent Fractions With Negative Numbers
skills.description: Recognise that −a/b, (−a)/b and a/(−b) are equal, and that (−a)/(−b) equals a/b.

skills.name: Dividing With Negative Decimals and Fractions
skills.description: Divide signed decimals and fractions by fixing the sign first, then dividing sizes or multiplying by the reciprocal.

skills.name: Reciprocals of Rational Numbers
skills.description: Find the reciprocal of a fraction, integer, or decimal so that their product is 1, keeping the original sign.

skills.name: Multiplying and Dividing With Zero
skills.description: Apply the rules that any number times zero is zero, zero divided by a nonzero number is zero, and division by zero is undefined.

skills.name: Fractions of Fractions
skills.description: Find a fraction of a fraction by multiplying numerators and denominators, reading the word 'of' as multiplication.

skills.name: Solving Problems Using Multiplication and Division of Rational Numbers
skills.description: Solve problems involving rates, repeated changes, and sharing by multiplying and dividing signed fractions and decimals.

skills.name: Solving Problems Using the Four Operations on Rational Numbers
skills.description: Solve multi-step problems that combine all four operations on signed fractions and decimals, following the order of operations.

skills.name: Divisibility of Integers by 2, 5, 10, 4, and 8
skills.description: Test whether an integer is divisible by 2, 5, 10, 4, or 8 by examining only its last one, two, or three digits.

skills.name: Divisibility of Integers by 3, 9, 6, and 7
skills.description: Test divisibility by 3 and 9 using digit sums, by 6 using the tests for 2 and 3, and by 7.

skills.name: Prime and Composite Numbers
skills.description: Classify whole numbers greater than 1 as prime or composite and test primality by trial division up to the square root.

skills.name: Prime Factors
skills.description: Break a whole number into the prime numbers that multiply to give it, using a factor tree or repeated division.

skills.name: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
skills.description: Every whole number greater than 1 is a product of primes in exactly one way, apart from the order of the factors.

skills.name: Finding Greatest Common Factors Using Prime Factorization
skills.description: Find the greatest common factor of two or more numbers by multiplying the primes they share, each at its lowest power.

skills.name: Finding Lowest Common Multiples Using Prime Factorization
skills.description: Find the lowest common multiple by multiplying every prime that appears in any of the numbers, each at its highest power.

skills.name: Natural Numbers, Integers, and Rational Numbers
skills.description: Distinguish natural numbers, integers, and rational numbers as nested sets and classify numbers by their definitions.

skills.name: Rational Numbers as Finite or Repeating Decimals
skills.description: Convert fractions to decimals and recognise that every rational number gives a terminating or repeating decimal.

skills.name: Writing Repeating Decimals as Fractions
skills.description: Convert a repeating decimal such as 0.272727... into an exact fraction by multiplying and subtracting to cancel the repeating tail.

skills.name: Introduction to Exponents
skills.description: Understanding exponent notation, where a base raised to a whole-number power means repeated multiplication of that base.

skills.name: Evaluating Exponents
skills.description: Computing the value of a power such as 3⁴ by carrying out the repeated multiplication step by step.

skills.name: Evaluating Larger Exponents
skills.description: Evaluating powers with bigger exponents efficiently, such as 2^10 or 3^6, by building on smaller known powers.

skills.name: Evaluating Exponents With Fractional Bases
skills.description: Evaluating powers of fractions by raising the numerator and the denominator to the exponent separately.

skills.name: Evaluating Exponents With Decimal Bases
skills.description: Raising decimal numbers to whole-number powers and placing the decimal point correctly in the result.

skills.name: Evaluating Whole Number Expressions Containing Exponents
skills.description: Evaluating whole-number expressions that include powers, applying exponents before multiplication, division, addition, and subtraction.

skills.name: Squaring Rational Numbers
skills.description: Raising fractions, decimals, and negative rational numbers to the second power, giving a result that is never negative.

skills.name: Cubing Rational Numbers
skills.description: Raising fractions, decimals, and signed numbers to the third power by multiplying the number by itself three times.

skills.name: Exponents With Rational Bases
skills.description: Evaluating powers of fractions and signed rational numbers, paying attention to parentheses and the sign of the result.

skills.name: The Zeroth Power
skills.description: Knowing that any nonzero number raised to the power zero equals 1, and why that definition is consistent.

skills.name: Powers of Negative One
skills.description: Evaluating (−1)^n quickly: the result is 1 when n is even and −1 when n is odd.

skills.name: Negative Exponents
skills.description: Interpreting a negative exponent as a reciprocal, so a^−n = 1/a^n for any nonzero base a.

skills.name: The Product Rule for Exponents
skills.description: Multiply powers with the same base by keeping the base and adding the exponents: a^m·a^n = a^(m+n).

skills.name: The Quotient Rule for Exponents
skills.description: Divide powers with the same nonzero base by keeping the base and subtracting exponents: a^m/a^n = a^(m−n).

skills.name: The Power Rule for Exponents
skills.description: Simplify a power raised to another power by multiplying the exponents: (a^m)^n = a^(mn).

skills.name: The Power of Product Rule for Exponents
skills.description: Raise a product to a power by giving every factor that power, as in (ab)^n = a^n·b^n.

skills.name: The Power of Quotient Rule for Exponents
skills.description: Raise a fraction to a power by raising its numerator and denominator separately: (a/b)^n = a^n/b^n.

skills.name: Combining the Rules of Exponents
skills.description: Simplify expressions that need several exponent rules at once, such as product, quotient, and power rules together.

skills.name: Evaluating Rational Number Expressions Without Exponents
skills.description: Evaluate expressions combining fractions, decimals, and signed numbers using the order of operations, with no powers involved.

skills.name: Evaluating Expressions With Positive Integer Exponents
skills.description: Evaluate numerical expressions containing positive whole-number exponents, following the order of operations.

skills.name: Evaluating Expressions With Integer Exponents
skills.description: Evaluate numerical expressions whose exponents may be positive, zero, or negative integers.

skills.name: The Square Root of a Perfect Square
skills.description: Find the square root of numbers like 49 or 144 that are squares of whole numbers.

skills.name: Squaring a Square Root
skills.description: Using (√a)² = a for a ≥ 0 to remove a square root, and distinguishing it from √(a²) = |a|.

skills.name: The Cube Root of a Perfect Cube
skills.description: Finding the exact cube root of a perfect cube, including negatives, fractions, and decimals.

skills.name: Surds
skills.description: Recognising surds, roots that cannot be simplified to a rational number, and writing them in simplest exact form.

skills.name: Simplifying Expressions With Surds
skills.description: Multiplying, dividing, and expanding brackets containing surds, then writing the result in simplest form.

skills.name: Evaluating Numerical Expressions Containing Radicals
skills.description: Evaluating numerical expressions that mix square or cube roots with other operations, following the order of operations.

skills.name: Adding and Subtracting Radicals
skills.description: Combining radical terms by adding or subtracting coefficients of like radicals, after simplifying each radical first.

skills.name: Rationalizing Denominators
skills.description: Rewriting a fraction so that no radical remains in the denominator, by multiplying by a suitable form of 1.

skills.name: Radicals as Fractional Exponents
skills.description: Rewrite roots as powers with fractional exponents, such as √x = x^(1/2), and convert back.

skills.name: The Product Rule for Radicals
skills.description: Use √(ab) = √a·√b to split roots of products apart or combine products of roots.

skills.name: The Quotient Rule for Radicals
skills.description: Use √(a/b) = √a/√b to split the root of a fraction or combine a quotient of roots.

skills.name: Introduction to Algebraic Expressions
skills.description: Understand what algebraic expressions are: combinations of variables, numbers, and operations that stand for a quantity.

skills.name: Constructing Algebraic Expressions
skills.description: Translate a verbal description of a quantity into an algebraic expression using variables, numbers, and operations.

skills.name: Evaluating Linear Expressions
skills.description: Find the numerical value of a linear expression by substituting a given value for the variable.

skills.name: Evaluating Rational Expressions
skills.description: Substitute values into an expression that is a fraction of polynomials, and recognise values that make it undefined.

skills.name: Identifying Terms in Linear Expressions
skills.description: Break a linear expression into its separate terms, which are the parts joined by addition or subtraction.

skills.name: Identifying Coefficients and Constants
skills.description: Pick out the numerical coefficient of each variable term and the constant term in an algebraic expression.

skills.name: The Greatest Common Factor of Two Linear Expressions
skills.description: Find the largest factor, numerical or algebraic, that divides both of two linear expressions.

skills.name: Identifying Like Terms in Linear Expressions
skills.description: Recognise which terms in an expression are like terms, meaning they have exactly the same variable part.

skills.name: Collecting Like Terms in Linear Expressions
skills.description: Combine like terms in a linear expression by adding their coefficients, producing a shorter equivalent expression.

skills.name: Applying the Distributive Law With Linear Expressions
skills.description: Expand a number or term times a bracketed linear expression by multiplying it into each term inside.

skills.name: The Distributive Law With Three Terms
skills.description: Expand a factor multiplied by a bracket containing three terms, multiplying the factor into each one.

skills.name: Distributing the Negative Sign in a Linear Expression
skills.description: Expand brackets preceded by a minus sign or negative factor, changing the sign of every term inside.

skills.name: Simplifying Linear Expressions Using the Distributive Law
skills.description: Simplify expressions containing brackets fully, by expanding with the distributive law and then collecting like terms.

skills.name: Simplifying Linear Expressions When a Group of Terms Is Subtracted
skills.description: Simplify an expression in which a bracketed group is subtracted, by removing the brackets and then collecting like terms.

skills.name: Simplifying Linear Expressions Containing Fractions
skills.description: Simplify linear expressions whose coefficients or terms are fractions by distributing and combining over common denominators.

skills.name: Factoring Linear Expressions
skills.description: Rewrite a linear expression as a product by taking out the greatest common factor of its terms.

skills.name: Solving Linear Equations by Trial and Error
skills.description: Find the solution of a simple linear equation by guessing values, checking them, and adjusting the guess.

skills.name: Solving One-Step Addition and Subtraction Equations
skills.description: Solve equations like x + a = b or x − a = b by adding or subtracting the same number on both sides.

skills.name: Solving One-Step Multiplication and Division Equations
skills.description: Solve equations like ax = b or x/a = b by dividing or multiplying both sides by the same nonzero number.

skills.name: Solving Two-Step Equations
skills.description: Solve equations such as 3x + 5 = 20 that need two inverse operations, usually undoing addition or subtraction before multiplication or division.

skills.name: Solving Linear Equations With Fractional Coefficients
skills.description: Solve linear equations whose coefficients or constants are fractions, usually by first clearing denominators with the least common denominator.

skills.name: Solving Linear Equations With Decimal Coefficients
skills.description: Solve linear equations with decimal coefficients, often by multiplying through by a power of 10 to clear the decimals.

skills.name: Solving Linear Equations With Variables on Both Sides
skills.description: Solve linear equations with the unknown on both sides by collecting variable terms on one side, and recognize identities and contradictions.

skills.name: Solving Linear Equations by Clearing a Rational Expression
skills.description: Solve a linear equation containing fractions by multiplying every term by the lowest common denominator.

skills.name: Solving Linear Equations Using Cross-Multiplication
skills.description: Solve an equation of the form a/b = c/d by cross-multiplying to get ad = bc, then solving the linear equation.

skills.name: Solving Two-Variable Equations
skills.description: Work with equations in two variables, such as 2x + 3y = 12, by finding solution pairs or isolating one variable in terms of the other.

skills.name: Linear Equations With Infinitely Many Solutions
skills.description: Recognise a linear equation that is an identity, true for every value of the variable, when simplification yields a true statement.

skills.name: Linear Equations With No Solutions
skills.description: Recognise a linear equation with no solution, a contradiction, when simplification leaves a false statement.

skills.name: Solving Linear Equations With Unknown Coefficients
skills.description: Solve a linear equation for x when some coefficients are letters, giving the answer as an expression and noting when division by a letter is allowed.

skills.name: Solving Linear Equations With Unknown Coefficients by Factoring
skills.description: Isolate an unknown that appears in several terms with letter coefficients by collecting those terms and factoring the unknown out.

skills.name: Solving Many-Variable Equations
skills.description: Rearrange an equation or formula containing several variables to express one chosen variable in terms of the others.

skills.name: Interpreting Linear Expressions
skills.description: Explain what each part of a linear expression means in a real-world context, including its rate and starting value.

skills.name: Modeling With Linear Equations
skills.description: Set up and solve a linear equation that describes a word problem, then interpret and check the answer in context.

skills.name: Inequalities
skills.description: Understand inequality symbols and the rules for manipulating inequalities, which have a whole range of values as solutions.

skills.name: Compound Inequalities
skills.description: Understand inequalities made from two conditions joined by AND or OR, and what each connective means for the solution set.

skills.name: Verifying Solutions of Linear Inequalities
skills.description: Check whether a given number satisfies a linear inequality by substituting it and deciding whether the resulting statement is true.

skills.name: Solving One-Step Linear Inequalities
skills.description: Solve inequalities needing a single operation, such as x + 4 > 9 or −3x ≤ 12, remembering to flip the sign for negative multipliers.

skills.name: Solving Two-Step Inequalities
skills.description: Solve inequalities such as −2x + 3 < 11 in two steps, reversing the inequality sign whenever you multiply or divide by a negative number.

skills.name: Representing Solutions to Inequalities on Number Lines
skills.description: Draw the solution set of an inequality on a number line using open or closed endpoints and shading.

skills.name: Further Solving Linear Inequalities
skills.description: Solve multi-step linear inequalities, including those with brackets, variables on both sides, and negative coefficients.

skills.name: Solving Compound Inequalities
skills.description: Carry out the algebra to solve AND and OR compound inequalities, then state the solution as an interval or union.

skills.name: Interval Notation
skills.description: Write sets of real numbers as intervals using brackets for included endpoints and parentheses for excluded ones.

skills.name: Unbounded Intervals
skills.description: Write and read intervals that extend forever in one or both directions, such as [3, ∞) or (−∞, 2), in interval notation.

skills.name: Unions of Intervals
skills.description: Combine intervals using union to describe numbers in at least one of them, matching conditions joined by 'or'.

skills.name: Intersections of Intervals
skills.description: Find the intersection of two intervals: the numbers belonging to both, corresponding to conditions joined by 'and'.

skills.name: Compound OR Inequalities
skills.description: Solve and describe inequalities joined by OR, whose solution includes every value satisfying at least one condition.

skills.name: Compound AND Inequalities
skills.description: Solve and describe inequalities joined by AND, whose solution is the overlap of both conditions.

skills.name: Solving Equations Using the Square Root Method
skills.description: Solve equations of the form x² = k, or (x − h)² = k, by isolating the square and taking both square roots.

skills.name: Solving Equations With Odd Exponents Using the Nth Root Method
skills.description: Solve equations like xⁿ = k with n odd by taking the nth root, which gives exactly one real solution.

skills.name: Solving Equations With Even Exponents Using the Nth Root Method
skills.description: Solve equations like xⁿ = k with n even by taking the nth root and including both positive and negative roots.

skills.name: The Cartesian Coordinate System
skills.description: Locate and plot points as ordered pairs on two perpendicular number lines, and identify the four quadrants.

skills.name: Distances Between Points in the Coordinate Plane
skills.description: Use the distance formula, built on Pythagoras' theorem, to find the length between two coordinate points.

skills.name: Two-Variable Linear Equations and Their Solutions
skills.description: Understand that a linear equation in two variables has infinitely many ordered-pair solutions lying on a line.

skills.name: Graphing Linear Equations
skills.description: Draw the straight-line graph of a linear equation using a table of values, the slope and intercept, or intercepts.

skills.name: Horizontal and Vertical Lines
skills.description: Recognise and graph horizontal lines y = k with slope 0 and vertical lines x = h with undefined slope.

skills.name: Calculating Slopes of Straight Lines
skills.description: Compute the slope of a line from two points as the change in y divided by the change in x.

skills.name: Equations of Lines in Slope-Intercept Form
skills.description: Write a line's equation as y = mx + b from its slope and y-intercept, from two points, or by rearranging.

skills.name: Properties of Lines Given in Slope-Intercept Form
skills.description: Read the slope, y-intercept, x-intercept and direction of a line directly from its y = mx + b equation.

skills.name: Equations of Lines in Point-Slope Form
skills.description: Write the equation of a line from a known point and slope using y − y₁ = m(x − x₁).

skills.name: Equations of Lines in Standard Form
skills.description: Write and convert line equations into standard form Ax + By = C, usually with integer coefficients.

skills.name: Properties of Lines Given in Standard Form
skills.description: Find the slope and intercepts of a line written as Ax + By = C without first redrawing or fully rearranging it.

skills.name: Parallel Lines in the Coordinate Plane
skills.description: Identify parallel lines by equal slopes and write the equation of a line parallel to a given one.

skills.name: Modeling With Linear Equations in Two Variables
skills.description: Turn a word problem with a constant rate and fixed amount into an equation of the form y = mx + c.

skills.name: Analyzing and Interpreting Graphs of Linear Equations
skills.description: Read a line graph in context, interpreting slope as a rate with units and the intercept as a starting value.

skills.name: Further Modeling With Linear Equations in Two Variables
skills.description: Build linear models from data points and compare competing linear models to answer practical questions.

skills.name: Distance-Time Graphs
skills.description: Interpret distance-time graphs, where the gradient gives speed and flat sections show the object at rest.

skills.name: Speed-Time Graphs
skills.description: Interpret speed-time graphs, reading acceleration from the gradient and recognising constant speed as a flat line.

skills.name: Calculating Distance From a Speed-Time Graph
skills.description: Find the distance travelled by calculating the area between a speed-time graph and the time axis.

skills.name: Introduction to Systems of Linear Equations
skills.description: Understand what a system of linear equations is and what it means for an ordered pair to solve it.

skills.name: Solving Systems of Equations by Substitution
skills.description: Solve a system by isolating one variable in one equation and substituting that expression into the other.

skills.name: Introduction to the Elimination Method
skills.description: Solve a two-variable system by adding or subtracting the equations so that one variable cancels out.

skills.name: Solving Systems of Linear Equations Using Elimination: One Transformation
skills.description: Use elimination after multiplying one equation by a constant so that one variable's coefficients match.

skills.name: Solving Systems of Linear Equations Using Elimination: Two Transformations
skills.description: Use elimination by multiplying both equations by different constants to create matching coefficients.

skills.name: Systems of Linear Equations With Fractional Coefficients
skills.description: Solve linear systems with fractional coefficients by multiplying each equation by its least common denominator.

skills.name: Systems of Linear Equations With Decimal Coefficients
skills.description: Solve linear systems with decimal coefficients by first multiplying through by a power of 10 to clear decimals.

skills.name: Solving Systems of Nonlinear Equations Using Graphs
skills.description: Estimate solutions of systems involving curves by graphing both equations and reading their intersection points.

skills.name: Systems of Equations With No Solutions and Infinitely Many Solutions
skills.description: Recognise during solving when a linear system has no solution or infinitely many, and describe the solution set.

skills.name: Consistency and Dependency in Linear Systems
skills.description: Classify a linear system as consistent or inconsistent, and dependent or independent, by its number of solutions.

skills.name: Calculating the Intersection of Two Lines
skills.description: Find where two lines cross by solving their equations simultaneously, and check the point in both.

skills.name: Writing Radical Expressions Using Fractional Exponents
skills.description: Convert between radical notation and rational exponents using ⁿ√(x^m) = x^(m/n).

skills.name: The Square Root of a Perfect Square With Algebraic Expressions
skills.description: Take square roots of perfect-square algebraic expressions by rooting the coefficient and halving each exponent.

skills.name: The Square Root of a Perfect Square With Domain Restrictions
skills.description: Simplify square roots of squared expressions correctly using absolute values, since √(x²) = |x| for every real x.

skills.name: The Cube Root of a Perfect Cube With Algebraic Expressions
skills.description: Take cube roots of perfect-cube algebraic expressions by cube-rooting the coefficient and dividing each exponent by 3.

skills.name: Simplifying Square Root Expressions Using the Product Rule
skills.description: Simplify square roots by factoring out the largest perfect square, using √(ab) = √a · √b.

skills.name: Simplifying Square Root Expressions Using the Quotient Rule
skills.description: Simplify square roots of fractions or quotients using √(a/b) = √a / √b for a ≥ 0 and b > 0.

skills.name: Combining Radical Expressions Using the Product Rule
skills.description: Multiply radicals with the same index by multiplying their radicands, √a · √b = √(ab), then simplify the result.

skills.name: Evaluating Algebraic Radical Expressions
skills.description: Substitute given values into expressions containing radicals and evaluate them, working out each radicand first.

skills.name: Adding and Subtracting Radical Expressions
skills.description: Combine radical terms by adding or subtracting coefficients of like radicals, simplifying each radical first.

skills.name: Equivalent Expressions With Fractions
skills.description: Rewrite a fraction or rational expression in an equivalent form by multiplying or dividing its numerator and denominator by the same nonzero factor.

skills.name: Simplifying Rational Expressions
skills.description: Reduce a rational expression to lowest terms by cancelling common factors and stating which values are excluded.

skills.name: Simplifying Rational Expressions by Factoring
skills.description: Simplify rational expressions with polynomial numerators and denominators by factoring both fully and cancelling common factors.

skills.name: Splitting Rational Expressions Into Separate Terms
skills.description: Break a fraction with a multi-term numerator into a sum of simpler fractions over the same denominator.

skills.name: Solving Rational Equations Containing One Fractional Term
skills.description: Solve an equation with a single fraction by multiplying both sides by its denominator to clear it.

skills.name: Solving Rational Equations Using Cross-Multiplication
skills.description: Solve an equation of the form a/b = c/d by cross-multiplying to get ad = bc.

skills.name: Solving Rational Equations Containing Binomials Using Cross-Multiplication
skills.description: Solve equations where one binomial fraction equals another by cross-multiplying and checking the excluded values.

skills.name: Solving Rational Equations Using the Flip Method
skills.description: Solve rational equations with the unknown in a denominator by taking reciprocals of both sides.

skills.name: Introduction to Functions
skills.description: Understand a function as a rule that assigns exactly one output to each allowed input, and use f(x) notation.

skills.name: Visual Representations of Functions
skills.description: Represent functions with mapping diagrams, tables, and graphs, and judge from each view whether a relation is a function.

skills.name: Graphs of Functions
skills.description: Plot and read the graph of a function as the set of points (x, f(x)) in the coordinate plane.

skills.name: The Domain of a Function
skills.description: Determine the set of input values for which a function is defined, and write it in interval notation.

skills.name: Global Extrema of Functions
skills.description: Find the absolute highest and lowest output values a function reaches across its entire domain.

skills.name: End Behavior of Functions
skills.description: Describe what a function's outputs do as the input grows very large in the positive or negative direction.

skills.name: The Range of a Function
skills.description: Find the set of all output values a function can produce, using its formula or its graph.

skills.name: The Range of a Function: Advanced Cases
skills.description: Find ranges for harder functions, such as rational functions or restricted domains, by solving for the input.

skills.name: The Roots of a Function
skills.description: Find the inputs that make a function equal zero, which are the x-intercepts of its graph.

skills.name: Increasing and Decreasing Functions
skills.description: Identify the intervals of x where a function's outputs rise, fall, or stay constant.

skills.name: Modeling With Linear Functions
skills.description: Build and interpret linear functions that describe real situations with a constant rate of change.

skills.name: Constructing Linear Functions
skills.description: Write the equation of a linear function from two points, a slope and a point, a table, or a graph.

skills.name: Absolute Value Expressions
skills.description: Evaluate and simplify expressions containing absolute value bars, treating each as a nonnegative distance from zero.

skills.name: Rules of Absolute Value
skills.description: Apply the basic absolute value rules: nonnegativity, |−a| = |a|, |ab| = |a||b|, and |a/b| = |a|/|b|.

skills.name: Further Rules of Absolute Value
skills.description: Use deeper absolute value properties, such as the triangle inequality and √(x²) = |x|, to simplify and bound expressions.

skills.name: Absolute Value Equations
skills.description: Solve equations such as |x − 3| = 5 by splitting them into a positive case and a negative case.

skills.name: Further Absolute Value Equations
skills.description: Solve harder absolute value equations, including ones with variables outside the bars or absolute values on both sides.

skills.name: Absolute Value Inequalities
skills.description: Solve inequalities like |x − 2| < 3 or |x| > 4 and write the solutions as intervals.

skills.name: Absolute Value Graphs
skills.description: Graph y = |x| and simple shifts of it, recognizing the V shape, the vertex, and the symmetry.

skills.name: Vertical Reflections of Absolute Value Graphs
skills.description: Reflect absolute value graphs across the x-axis, turning y = |x| into the downward-opening V of y = −|x|.

skills.name: Stretches of Absolute Value Graphs
skills.description: See how y = a|x| becomes narrower or wider than y = |x| as the positive factor a changes.

skills.name: Combining Transformations of Absolute Value Graphs
skills.description: Sketch graphs of the form y = a|x − h| + k by combining shifts, stretches, and reflections of y = |x|.

skills.name: Domain and Range of Absolute Value Functions
skills.description: Find the domain and range of absolute value functions, using the vertex and opening direction to bound outputs.

skills.name: The Product Rule for Exponents With Algebraic Expressions
skills.description: Multiply powers that share the same base by adding their exponents, using aᵐ · aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ on algebraic terms.

skills.name: The Quotient Rule for Exponents With Algebraic Expressions
skills.description: Divide powers with the same nonzero base by subtracting exponents, using aᵐ/aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ on algebraic expressions.

skills.name: The Power Rule for Exponents With Algebraic Expressions
skills.description: Simplify a power raised to another power by multiplying the exponents, using (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ on algebraic expressions.

skills.name: The Power of Product Rule With Algebraic Expressions
skills.description: Raise a product to a power by applying the exponent to every factor, using (ab)ⁿ = aⁿbⁿ on algebraic expressions.

skills.name: The Power of Quotient Rule With Algebraic Expressions
skills.description: Raise a fraction to a power by applying the exponent to both numerator and denominator, using (a/b)ⁿ = aⁿ/bⁿ with b ≠ 0.

skills.name: Combining the Rules of Exponents With Algebraic Expressions
skills.description: Simplify expressions that need several exponent rules at once, applying powers of products and quotients before multiplying and dividing.

skills.name: Solving Exponential Equations
skills.description: Solve equations with the unknown in an exponent by writing both sides as powers of the same base and equating the exponents.

skills.name: Creating Exponential Growth Expressions
skills.description: Write an exponential expression a(1 + r)ᵗ or a doubling formula for a quantity that grows by a fixed percentage each period.

skills.name: Creating Exponential Decay Expressions
skills.description: Write an exponential expression a(1 − r)ᵗ or a(1/2)^(t/h) that describes a quantity shrinking by a fixed percentage or half-life.

skills.name: Exponential Functions
skills.description: Understand functions of the form f(x) = a·bˣ, where the base b is a constant multiplier and the variable is in the exponent.

skills.name: Modeling Exponential Growth With Functions
skills.description: Build a growth function such as f(x) = a·bˣ or a compound-interest formula from a verbal description or from two data points.

skills.name: Interpreting Exponential Growth
skills.description: Explain what the initial value, growth factor and growth rate of an exponential growth model mean in a real situation.

skills.name: Solving Exponential Growth Problems
skills.description: Apply an exponential growth model to predict a future value or find how long it takes to reach a target, such as a doubling time.

skills.name: Modeling Exponential Decay With Functions
skills.description: Build a decay function f(t) = a·bᵗ from a description or data points, choosing the variables, units and a sensible domain.

skills.name: Interpreting Exponential Decay
skills.description: Read the initial value, decay factor and percentage decrease from an exponential decay model or table, and explain them in context.

skills.name: Solving Exponential Decay Problems
skills.description: Use an exponential decay model to find a future amount or the time needed to fall to a given level, such as with half-life.

skills.name: Graphing Exponential Growth Functions
skills.description: Sketch graphs of growth functions y = a·bˣ with b > 1 by plotting key points and drawing the horizontal asymptote.

skills.name: Graphing Exponential Decay Functions
skills.description: Sketch graphs of decay functions y = a·bˣ with 0 < b < 1, showing their falling shape and horizontal asymptote.

skills.name: Introduction to Polynomials
skills.description: Recognise polynomials and name their parts: terms, coefficients, constants, and the leading term.

skills.name: The Degree of a Polynomial
skills.description: Find the degree of a term or polynomial from its highest power, and use degree to name polynomials.

skills.name: Simplifying Polynomials
skills.description: Simplify a polynomial by combining like terms and writing the result in standard descending order.

skills.name: The Distributive Law for Polynomials
skills.description: Use a(b + c) = ab + ac to multiply a monomial or polynomial across a bracket of terms.

skills.name: Adding and Subtracting Polynomials
skills.description: Add or subtract polynomials by combining like terms, taking care to distribute a minus sign across brackets.

skills.name: Monomials, Binomials and Trinomials
skills.description: Classify a polynomial as a monomial, binomial, or trinomial by counting its terms after simplifying.

skills.name: Multiplying Binomials
skills.description: Multiply two binomials by multiplying each term of one by each term of the other, often using FOIL.

skills.name: Multiplying Polynomials
skills.description: Multiply polynomials of any size by distributing every term of one across every term of the other.

skills.name: Squaring Binomials
skills.description: Expand the square of a binomial using the pattern (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b².

skills.name: Expanding Binomials Using Pascal's Triangle
skills.description: Expand powers such as (a + b)ⁿ quickly by reading the coefficients from a row of Pascal's triangle.

skills.name: The Difference of Squares Formula
skills.description: Multiply conjugate binomials quickly using the pattern (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².

skills.name: The Greatest Common Factor of Two Monomials
skills.description: Find the largest monomial dividing two monomials by combining the GCF of their coefficients with the lowest shared variable powers.

skills.name: Factoring Polynomials Using GCFs
skills.description: Factor a polynomial by taking out the greatest common factor shared by all of its terms.

skills.name: Factoring Perfect Square Trinomials
skills.description: Recognise trinomials like x² + 10x + 25 as perfect squares and factor them as (x + 5)².

skills.name: Factoring Perfect Square Trinomials With Leading Coefficients
skills.description: Factor perfect square trinomials whose leading coefficient is not 1, such as 4x² − 12x + 9 = (2x − 3)².

skills.name: Factoring Differences of Squares
skills.description: Factor expressions of the form a² − b² into (a + b)(a − b).

skills.name: Factoring Trinomials
skills.description: Factor trinomials of the form x² + bx + c by finding two numbers that multiply to c and add to b.

skills.name: Factoring Trinomials Using Common Factors
skills.description: Factor trinomials by first removing a common factor, then factoring the simpler trinomial that remains.

skills.name: Factoring Trinomials With Leading Coefficients
skills.description: Factor trinomials ax² + bx + c where a is not 1, using the ac (grouping) method or trial and check.

skills.name: Further Factoring Trinomials With Leading Coefficients
skills.description: Factor harder trinomials with leading coefficients, including negative leading terms and trinomials in two variables.

skills.name: Points, Lines, Rays, and Segments
skills.description: Distinguish the basic objects of geometry—points, lines, rays, and segments—and name them with correct notation.

skills.name: Parallel and Perpendicular Lines
skills.description: Recognize parallel and perpendicular lines, use their symbols, and test for them using slopes.

skills.name: Measures of Segments
skills.description: Find and use the length of a line segment, including on a number line and in segment notation.

skills.name: Congruent Segments
skills.description: Identify segments of equal length and record this with the congruence symbol and tick marks.

skills.name: Midpoints
skills.description: Locate the point that splits a segment into two equal halves by averaging the endpoint coordinates.

skills.name: Collinear Points
skills.description: Recognize and test whether three or more points lie on a single straight line.

skills.name: The Segment Addition Postulate
skills.description: Use the fact that if B lies between A and C, then AB + BC = AC, to find unknown lengths.

skills.name: Angles and Measures of Angles
skills.description: Name angles by their vertex and sides, and measure them in degrees with a protractor.

skills.name: Measuring Angles Using a Protractor
skills.description: Use a protractor correctly to measure or draw an angle in degrees, choosing the right scale.

skills.name: Sums of Angles
skills.description: Add adjacent angles, and use the fixed totals for angles on a straight line and around a point.

skills.name: Right, Straight, Full, and Null Angles
skills.description: Know the special angles of 90, 180, 360 and 0 degrees and use them to classify other angles.

skills.name: Acute, Obtuse, and Reflex Angles
skills.description: Classify angles by size as acute, right, obtuse, straight, or reflex.

skills.name: Congruent Angles
skills.description: Recognize angles with equal measures and use arc marks and congruence facts to find unknown angles.

skills.name: Vertical Angles
skills.description: Use the fact that opposite angles formed by two intersecting lines are equal.

skills.name: Solving Problems With Angles
skills.description: Combine angle facts from a diagram into an equation, solve for the unknown, and check the resulting angles.

skills.name: Complementary Angles
skills.description: Find and use pairs of angles whose measures add up to 90°.

skills.name: Non-Adjacent Complementary Angles
skills.description: Recognise complementary angles that add to 90 degrees even when they are separate and share no side.

skills.name: Supplementary Angles
skills.description: Use the fact that supplementary angles add to 180 degrees to find unknown angles.

skills.name: Corresponding Angles
skills.description: Identify angles in matching positions where a transversal crosses two lines, and use their equality when the lines are parallel.

skills.name: Alternate Angles
skills.description: Use the equality of alternate angles formed when a transversal crosses parallel lines.

skills.name: Consecutive Angles
skills.description: Use the fact that consecutive interior angles between parallel lines add up to 180°.

skills.name: Angle Bisectors
skills.description: Divide an angle into two equal angles with a bisecting ray and use this to find unknown measures.

skills.name: Segment Bisectors and the Perpendicular Bisector Theorem
skills.description: Find midpoints and bisectors of segments, and use the fact that perpendicular bisector points are equidistant from the endpoints.

skills.name: Circles
skills.description: Name the parts of a circle, including centre, radius, diameter, chord, tangent, and arc, and relate them.

skills.name: Arcs, Segments, and Sectors of Circles
skills.description: Calculate arc lengths, sector areas, and segment areas from a circle's radius and central angle.

skills.name: The Circumference of a Circle
skills.description: Find the distance around a circle with C = 2πr or C = πd, and work backwards to the radius or diameter.

skills.name: Areas of Circles
skills.description: Find the area enclosed by a circle using A = πr², working from either the radius or the diameter.

skills.name: Interior Angles of Triangles
skills.description: Use the fact that the three interior angles of any triangle add up to 180° to find missing angles.

skills.name: Exterior Angles of Triangles
skills.description: Use the fact that a triangle's exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior angles not adjacent to it.

skills.name: Classifying Triangles
skills.description: Name triangles by their sides (equilateral, isosceles, scalene) and by their angles (acute, right, obtuse).

skills.name: The Triangle Inequality
skills.description: Decide whether three lengths can form a triangle by checking that each side is shorter than the sum of the other two.

skills.name: The Isosceles Triangle Theorem
skills.description: Use the theorem that angles opposite equal sides of a triangle are equal, and its converse, to find unknown angles or sides.

skills.name: Heights of Triangles
skills.description: Identify and calculate a triangle's height, the perpendicular distance from a vertex to the line of the opposite side.

skills.name: The Pythagorean Theorem
skills.description: Relate the sides of a right triangle by a² + b² = c² to find an unknown length, or test whether an angle is right.

skills.name: Isosceles Right Triangles
skills.description: Use the 1 : 1 : √2 side ratio of a 45-45-90 triangle to find a missing leg or hypotenuse.

skills.name: 30-60-90 Triangles
skills.description: Use the fixed side ratio 1 : √3 : 2 of a 30-60-90 triangle to find missing sides without a calculator.

skills.name: Polygons
skills.description: Recognise, name, and classify closed straight-sided shapes by their number of sides, angles, and convexity.

skills.name: Interior Angles of Polygons
skills.description: Find the interior angle sum of an n-sided polygon with (n − 2) × 180°, and each angle of a regular polygon.

skills.name: Exterior Angles of Polygons
skills.description: Use the fact that the exterior angles of a convex polygon sum to 360° to find angles and numbers of sides.

skills.name: Congruent Polygons
skills.description: Recognize polygons that match exactly in shape and size and use corresponding sides and angles to find unknowns.

skills.name: Regular Polygons
skills.description: Work with polygons whose sides and angles are all equal, finding their interior and exterior angles and symmetries.

skills.name: The Perimeter of a Polygon
skills.description: Find the perimeter of a polygon by adding its side lengths, including finding missing sides first.

skills.name: Classifying Quadrilaterals
skills.description: Identify parallelograms, rectangles, rhombuses, squares, trapezoids, and kites from their defining side and angle properties.

skills.name: Properties of Rectangles and Squares
skills.description: Use the defining properties of rectangles and squares, including their sides, angles, diagonals, and symmetry.

skills.name: Areas of Rectangles and Squares
skills.description: Calculate the area of a rectangle as length times width and of a square as side length squared.

skills.name: Areas of Triangles
skills.description: Compute a triangle's area as half the base times the perpendicular height, A = ½bh.

skills.name: Areas of Trapezoids
skills.description: Find a trapezoid's area by averaging its two parallel sides and multiplying by the perpendicular height.

skills.name: Areas and Perimeters of Composite Shapes
skills.description: Find the area and perimeter of shapes built from rectangles, triangles, and other simple pieces by adding or subtracting parts.

skills.name: Introduction to Quadratic Equations
skills.description: Recognize quadratic equations, write them in standard form ax² + bx + c = 0, and check proposed solutions.

skills.name: Solving Perfect Square Quadratic Equations
skills.description: Solve equations of the form (x − h)² = k by taking square roots of both sides, remembering the ± sign.

skills.name: Perfect Square Quadratic Equations with One or No Solutions
skills.description: Recognize when a squared expression set equal to zero or a negative number gives exactly one or no real solutions.

skills.name: The Zero Product Rule for Solving Quadratic Equations
skills.description: Use the fact that a product equals zero only when a factor is zero to solve factored quadratic equations.

skills.name: Solving Quadratic Equations Using a Difference of Squares
skills.description: Solve quadratics like x² − 49 = 0 by factoring a difference of two squares as (a − b)(a + b).

skills.name: Solving Quadratic Equations with No Constant Term
skills.description: Solve quadratics of the form ax² + bx = 0 by factoring out x, which always gives x = 0 as one root.

skills.name: Solving Quadratic Equations by Factoring
skills.description: Solve quadratics with leading coefficient 1 by factoring x² + bx + c into two binomials and using the zero product rule.

skills.name: Solving Quadratic Equations with Leading Coefficients by Factoring
skills.description: Factor quadratics ax² + bx + c with a ≠ 1, for example by the ac (grouping) method, and solve with the zero product rule.

skills.name: Completing the Square With Odd Linear Terms
skills.description: Complete the square when the x-coefficient is odd, handling the resulting halves and quarters exactly.

skills.name: Completing the Square With Leading Coefficients
skills.description: Complete the square on ax² + bx + c when a ≠ 1 by dividing through by a or factoring a out of the x-terms.

skills.name: Solving Quadratic Equations by Completing the Square
skills.description: Solve x² + bx + c = 0 by rewriting the left side as a perfect square, then taking square roots.

skills.name: Solving Quadratic Equations With Leading Coefficients by Completing the Square
skills.description: Complete the square on ax² + bx + c = 0 when a ≠ 1 by first dividing through by the leading coefficient.

skills.name: The Quadratic Formula
skills.description: Solve any quadratic ax² + bx + c = 0 using x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / (2a).

skills.name: The Discriminant of a Quadratic Equation
skills.description: Use the discriminant b² − 4ac to predict the number and type of solutions of a quadratic equation before solving it.

skills.name: Determining Unknown Parameters in Quadratic Equations With One Real Solution
skills.description: Find the value of an unknown coefficient that gives a quadratic equation exactly one real solution by setting the discriminant to zero.

skills.name: Equating Polynomial Coefficients
skills.description: Find unknown constants by matching the coefficients of like powers of x on both sides of a polynomial identity.

skills.name: Vieta's Formulas
skills.description: Relate the sum and product of a quadratic's roots to its coefficients: r₁ + r₂ = −b/a and r₁r₂ = c/a.

skills.name: Graphing Elementary Quadratic Functions
skills.description: Sketch basic parabolas such as y = x², y = ax² and y = x² + k from a table of values and their key features.

skills.name: Vertical Reflections of Quadratic Functions
skills.description: Reflect a parabola across the x-axis by negating the function, turning y = x² into the downward-opening y = −x².

skills.name: Graphs of General Quadratic Functions
skills.description: Graph y = ax² + bx + c by finding its direction of opening, y-intercept, vertex, axis of symmetry and any x-intercepts.

skills.name: Roots of Quadratic Functions
skills.description: Find the zeros of a quadratic function, the x-values where f(x) = 0 and the graph crosses or touches the x-axis.

skills.name: The Discriminant of a Quadratic Function
skills.description: Use b² − 4ac to tell how many times the graph of y = ax² + bx + c meets the x-axis.

skills.name: The Axis of Symmetry of a Parabola
skills.description: Find the vertical line x = h that divides a parabola into mirror-image halves, using x = −b/(2a) or symmetric points.

skills.name: The Average of the Roots Formula
skills.description: Use the fact that the average of a quadratic's two roots is −b/(2a), which locates the vertex's x-coordinate.

skills.name: The Vertex Form of a Parabola
skills.description: Read the vertex, axis, direction and stretch of a parabola from y = a(x − h)² + k.

skills.name: Writing the Equation of a Parabola in Vertex Form
skills.description: Write a parabola's equation in vertex form, either from its vertex and one other point or by completing the square.

skills.name: Domain and Range of Quadratic Functions
skills.description: Determine the domain and range of a quadratic function, using the vertex and the sign of a to find the range.

skills.name: Solving Systems of Nonlinear Equations
skills.description: Solve systems where at least one equation is nonlinear, such as a circle and a line, using substitution or elimination.

skills.name: Finding Intersections of Lines and Quadratic Functions
skills.description: Find where a line meets a parabola by setting the expressions equal and solving the resulting quadratic equation.

skills.name: Inverses of Quadratic Functions
skills.description: Find the inverse of a quadratic function by restricting its domain to one side of the vertex, then solving for x.

skills.name: Modeling Downwards Vertical Motion
skills.description: Model falling or downward-thrown objects with a quadratic height function and solve it to find landing times.

skills.name: Closure Properties of Polynomials
skills.description: Understand that adding, subtracting, or multiplying polynomials always gives a polynomial, while dividing does not.

skills.name: The Least Common Multiple of Two Monomials
skills.description: Find the least common multiple of two monomials using the LCM of the coefficients and highest variable powers.

skills.name: The Least Common Multiple of Two Polynomials
skills.description: Find the least common multiple of two polynomials by factoring each and keeping every factor at its highest power.

skills.name: Determining the Roots of Polynomials
skills.description: Find the values of x that make a polynomial equal zero, usually by factoring and using the zero-product property.

skills.name: Solving Polynomial Equations Using the GCF
skills.description: Solve polynomial equations by factoring out the greatest common factor and applying the zero-product property.

skills.name: Solving Cubic Equations by Grouping
skills.description: Solve four-term cubic equations by grouping pairs of terms to factor, then setting each factor equal to zero.

skills.name: Graphing Elementary Cubic Functions
skills.description: Sketch y = x³ and its shifted, stretched, and reflected versions using key points and transformations.

skills.name: End Behavior of Polynomials
skills.description: Predict what a polynomial graph does far to the left and right using its degree and leading coefficient.

skills.name: Further Factoring of Polynomials Using GCFs
skills.description: Take out harder greatest common factors, including negative factors, several variables, and whole binomial factors.

skills.name: Factoring Higher-Order Polynomials as a Difference of Squares
skills.description: Factor higher-power expressions such as x⁴ − 16 by spotting squares of powers, repeating the pattern where possible.

skills.name: Factoring Cubic Expressions by Grouping
skills.description: Factor four-term cubic expressions by pairing terms and pulling out a shared binomial factor.

skills.name: Factoring Sums and Differences of Cubes
skills.description: Factor a³ + b³ and a³ − b³ using the standard sum and difference of cubes formulas.

skills.name: Factoring Biquadratic Expressions
skills.description: Factor fourth-degree expressions of the form ax⁴ + bx² + c by treating them as quadratics in x².

skills.name: Dividing Polynomials Using Synthetic Division
skills.description: Divide a polynomial by x − c quickly using synthetic division on its coefficients alone.

skills.name: Dividing Polynomials by Linear Binomials Using Long Division
skills.description: Divide a polynomial by a linear binomial such as x − 2 using the long division algorithm.

skills.name: Dividing Polynomials Using Long Division
skills.description: Divide one polynomial by another of any degree using long division, finding the quotient and remainder.

skills.name: Dividing Polynomials by Manipulating Rational Expressions
skills.description: Divide polynomials by rewriting the numerator so the divisor can be split off algebraically, without the long division layout.

skills.name: The Factor Theorem
skills.description: State and use the rule that (x − a) is a factor of a polynomial p(x) exactly when p(a) = 0.

skills.name: Determining Polynomial Coefficients Using the Factor Theorem
skills.description: Use the fact that (x − a) is a factor exactly when p(a) = 0 to solve for unknown coefficients in a polynomial.

skills.name: Factoring Cubic Polynomials Using the Factor Theorem
skills.description: Factor a cubic by finding one root with the factor theorem, dividing it out, and factoring the remaining quadratic.

skills.name: Factoring Quartic Polynomials Using the Factor Theorem
skills.description: Factor a degree-4 polynomial by repeatedly finding roots with the factor theorem and dividing until a quadratic remains.

skills.name: Multiplicities of the Roots of Polynomials
skills.description: Identify how many times a root is repeated in a polynomial and what that means for factoring and for the graph.

skills.name: The Remainder Theorem
skills.description: Find the remainder of dividing a polynomial f(x) by (x − a) simply by evaluating f(a).

skills.name: The Rational Roots Theorem
skills.description: List the only possible rational roots of an integer-coefficient polynomial using divisors of its constant and leading coefficients.

skills.name: Graphing Cubic Curves Containing Three Distinct Real Roots
skills.description: Sketch a cubic with three different real roots using its x-intercepts, y-intercept, and the sign of the leading coefficient.

skills.name: Graphing Cubic Curves Containing a Double Root
skills.description: Sketch a cubic of the form a(x − r)²(x − s), touching the axis at the double root and crossing at the single root.

skills.name: Graphing Cubic Curves Containing One Distinct Real Root
skills.description: Sketch a cubic that meets the x-axis only once, either through an irreducible quadratic factor or a triple root.

skills.name: Graphing General Polynomials
skills.description: Sketch any factored polynomial from its end behaviour, real roots, root multiplicities, and y-intercept.

skills.name: The Real Number System
skills.description: Classify numbers as natural, whole, integer, rational, or irrational, and see how these sets nest inside the reals.

skills.name: Sums and Products of Rational and Irrational Numbers
skills.description: Decide whether sums and products involving rational and irrational numbers are rational or irrational, and justify it.

skills.name: Imaginary Numbers
skills.description: Define i as a square root of −1, simplify square roots of negative numbers, and reduce powers of i.

skills.name: Quadratic Equations with Purely Imaginary Solutions
skills.description: Solve quadratics such as x² + 9 = 0 whose solutions are pure multiples of i, using square roots of negative numbers.

skills.name: Complex Numbers
skills.description: Write numbers in the form a + bi and add, subtract, and multiply them using i² = −1.

skills.name: Adding and Subtracting Complex Numbers
skills.description: Add or subtract complex numbers by combining real parts with real parts and imaginary parts with imaginary parts.

skills.name: Multiplying Complex Numbers
skills.description: Multiply complex numbers by distributing every term, replacing i² with −1, and collecting real and imaginary parts.

skills.name: Solving Quadratic Equations With Complex Roots
skills.description: Use the quadratic formula when the discriminant is negative to find a pair of complex conjugate roots.

skills.name: The Cyclic Property of the Imaginary Unit
skills.description: Simplify any whole-number power of i using the repeating four-step cycle i, −1, −i, 1.

skills.name: The Complex Plane
skills.description: Plot complex numbers as points or arrows, using a horizontal real axis and a vertical imaginary axis.

skills.name: The Magnitude of a Complex Number
skills.description: Compute a complex number's distance from the origin, |a + bi| = √(a² + b²), using the Pythagorean theorem.

skills.name: The Argument of a Complex Number
skills.description: Find the angle a complex number makes with the positive real axis, taking care to place it in the correct quadrant.

skills.name: The Arithmetic of Functions
skills.description: Combine functions by adding, subtracting, multiplying, and dividing their outputs, while tracking the domain of each result.

skills.name: Describing Function Composition
skills.description: Explain and evaluate compositions f(g(x)), where one function's output becomes the next function's input.

skills.name: Local Extrema of Functions
skills.description: Identify local maxima and minima, the points where a function is higher or lower than all nearby values.

skills.name: One-To-One Functions
skills.description: Recognize one-to-one functions, where each output comes from exactly one input, using algebra or the horizontal line test.

skills.name: Introduction to Inverse Functions
skills.description: Understand an inverse function as the rule that undoes a function, sending each output back to the input it came from.

skills.name: Calculating the Inverse of a Function
skills.description: Find a formula for an inverse function by swapping x and y and solving for y, then check it by composition.

skills.name: Graphs of Inverse Functions
skills.description: Sketch the graph of an inverse function by reflecting the original graph across the line y = x.

skills.name: Domain and Range of Inverse Functions
skills.description: Find the domain and range of an inverse function by swapping those of the original, restricting the domain when needed.

skills.name: Invertible Functions
skills.description: Decide whether a function has an inverse, and restrict its domain when needed to make it invertible.

skills.name: Plotting X as a Function of Y
skills.description: Graph relations written as x = g(y) by choosing y-values, computing x, and plotting the resulting points.

skills.name: Periodic Functions
skills.description: Recognize functions whose values repeat at regular intervals and find the length of one repeating cycle, the period.

skills.name: Even and Odd Functions
skills.description: Classify functions by symmetry: even functions satisfy f(−x) = f(x) and odd functions satisfy f(−x) = −f(x).

skills.name: Unbounded Behavior of Functions Near a Point
skills.description: Describe how a function's values grow without bound as the input approaches a point, producing a vertical asymptote.

skills.name: Vertical Translations of Functions
skills.description: Shift a graph up or down by adding a constant to the function's output.

skills.name: Horizontal Translations of Functions
skills.description: Shift a graph left or right by replacing x with x − h, which moves every point h units horizontally.

skills.name: Vertical Stretches of Functions
skills.description: Stretch or compress a graph vertically by multiplying the function's output by a constant factor.

skills.name: Horizontal Stretches of Functions
skills.description: Stretch or compress a graph horizontally by replacing x with bx, where the effect is a scale by 1/b.

skills.name: Vertical Reflections of Functions
skills.description: Reflect a graph across the x-axis by multiplying the function's output by −1.

skills.name: Horizontal Reflections of Functions
skills.description: Reflect a graph across the y-axis by replacing x with −x in the function.

skills.name: Combining Graph Transformations: Two Operations
skills.description: Combine two graph transformations, such as a stretch and a shift, and see when their order changes the result.

skills.name: Combining Graph Transformations: Three or More Operations
skills.description: Apply three or more stretches, reflections, and shifts to a graph in a consistent order and track key points.

skills.name: Constructing Functions Using Transformations
skills.description: Write the formula for a function by applying described transformations to a known parent function.

skills.name: Combining Reflections With Other Graph Transformations
skills.description: Combine reflections across an axis with shifts and stretches, handling the negative sign in the correct place.

skills.name: Finding Points on Transformed Curves
skills.description: Given a point on y = f(x), find the matching point on a transformed graph such as y = a·f(x − h) + k.

skills.name: The Domain and Range of Transformed Functions
skills.description: Find the domain and range of a transformed function by tracking how each transformation moves the parent's boundaries.

skills.name: Converting From Exponential to Logarithmic Form
skills.description: Rewriting an exponential statement such as b^y = x as the equivalent logarithm log_b(x) = y.

skills.name: Converting From Logarithmic to Exponential Form
skills.description: Rewriting a logarithmic statement log_b(x) = y as b^y = x, often to evaluate a log or solve for an unknown.

skills.name: Evaluating Logarithms
skills.description: Finding the value of a logarithm such as log_2(8) by asking what exponent on the base produces the argument.

skills.name: The Natural Logarithm
skills.description: The logarithm with base e ≈ 2.71828, written ln(x), which is the inverse of the exponential function e^x.

skills.name: The Common Logarithm
skills.description: The base-10 logarithm, written log(x) or log10(x), which gives the power of 10 that produces x.

skills.name: Simplifying Logarithmic Expressions
skills.description: Using the inverse relationship between logs and exponentials, such as log_b(b^x) = x, to reduce log expressions to simpler values.

skills.name: The Product Rule for Logarithms
skills.description: Using log_b(MN) = log_b(M) + log_b(N) to split the log of a product into a sum, or combine a sum into one log.

skills.name: The Quotient Rule for Logarithms
skills.description: Using log_b(M/N) = log_b(M) − log_b(N) to turn the log of a quotient into a difference, or the reverse.

skills.name: The Power Rule for Logarithms
skills.description: Using log_b(M^p) = p·log_b(M) to move an exponent in front of a logarithm or back inside it.

skills.name: Combining the Laws of Logarithms
skills.description: Expanding or condensing logarithmic expressions by applying the product, quotient, and power rules together.

skills.name: The Change of Base Formula for Logarithms
skills.description: Rewriting a logarithm in any base as a ratio of logs in another base, such as log_b(x) = ln(x)/ln(b).

skills.name: Solving Exponential Equations Using Logarithms
skills.description: Solving equations where the unknown is in an exponent by taking logarithms of both sides, as in 3^x = 20.

skills.name: Solving Equations Containing the Exponential Function
skills.description: Solve equations involving eˣ by isolating the exponential term and taking the natural logarithm of both sides.

skills.name: Solving Exponential Equations With Different Bases
skills.description: Solve exponential equations with bases like 4 and 8 by rewriting both as powers of a shared base, then equating exponents.

skills.name: Solving Exponential Equations With Different Bases Using Logarithms
skills.description: Solve exponential equations whose bases cannot share a common base by taking logarithms of both sides and solving for the exponent.

skills.name: Solving Exponential Equations Using the Zero-Product Property
skills.description: Solve exponential equations by factoring, often after substituting u = bˣ, then setting each factor to zero and rejecting impossible cases.

skills.name: Solving Logarithmic Equations
skills.description: Solving equations with the unknown inside a logarithm by isolating the log, converting to exponential form, and checking the domain.

skills.name: Solving Logarithmic Equations Containing the Natural Logarithm
skills.description: Solving equations involving ln(x) by isolating the natural logarithm and exponentiating with base e.

skills.name: Solving Logarithmic Equations Using the Laws of Logarithms
skills.description: Solving log equations by first condensing several same-base logs into one with the product or quotient rule.

skills.name: Solving Logarithmic Equations by Combining the Laws of Logarithms
skills.description: Solving log equations that need several log laws at once, including the power rule, before converting to exponential form.

skills.name: Solving Logarithmic Equations With Logarithms on Both Sides
skills.description: Solving equations of the form log_b(A) = log_b(B) by setting the arguments equal and rejecting invalid solutions.

skills.name: Vertical Translations of Exponential Growth Functions
skills.description: Shifting an exponential growth graph up or down by adding a constant, which moves its horizontal asymptote and range.

skills.name: Vertical Translations of Exponential Decay Functions
skills.description: Shift a decay graph such as y = (1/2)ˣ up or down by adding a constant k, which moves its horizontal asymptote to y = k.

skills.name: Vertical Reflections of Exponential Functions
skills.description: Reflect an exponential graph across the x-axis by negating the function, as in y = −bˣ, and describe the effect on range and direction.

skills.name: Combining Graph Transformations of Exponential Functions
skills.description: Graph y = a·b^(x − h) + k by applying horizontal shifts, stretches, reflections and vertical shifts to a basic exponential graph in order.

skills.name: Properties of Transformed Exponential Functions
skills.description: Determine the domain, range, asymptote, intercepts and increasing or decreasing behavior of f(x) = a·b^(x − h) + k.

skills.name: Inverses of Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
skills.description: Recognize y = bˣ and y = log_b(x) as inverse functions, and find inverses of simple exponential and logarithmic functions.

skills.name: Graphing Logarithmic Functions
skills.description: Sketching y = log_b(x) and its transformations using the inverse relationship with exponentials, the domain, and the vertical asymptote.

skills.name: Combining Graph Transformations of Logarithmic Functions
skills.description: Applying several shifts, stretches, and reflections together to graph functions of the form y = a·log_b(x − h) + k.

skills.name: Properties of Transformed Logarithmic Functions
skills.description: Reading the domain, range, asymptote, intercepts, and increasing or decreasing behaviour of a transformed logarithmic function from its equation.

skills.name: Simplifying Rational Expressions Using Polynomial Factorization
skills.description: Reduce a rational expression to lowest terms by factoring numerator and denominator and cancelling common factors.

skills.name: Adding and Subtracting Rational Expressions
skills.description: Combine rational expressions by rewriting them over a least common denominator and adding or subtracting numerators.

skills.name: Adding Rational Expressions With No Common Factors in the Denominator
skills.description: Add rational expressions whose denominators share no factors by using their product as the common denominator.

skills.name: Multiplying Rational Expressions
skills.description: Multiply rational expressions by factoring, cancelling common factors across numerators and denominators, then multiplying.

skills.name: Dividing Rational Expressions
skills.description: Divide one rational expression by another by multiplying by the reciprocal of the divisor, then simplify.

skills.name: Expressing Rational Functions as Sums of Partial Fractions
skills.description: Decompose a rational function into a sum of simpler fractions whose denominators are the factors of the original.

skills.name: Rational Equations With Three Terms
skills.description: Solve rational equations with three fractional terms by multiplying every term by the least common denominator.

skills.name: Advanced Rational Equations
skills.description: Solve rational equations whose denominators must be factored and which lead to quadratics and possible extraneous roots.

skills.name: Graphing Reciprocal Functions
skills.description: Sketch y = 1/x and y = k/x, showing both branches and the asymptotes along the axes.

skills.name: Graph Transformations of Reciprocal Functions
skills.description: Sketch y = a/(x − h) + k by shifting the asymptotes of y = 1/x and stretching or reflecting its branches.

skills.name: Combining Graph Transformations of Reciprocal Functions
skills.description: Apply several transformations at once to y = 1/x, tracking asymptotes and key points through each step.

skills.name: Domain and Range of Transformed Reciprocal Functions
skills.description: State the domain and range of y = a/(x − h) + k by reading off the excluded x-value and y-value.

skills.name: Inverses of Reciprocal Functions
skills.description: Find the inverse of a reciprocal function by swapping x and y, and note how the asymptotes swap too.

skills.name: Finding Intersections of Lines and Reciprocal Functions
skills.description: Find where a straight line meets a reciprocal curve by setting them equal and solving the resulting quadratic.

skills.name: Roots of Rational Functions
skills.description: Find the x-intercepts of a rational function by setting the numerator to zero and excluding denominator zeros.

skills.name: Vertical Asymptotes of Rational Functions
skills.description: Locate vertical asymptotes of a rational function at denominator zeros that remain after cancelling common factors.

skills.name: Horizontal Asymptotes of Rational Functions
skills.description: Find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function by comparing the degrees of numerator and denominator.

skills.name: Rationalizing Denominators of Algebraic Expressions
skills.description: Remove a single radical from a denominator by multiplying top and bottom by a suitable root.

skills.name: Rationalizing Denominators With Two Terms
skills.description: Rationalize a two-term denominator containing a radical by multiplying by its conjugate.

skills.name: Further Rationalizing Denominators of Algebraic Expressions
skills.description: Rationalize harder denominators, such as sums or differences of two radicals, and simplify the resulting expressions.

skills.name: Solving Radical Equations
skills.description: Solve equations containing a radical by isolating it, raising both sides to a power, and checking for extraneous solutions.

skills.name: Inverses of Radical Functions
skills.description: Find inverses of square root and cube root functions, restricting domains so the inverse is a function.

skills.name: Graphing the Square Root Function
skills.description: Sketch y = √x from key points, recognizing its starting point, domain x ≥ 0, and range y ≥ 0.

skills.name: Graph Transformations of Square Root Functions
skills.description: Sketch y = a√(b(x − h)) + k by shifting, stretching, and reflecting the basic square root curve.

skills.name: Graphing the Cube Root Function
skills.description: Sketch y = ∛x from key points, noting it is defined for all real numbers and symmetric about the origin.

skills.name: Properties of Transformed Square Root Functions
skills.description: Read the endpoint, direction, and intercepts of a transformed square root function directly from its equation.

skills.name: The Domain of a Transformed Radical Function
skills.description: Determine which inputs a transformed radical function accepts by requiring an even-index radicand to be non-negative.

skills.name: The Range of a Transformed Radical Function
skills.description: Determine the possible output values of a transformed radical function from its vertical shift and reflection.

skills.name: Roots of Transformed Radical Functions
skills.description: Find where a transformed square root or cube root function crosses the x-axis by solving f(x) = 0.

skills.name: Introduction to Sequences
skills.description: Understand a sequence as an ordered list of terms indexed by position and generate terms from an explicit formula.

skills.name: Recursive Sequences
skills.description: Define a sequence by giving starting terms and a rule that builds each new term from earlier ones.

skills.name: Fibonacci Sequences
skills.description: Generate and analyse the Fibonacci sequence, where each term is the sum of the two terms before it.

skills.name: Sigma Notation
skills.description: Read and write sums compactly with the Greek letter sigma, an index variable, and lower and upper limits.

skills.name: Properties of Finite Series
skills.description: Use rules for splitting, scaling and evaluating finite sums written in sigma notation, including standard sum formulas.

skills.name: Arithmetic Sequences
skills.description: Recognize sequences that change by the same amount each step and describe them with a first term and common difference.

skills.name: Recursive Formulas for Arithmetic Sequences
skills.description: Write and use a recursive rule for an arithmetic sequence: a first term plus a rule adding the common difference.

skills.name: The Nth Term of an Arithmetic Sequence
skills.description: Write and use an = a1 + (n − 1)d to find any term of an arithmetic sequence without listing the earlier terms.

skills.name: Translating Between Explicit and Recursive Formulas for Arithmetic Sequences
skills.description: Convert an arithmetic sequence's recursive rule into an explicit nth-term formula, and convert explicit formulas back.

skills.name: Finding the Common Difference of an Arithmetic Sequence
skills.description: Calculate the common difference of an arithmetic sequence by subtracting consecutive terms or reading it from a formula.

skills.name: Finding the Nth Term of an Arithmetic Sequence Given Two Terms
skills.description: Build the explicit formula of an arithmetic sequence when only two of its terms and their positions are known.

skills.name: Determining Indexes of Terms in Arithmetic Sequences
skills.description: Find the position of a given value in an arithmetic sequence, or show that the value is not a term.

skills.name: Introduction to Geometric Sequences
skills.description: Identify geometric sequences, in which each term is multiplied by the same nonzero common ratio to get the next.

skills.name: The Recursive Formula for a Geometric Sequence
skills.description: Describe a geometric sequence recursively with a first term and the rule that each term is r times the previous one.

skills.name: The Nth Term of a Geometric Sequence
skills.description: Use the explicit formula an = a1·r^(n−1) to find any term of a geometric sequence directly.

skills.name: Translating Between Explicit and Recursive Formulas for Geometric Sequences
skills.description: Move between the recursive rule and the explicit formula of a geometric sequence by identifying its first term and ratio.

skills.name: Finding the Common Ratio of a Geometric Sequence Given Two Terms
skills.description: Find the common ratio of a geometric sequence from two known terms that need not be next to each other.

skills.name: Determining Indexes of Terms in Geometric Sequences
skills.description: Solve for the position of a given term in a geometric sequence, using powers or logarithms.

skills.name: Finding Equations of Parallel Lines
skills.description: Write the equation of a line parallel to a given line and passing through a given point, using equal slopes.

skills.name: Perpendicular Lines in the Coordinate Plane
