skills.description: Decide whether two lines in the coordinate plane are perpendicular by checking whether their slopes multiply to −1.

skills.name: Finding Equations of Perpendicular Lines
skills.description: Write the equation of a line perpendicular to a given line through a given point, using the negative reciprocal slope.

skills.name: Midpoints in the Coordinate Plane
skills.description: Find the midpoint of a segment by averaging the x-coordinates and the y-coordinates of its endpoints.

skills.name: The Distance Formula
skills.description: Find the straight-line distance between two points in the plane from their coordinates.

skills.name: The Shortest Distance Between a Point and a Line
skills.description: Find the perpendicular distance from a point to a straight line, the smallest distance to any point on the line.

skills.name: The Distance Formula in Three Dimensions
skills.description: Compute the distance between two points in space by adding a z-difference term to the planar distance formula.

skills.name: Translations of Geometric Figures
skills.description: Slide every point of a figure the same distance in the same direction, described by a vector or coordinate rule.

skills.name: Rotations of Geometric Figures
skills.description: Rotate a figure by a given angle and direction about a centre, keeping every point the same distance from that centre.

skills.name: Rotating Objects in the Coordinate Plane Using Functions
skills.description: Rotate points and figures about the origin with coordinate rules, including the general formula for any angle θ.

skills.name: Reflections of Geometric Figures in the Cartesian Plane
skills.description: Reflect figures across the x-axis or y-axis, or through the origin, using simple coordinate sign changes.

skills.name: Reflections of Figures Across Arbitrary Lines
skills.description: Reflect a figure across any line, including slanted lines, by using perpendiculars to the mirror line.

skills.name: Dilations of Geometric Figures
skills.description: Enlarge or reduce a figure from a fixed centre by a scale factor, producing a similar figure with the same angles.

skills.name: Dilations of Figures in the Coordinate Plane
skills.description: Dilate a figure in the coordinate plane by multiplying coordinates by a scale factor, about the origin or another centre.

skills.name: Stretches of Geometric Figures
skills.description: Scale a figure by a factor in one direction only, such as (x, y) → (kx, y), and track how its shape changes.

skills.name: Combining Stretches of Geometric Figures
skills.description: Apply horizontal and vertical stretches together, using (x, y) → (ax, by), and describe their combined effect on a figure.

skills.name: Combining Geometric Transformations
skills.description: Apply a sequence of geometric transformations to a figure and track how their order changes the final image.

skills.name: Rigid Motions and Congruence
skills.description: Use translations, reflections, and rotations to show that two figures are congruent by mapping one exactly onto the other.

skills.name: Similarity and Similar Polygons
skills.description: Recognize similar polygons, which have equal corresponding angles and proportional sides, and use the scale factor to find missing lengths.

skills.name: Similarity Transformations
skills.description: Combine rigid motions with dilations to map a figure onto a copy with the same shape but possibly a different size.

skills.name: Reflective Symmetry
skills.description: Identify lines of symmetry, where reflecting or folding a figure maps it exactly onto itself.

skills.name: Rotational Symmetry
skills.description: Decide whether a figure looks unchanged after a partial turn about its centre, and find its order of rotational symmetry.

skills.name: Identifying Three-Dimensional Shapes
skills.description: Name common solids such as prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones, and spheres by examining their faces and bases.

skills.name: Faces, Vertices, and Edges of Polyhedrons
skills.description: Count and identify the faces, edges, and vertices of polyhedra such as prisms and pyramids.

skills.name: Nets of Polyhedrons
skills.description: Recognize and draw nets, the flat arrangements of polygons that fold up into a given polyhedron.

skills.name: Finding Surface Areas Using Nets
skills.description: Find a solid's surface area by unfolding it into a flat net and adding the areas of all its pieces.

skills.name: Volumes of Cubes
skills.description: Calculate a cube's volume with V = s³, multiplying the edge length by itself three times.

skills.name: Volumes of Rectangular Solids
skills.description: Compute the volume of a box-shaped solid by multiplying its length, width, and height, V = lwh.

skills.name: Surface Areas of Cubes
skills.description: Compute a cube's surface area with SA = 6s², since it has six identical square faces.

skills.name: Volumes of Spheres
skills.description: Calculate a sphere's volume using V = (4/3)πr³.

skills.name: Surface Areas of Spheres
skills.description: Compute a sphere's surface area with SA = 4πr², four times the area of its largest cross-sectional circle.

skills.name: Volumes of Cylinders
skills.description: Find a cylinder's volume by multiplying the area of its circular base by its height, V = πr²h.

skills.name: Surface Areas of Cylinders
skills.description: Find a cylinder's surface area by adding its two circular ends to the curved rectangle that wraps around it.

skills.name: Euler's Formula for Polyhedra
skills.description: Use V − E + F = 2 to relate the numbers of vertices, edges, and faces of a convex polyhedron.

skills.name: The Five Platonic Solids
skills.description: Identify the five regular convex polyhedra: tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, and icosahedron.

skills.name: Angles and Sides in Right Triangles
skills.description: Name the hypotenuse, opposite side and adjacent side of a right triangle relative to a chosen acute angle.

skills.name: The Trigonometric Ratios
skills.description: Define sine, cosine and tangent as ratios of sides in a right triangle and compute them for a given angle.

skills.name: Calculating Trigonometric Ratios Using the Pythagorean Theorem
skills.description: Find all trigonometric ratios of an angle from one given ratio or two sides by first finding the missing side.

skills.name: Calculating Side Lengths of Right Triangles Using Trigonometry
skills.description: Use sine, cosine or tangent with a known angle and side to calculate an unknown side of a right triangle.

skills.name: Calculating Angles in Right Triangles Using Trigonometry
skills.description: Find an unknown acute angle in a right triangle from two known sides using inverse sine, cosine or tangent.

skills.name: The Reciprocal Trigonometric Ratios
skills.description: Define cosecant, secant and cotangent as reciprocals of sine, cosine and tangent, and calculate them from triangle sides.

skills.name: Trigonometric Functions of Complementary Angles
skills.description: Use cofunction identities: the sine of an angle equals the cosine of its complement, with similar tangent-cotangent and secant-cosecant pairs.

skills.name: Special Trigonometric Ratios
skills.description: Know the exact sine, cosine and tangent of 30°, 45° and 60°, derived from two special right triangles.

skills.name: Calculating Areas of Right Triangles Using Trigonometry
skills.description: Find a right triangle's area when only an angle and one side are known, using trigonometry to get the missing leg.

skills.name: Introduction to Radians
skills.description: Measure angles in radians, where one radian cuts off an arc equal to the radius, and convert between radians and degrees.

skills.name: Trigonometric Ratios With Radians
skills.description: Evaluate sine, cosine and tangent for angles given in radians, including exact values at π/6, π/4 and π/3.

skills.name: The Law of Sines
skills.description: Use a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C to find missing sides or angles when a side and its opposite angle are known.

skills.name: The Law of Cosines
skills.description: Use c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos C to find a missing side or angle in any triangle from SAS or SSS information.

skills.name: The Area of a General Triangle
skills.description: Calculate the area of any triangle from two sides and their included angle using Area = ½ab sin C.

skills.name: Angles in the Coordinate Plane
skills.description: Place angles in standard position on coordinate axes and identify the quadrant in which the terminal side lies.

skills.name: Negative Angles in the Coordinate Plane
skills.description: Draw and interpret negative angles, which rotate clockwise from the positive x-axis, and relate them to positive angles.

skills.name: Coterminal Angles
skills.description: Identify angles that share the same terminal side by adding or subtracting full turns of 360° or 2π.

skills.name: Calculating Reference Angles
skills.description: Find the acute angle between an angle's terminal side and the x-axis, used to evaluate trig functions in any quadrant.

skills.name: Properties of the Unit Circle in the First Quadrant
skills.description: Describe first-quadrant points on the unit circle as (cos θ, sin θ) and learn the key coordinates at 30°, 45° and 60°.

skills.name: Extending the Trigonometric Ratios Using the Unit Circle
skills.description: Define sine, cosine and tangent for any angle using the coordinates of a point on the unit circle.

skills.name: Extending the Trigonometric Ratios Using Angles in Radians
skills.description: Evaluate trigonometric functions of radian angles in any quadrant, such as 7π/6 or 5π/3, using reference angles.

skills.name: Extending the Trigonometric Ratios to Negative Angles
skills.description: Evaluate trig functions of negative angles using the symmetry rules sin(−θ) = −sin θ and cos(−θ) = cos θ.

skills.name: Extending the Trigonometric Ratios to Large Angles
skills.description: Evaluate trigonometric functions of angles bigger than 360° by removing full turns, then using reference angles and quadrant signs.

skills.name: Using the Pythagorean Identity in the First Quadrant
skills.description: Use sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 to find cosine from sine, or sine from cosine, for an acute angle.

skills.name: Extending the Pythagorean Identity to All Quadrants
skills.description: Apply sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 to angles in any quadrant, choosing the sign of the square root from the quadrant.

skills.name: Finding Trigonometric Ratios of Quadrantal Angles
skills.description: Find sine, cosine and tangent of angles on the axes, such as 0°, 90°, 180° and 270°, from unit-circle coordinates.

skills.name: Trigonometric Ratios of Quadrantal Angles Outside the Standard Range
skills.description: Find exact sine, cosine, and tangent values of quadrantal angles beyond 0° to 360°, such as 450° or −90°, using coterminal angles.

skills.name: Finding Trigonometric Ratios of Special Angles Using the Unit Circle
skills.description: Read exact trig values for multiples of 30° and 45°, such as 150° or 225°, from symmetric points on the unit circle.

skills.name: Evaluating Trigonometric Expressions
skills.description: Evaluate expressions that combine trigonometric values, such as 2 sin 30° + cos²45°, exactly using known special values.

skills.name: Further Extensions of the Special Trigonometric Ratios
skills.description: Apply special-angle values to negative angles, angles beyond 360°, and the reciprocal functions secant, cosecant and cotangent.

skills.name: Graphing Sine and Cosine
skills.description: Plot y = sin x and y = cos x from unit-circle values, showing their wave shape, period 2π, and range from −1 to 1.

skills.name: Graphing Tangent and Cotangent
skills.description: Sketch y = tan x and y = cot x, placing their vertical asymptotes, zeros, and period-π branches correctly.

skills.name: Graphing Secant and Cosecant
skills.description: Sketch y = sec x and y = csc x as reciprocals of cosine and sine, with U-shaped branches and vertical asymptotes.

skills.name: Describing Properties of the Sine Function
skills.description: Describe the graph of y = sin x, including its domain, range, period, amplitude, zeros, symmetry and key points.

skills.name: Describing Properties of the Cosine Function
skills.description: Describe the graph of y = cos x, including its domain, range, period, amplitude, zeros, symmetry and key points.

skills.name: Describing Properties of the Tangent Function
skills.description: Describe the graph of y = tan x, with period π, vertical asymptotes at odd multiples of π/2, and increasing branches.

skills.name: Describing Properties of the Secant Function
skills.description: Describe the graph of y = sec x: its domain, range, period, vertical asymptotes and relationship to the cosine curve.

skills.name: Describing Properties of the Cosecant Function
skills.description: Describe the graph of y = csc x: its domain, range, period, vertical asymptotes and relationship to the sine curve.

skills.name: Describing Properties of the Cotangent Function
skills.description: Describe the graph of y = cot x, with period π, vertical asymptotes at multiples of π, and decreasing branches.

skills.name: Vertical Translations of Trigonometric Functions
skills.description: Shift trigonometric graphs up or down with y = f(x) + D, moving the midline and the range.

skills.name: Vertical Stretches of Trigonometric Functions
skills.description: Scale a trigonometric graph vertically with y = A f(x), changing the amplitude of sinusoids or the steepness of tangent branches.

skills.name: Horizontal Translations of Trigonometric Functions
skills.description: Shift trigonometric graphs left or right using y = f(x − C) and identify the resulting phase shift.

skills.name: Horizontal Stretches of Trigonometric Functions
skills.description: Change the period of a trigonometric function with y = f(Bx), compressing or stretching its graph horizontally.

skills.name: Combining Graph Transformations of Sine and Cosine
skills.description: Apply several transformations at once to sine or cosine, in a sensible order, to graph y = A sin(B(x − C)) + D.

skills.name: Graph Transformations of Tangent and Cotangent
skills.description: Apply individual stretches, shifts, and reflections to tangent and cotangent graphs and track how asymptotes and key points move.

skills.name: Combining Graph Transformations of Tangent and Cotangent
skills.description: Graph tangent and cotangent functions that combine scaling, phase shift, reflection, and vertical shift in one equation.

skills.name: Combining Graph Transformations of Secant and Cosecant
skills.description: Sketch secant and cosecant graphs that combine stretches, shifts, and reflections by first drawing the transformed guide sinusoid.

skills.name: Graphing Reflections of Trigonometric Functions
skills.description: Reflect trigonometric graphs across the x-axis or y-axis and use even and odd symmetry to predict the result.

skills.name: Properties of Transformed Sine and Cosine Functions
skills.description: Identify the amplitude, period, phase shift, midline, and range of a transformed sine or cosine function from its equation.

skills.name: Finding Zeros and Extrema of Transformed Sine and Cosine Functions
skills.description: Locate the x-intercepts, maxima, and minima of transformed sine and cosine functions, including every repeat.

skills.name: Properties of Transformed Tangent and Cotangent Functions
skills.description: Determine the period, asymptotes, domain, and range of transformed tangent and cotangent functions from their equations.

skills.name: Properties of Transformed Secant and Cosecant Functions
skills.description: Read the period, asymptotes, domain, and range of transformed secant and cosecant functions directly from their equations.

skills.name: Introduction to Vectors
skills.description: Learn what a vector is, how it differs from a scalar, and how vectors are written and compared.

skills.name: The Triangle Law for the Addition of Two Vectors
skills.description: Add two vectors geometrically by placing them head to tail and drawing the resultant from start to finish.

skills.name: The Magnitude of a Vector
skills.description: Find the length of a two-dimensional vector from its components using the Pythagorean theorem.

skills.name: Problem Solving Using Vector Diagrams
skills.description: Solve geometry problems by labelling a vector diagram, routing paths through known vectors, and interpreting results.

skills.name: Parallel Vectors
skills.description: Decide whether two vectors are parallel by checking whether one is a scalar multiple of the other.

skills.name: Unit Vectors
skills.description: Use vectors of length one to represent pure direction, including i and j, and normalize any nonzero vector.

skills.name: Linear Combinations of Vectors and Their Properties
skills.description: Form linear combinations sa + tb of vectors, apply their algebraic rules, and find unknown coefficients.

skills.name: Describing the Position Vector of a Point Using Known Vectors
skills.description: Express the position vector of a point, such as a midpoint or dividing point, in terms of given vectors.

skills.name: Two-Dimensional Vectors Expressed in Component Form
skills.description: Write a plane vector as horizontal and vertical components, (x, y) or xi + yj, and convert from length and angle.

skills.name: Addition and Scalar Multiplication of Cartesian Vectors in 2D
skills.description: Add, subtract and scale 2D vectors by working component by component on their x and y parts.

skills.name: Calculating the Magnitude of Cartesian Vectors in 2D
skills.description: Find the length of a 2D vector (x, y) using Pythagoras: its magnitude is √(x² + y²).

skills.name: The Finite Limit of a Function
skills.description: Understand lim x→a f(x) = L as the number f(x) approaches when x gets close to a, regardless of the value f(a).

skills.name: The Left and Right-Sided Limits of a Function
skills.description: Find the one-sided limits lim x→a⁻ f(x) and lim x→a⁺ f(x) by approaching a point only from the left or only from the right.

skills.name: Finding the Existence of a Limit Using One-Sided Limits
skills.description: Decide whether a two-sided limit exists by checking that the left-hand and right-hand limits both exist and are equal.

skills.name: Limits at Infinity from Graphs
skills.description: Use a graph's far-left and far-right behaviour to find limits as x → ∞ or x → −∞ and identify horizontal asymptotes.

skills.name: Infinite Limits from Graphs
skills.description: Read from a graph when a function grows without bound near a point, and write limits such as lim x→a f(x) = ∞ or −∞.

skills.name: Limits of Power Functions, and the Constant Rule for Limits
skills.description: Use the basic results lim x→a c = c and lim x→a xⁿ = aⁿ as building blocks for evaluating limits.

skills.name: The Sum Rule for Limits
skills.description: Find the limit of a sum or difference by adding or subtracting the individual limits, when each one exists.

skills.name: The Product and Quotient Rules for Limits
skills.description: Find the limit of a product or quotient from the limits of its parts, provided they exist and the denominator's limit is nonzero.

skills.name: The Power and Root Rules for Limits
skills.description: Pass a limit through powers and roots, using lim [f(x)]ⁿ = [lim f(x)]ⁿ and the matching rule for nth roots.

skills.name: Limits at Infinity of Polynomials
skills.description: Find the end behaviour of a polynomial as x → ±∞ from the sign of its leading coefficient and its degree.

skills.name: Limits of Reciprocal Functions
skills.description: Find limits of reciprocal functions like 1/x and 1/(x − a), including unbounded behaviour near zero and approach to 0 at infinity.

skills.name: Limits of Exponential Functions
skills.description: Evaluate limits of exponential functions such as bˣ and e^(−x), including their end behaviour and values at finite points.

skills.name: Limits of Logarithmic Functions
skills.description: Evaluate limits of logarithmic functions, including their behaviour as x → 0 from the right and as x → ∞.

skills.name: Limits of Radical Functions
skills.description: Evaluate limits of functions involving square roots and other radicals, paying attention to where the radicand is allowed.

skills.name: Limits of Trigonometric Functions
skills.description: Evaluate limits of sine, cosine, and tangent, using continuity for direct substitution and noting where tangent is undefined.

skills.name: Limits of Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions
skills.description: Evaluate limits of secant, cosecant, and cotangent by rewriting them as reciprocals involving sine and cosine.

skills.name: Limits of Piecewise Functions
skills.description: Evaluate limits of piecewise-defined functions, using the correct formula on each side of a boundary and comparing one-sided limits.

skills.name: Calculating Limits of Rational Functions by Factoring
skills.description: Resolve a 0/0 form in a rational function limit by factoring, cancelling the common factor, and then substituting.

skills.name: Determining Continuity from Graphs
skills.description: Identify from a graph where a function is continuous, spotting holes, jumps, and vertical asymptotes as discontinuities.

skills.name: Defining Continuity at a Point
skills.description: State and apply the three-part test for continuity at x = a: f(a) exists, the limit exists, and they are equal.

skills.name: Left and Right Continuity
skills.description: Decide whether a function is continuous from the left or from the right at a point by comparing one-sided limits with f(a).

skills.name: Continuity Over an Interval
skills.description: Determine whether a function is continuous on an open or closed interval, using one-sided continuity at included endpoints.

skills.name: The Average Rate of Change of a Function
skills.description: Compute how much a function's output changes per unit of input between two points, the slope of a secant line.

skills.name: The Average Rate of Change of a Function over a Varying Interval
skills.description: Express the average rate of change over [a, a + h] as an algebraic formula in h and simplify it.

skills.name: The Instantaneous Rate of Change of a Function at a Point
skills.description: Find how fast a function is changing at a single input by taking the limit of average rates as the interval shrinks.

skills.name: Defining the Derivative Using Derivative Notation
skills.description: Define the derivative as a limit of difference quotients and read and write its common notations.

skills.name: The Power Rule for Differentiation
skills.description: Differentiate powers of x with d/dx(xⁿ) = nxⁿ⁻¹, including roots and reciprocals rewritten as powers.

skills.name: The Sum and Constant Multiple Rules for Differentiation
skills.description: Differentiate sums, differences and constant multiples term by term, combining this with the power rule.

skills.name: Calculating the Slope of a Tangent Line Using Differentiation
skills.description: Compute the slope of the tangent to a curve at a point by evaluating the derivative there.

skills.name: Calculating the Equation of a Tangent Line Using Differentiation
skills.description: Write the equation of the line touching a curve at a given point, using the derivative as its slope.

skills.name: Calculating the Equation of a Normal Line Using Differentiation
skills.description: Find the line perpendicular to a curve's tangent at a point, using the negative reciprocal of the derivative as its slope.

skills.name: Interpreting the Meaning of the Derivative in Context
skills.description: Explain what a derivative's value and sign mean in a real situation, with correct units of output per input.

skills.name: Differentiating Exponential Functions
skills.description: Differentiate eˣ, aˣ and exponentials of inner functions using d/dx(eˣ) = eˣ and the chain rule.

skills.name: Differentiating Logarithmic Functions
skills.description: Differentiate ln x, logarithms to other bases, and logs of inner functions, using log laws to simplify first.

skills.name: Differentiating Trigonometric Functions
skills.description: Find derivatives of sine, cosine and tangent, and combine them with other rules, working in radians.

skills.name: Second and Higher-Order Derivatives
skills.description: Differentiate repeatedly to find second, third and higher derivatives, and interpret the second derivative as concavity or acceleration.

skills.name: The Product Rule for Differentiation
skills.description: Differentiate a product of two functions with (fg)' = f'g + fg'.

skills.name: The Quotient Rule for Differentiation
skills.description: Differentiate a ratio of two functions with (f/g)' = (f'g − fg')/g², where g is nonzero.

skills.name: Calculating Derivatives From Data and Tables
skills.description: Use tabulated function and derivative values with differentiation rules, or estimate derivatives from data using difference quotients.

skills.name: Calculating Derivatives From Graphs
skills.description: Read derivative values as tangent slopes from a graph and use graphed values with differentiation rules.

skills.name: Differentiating Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions
skills.description: Differentiate secant, cosecant and cotangent, deriving their formulas from sine and cosine with the quotient rule.

skills.name: The Chain Rule for Differentiation
skills.description: Differentiate a composite function f(g(x)) by multiplying the outer derivative, evaluated at the inner function, by the inner derivative.

skills.name: The Chain Rule With Exponential Functions
skills.description: Differentiate exponentials with a function in the exponent, such as e^(g(x)) or a^(g(x)), using the chain rule.

skills.name: The Chain Rule With Logarithmic Functions
skills.description: Differentiate logarithms of inner functions, such as ln(g(x)), using the result d/dx ln(g(x)) = g′(x)/g(x).

skills.name: The Chain Rule With Trigonometric Functions
skills.description: Differentiate trigonometric functions of an inner expression, such as sin(g(x)) or cos²(x), using the chain rule.

skills.name: Selecting Procedures for Calculating Derivatives
skills.description: Decide which differentiation rules an expression needs, and in what order, by analysing its structure.

skills.name: The Antiderivative
skills.description: Find a function whose derivative is a given function, and write the general antiderivative with an arbitrary constant C.

skills.name: The Constant Multiple Rule for Indefinite Integrals
skills.description: Move a constant factor outside an indefinite integral, using ∫ k·f(x) dx = k ∫ f(x) dx.

skills.name: The Sum Rule for Indefinite Integrals
skills.description: Integrate a sum or difference term by term, using ∫ [f(x) ± g(x)] dx = ∫ f(x) dx ± ∫ g(x) dx.

skills.name: Integrating the Reciprocal Function
skills.description: Integrate 1/x to get ln|x| + C, the case the power rule for integration cannot handle.

skills.name: Integrating Exponential Functions
skills.description: Find antiderivatives of eˣ, e^(kx) and aˣ, and evaluate definite integrals of simple exponentials.

skills.name: Integrating Trigonometric Functions
skills.description: Recall and apply the standard antiderivatives of sine, cosine and the other basic trig derivative results.

skills.name: The Mean of a Data Set
skills.description: Compute the arithmetic mean by adding all values and dividing by how many there are, and interpret it as a balance point.

skills.name: Variance and Standard Deviation
skills.description: Measure spread by averaging squared deviations from the mean (variance) and taking the square root (standard deviation).

skills.name: Estimating Means and Variances For Grouped Data
skills.description: Estimate the mean and variance from a frequency table of class intervals by treating each class as its midpoint.

skills.name: Covariance
skills.description: Measure how two paired variables vary together by averaging the products of their deviations from their means.

skills.name: Sums of Squares
skills.description: Compute sums of squared deviations such as Sxx, Syy and Sxy, the building blocks of variance, correlation and regression.

skills.name: The Z-Score
skills.description: Standardize a value as the number of standard deviations it lies above or below the mean, using z = (x − μ)/σ.

skills.name: Scatter Plots
skills.description: Plot paired numerical data as points to reveal the direction, form, strength, clusters, and outliers of a relationship.

skills.name: Trend Lines
skills.description: Draw a line of best fit through a scatter plot and write its equation to summarise a linear trend.

skills.name: Making Predictions Using Trend Lines
skills.description: Use a trend line's equation to estimate values, distinguishing reasonable interpolation from risky extrapolation.

skills.name: Linear Correlation
skills.description: Describe whether paired data follow a straight-line pattern by its direction and strength, without confusing correlation with causation.

skills.name: The Linear Correlation Coefficient
skills.description: Calculate and interpret Pearson's r, a number from −1 to 1 measuring the direction and strength of a linear relationship.

skills.name: Linear Regression
skills.description: Fit the least-squares line ŷ = a + bx to paired data and interpret its slope and intercept.

skills.name: Residuals and Residual Plots
skills.description: Compute residuals as observed minus predicted values and read residual plots to judge whether a model fits.

skills.name: Selecting a Regression Model
skills.description: Choose between linear, quadratic, exponential and other regression models using the data's shape, residual plots, and context.

skills.name: Sets
skills.description: Use set language and notation to describe collections of outcomes, the building blocks of sample spaces and events in probability.

skills.name: Experimental Probability
skills.description: Estimate a probability from repeated trials as the relative frequency of the event, and understand its limits.

skills.name: Using Experimental Probability to Make Predictions
skills.description: Estimate a probability from recorded trials and use it to predict how often an outcome will occur in future trials.

skills.name: Sample Spaces and Events in Probability
skills.description: List all possible outcomes of an experiment as a sample space and describe events as subsets of it.

skills.name: The Likelihood of an Event
skills.description: Describe how likely an event is on a 0-to-1 scale using terms such as impossible, unlikely, even chance, likely, and certain.

skills.name: Single Events in Probability
skills.description: Find the probability of one event from equally likely outcomes by dividing favourable outcomes by total outcomes.

skills.name: Using Probability to Make Predictions
skills.description: Multiply a theoretical probability by the number of trials to predict how many times an outcome should occur.

skills.name: The Complement of an Event
skills.description: Find the probability that an event does not happen using P(not A) = 1 − P(A).

skills.name: Venn Diagrams in Probability
skills.description: Represent a sample space and its events as overlapping regions to organise outcomes and read off probabilities.

skills.name: The Union of Sets
skills.description: Combine two sets into A ∪ B, containing every element in either set, to describe 'A or B' events.

skills.name: The Intersection of Sets
skills.description: Find the elements common to two sets, A ∩ B, and use it to describe outcomes where two events both occur.

skills.name: Compound Events in Probability From Experimental Data
skills.description: Estimate probabilities of combined events such as 'A and B' or 'A or B' from frequency tables of observed data.

skills.name: Computing Probabilities for Compound Events Using Venn Diagrams
skills.description: Add the appropriate Venn diagram regions to find probabilities of unions and intersections of events.

skills.name: Computing Probabilities of Events Containing Complements Using Venn Diagrams
skills.description: Use regions outside a Venn diagram circle to find probabilities involving 'not', such as P(A′) or P(A ∩ B′).

skills.name: The Rules of Sum and Product
skills.description: Count outcomes by adding options for either-or choices and multiplying options for choices made in successive stages.

skills.name: Factorials
skills.description: Compute n!, the product of the whole numbers from n down to 1, and simplify ratios of factorials.

skills.name: Factorials in Variable Expressions
skills.description: Simplify and solve expressions and equations containing factorials of unknowns, such as n!/(n − 2)! = 30.

skills.name: Ordering Objects
skills.description: Count arrangements of objects in a line, including cases with identical objects or items that must stay together.

skills.name: Permutations
skills.description: Count ordered arrangements of r objects chosen from n using P(n, r) = n!/(n − r)!.

skills.name: Combinations
skills.description: Count unordered selections of r objects from n using C(n, r) = n! / (r!(n − r)!).

skills.name: Computing Probabilities Using Combinatorics
skills.description: Compute equally likely probabilities as favorable over total outcomes, using combinations or permutations to count both.

skills.name: Pascal's Triangle and the Binomial Coefficients
skills.description: Build Pascal's triangle by adding adjacent entries and read its rows as the binomial coefficients C(n, k).

skills.name: Expanding a Binomial Using Binomial Coefficients
skills.description: Expand (a + b)^n using binomial coefficients C(n, k) and find specific terms without expanding fully.

skills.name: The Special Case of the Binomial Theorem
skills.description: Expand (1 + x)^n with the simplified binomial formula, and reduce general binomials to this form.

skills.name: Approximating Values Using the Binomial Theorem
skills.description: Estimate powers such as 1.02^5 or 0.99^10 by keeping only the first few terms of a binomial expansion.

skills.name: Expressing an Arithmetic Series in Sigma Notation
skills.description: Rewrite an arithmetic series written out term by term as a compact sum using sigma notation and limits.

skills.name: Finding the Sum of an Arithmetic Series
skills.description: Add the terms of an arithmetic series with Sn = n(a1 + an)/2 or its equivalent form using the common difference.

skills.name: Finding the First Term of an Arithmetic Series
skills.description: Work backward from a known sum, number of terms and difference or last term to find an arithmetic series' first term.

skills.name: Calculating the Number of Terms in an Arithmetic Series
skills.description: Count how many terms an arithmetic series has, from its first term, last term and difference, or from its sum.

skills.name: The Sum of a Finite Geometric Series
skills.description: Derive and use the formula Sn = a(1 − r^n)/(1 − r) for adding the terms of a finite geometric series.

skills.name: The Sum of the First N Terms of a Geometric Series
skills.description: Apply the partial-sum formula Sn to find geometric sums, missing values, or how many terms reach a target total.

skills.name: Writing Geometric Series in Sigma Notation
skills.description: Express a geometric sum compactly in sigma notation by identifying its first term, common ratio, and number of terms.

skills.name: Sums of Finite Geometric Series Given in Sigma Notation
skills.description: Evaluate a finite geometric sum given in sigma notation by identifying its first term, ratio and number of terms.

skills.name: Convergence of Geometric Sequences
skills.description: Decide whether a geometric sequence approaches a limit by examining the size and sign of its common ratio.

skills.name: Further Convergence of Geometric Sequences
skills.description: Find limits of sequences built from geometric terms and determine the values of a variable that make them converge.

skills.name: Infinite Series and Partial Sums
skills.description: Form the sequence of partial sums of an infinite series and use its limit to define the series' value.

skills.name: Convergent and Divergent Infinite Series
skills.description: Classify an infinite series as convergent or divergent from the behaviour of its partial sums and terms.

skills.name: Properties of Infinite Series
skills.description: Combine convergent infinite series term by term, using sum and constant-multiple rules to find new sums.

skills.name: Further Properties of Infinite Series
skills.description: Apply further series facts: dropping finitely many terms, reindexing, and combining convergent with divergent series.

skills.name: Finding the Sum of an Infinite Geometric Series
skills.description: Compute the sum of a convergent infinite geometric series with S = a/(1 − r), valid only when |r| < 1.

skills.name: Writing an Infinite Geometric Series in Sigma Notation
skills.description: Write an infinite geometric series in sigma notation by finding its first term and common ratio.

skills.name: Sums of Infinite Geometric Series Given in Sigma Notation
skills.description: Evaluate infinite geometric series written in sigma notation, checking convergence and reading the first term correctly.

skills.name: Convergence of Geometric Series
skills.description: Determine when an infinite geometric series has a finite sum, using the condition |r| < 1.

skills.name: Solving Elementary Quadratic Inequalities
skills.description: Solve simple quadratic inequalities such as x² < 9 or x² ≥ 5, avoiding the mistake of taking only one square root.

skills.name: Solving Quadratic Inequalities From Graphs
skills.description: Read the solution of a quadratic inequality directly from a given graph of a parabola.

skills.name: Solving Quadratic Inequalities Using the Graphical Method
skills.description: Solve a quadratic inequality by finding its roots, sketching the parabola, and choosing the part above or below the axis.

skills.name: Solving Quadratic Inequalities Using the Sign Table Method
skills.description: Solve a quadratic inequality by factoring it and tracking the sign of each linear factor across the intervals set by the roots.

skills.name: Solving Inequalities Involving Positive and Negative Factors
skills.description: Solve product inequalities by reasoning about when factors share or differ in sign, including factors that are always positive.

skills.name: Inequalities Involving Powers of Binomials
skills.description: Solve inequalities containing powers such as (x − a)ⁿ, using how even and odd powers affect the sign.

skills.name: Solving Polynomial Inequalities Using a Graphical Method
skills.description: Solve polynomial inequalities by sketching the graph from its roots, multiplicities and end behaviour, then reading where it lies above or below the axis.

skills.name: Solving Polynomial Inequalities Using the Sign Table Method
skills.description: Solve polynomial inequalities by factoring completely and recording each factor's sign on every interval in a table.

skills.name: Solving Rational Inequalities
skills.description: Solve inequalities involving fractions with variables in the denominator using zeros, excluded values and a sign table.

skills.name: Solving Inequalities Involving Exponential Functions and Polynomials
skills.description: Solve inequalities that mix exponential and polynomial expressions, often by factoring out an always-positive exponential.

skills.name: Solving Radical Inequalities
skills.description: Solve inequalities involving square roots by combining the domain condition with a careful squaring step.

skills.name: Solving Inequalities Involving Exponential Functions
skills.description: Solve inequalities involving expressions like a^x by matching bases or taking logarithms, reversing direction when the base is below one.

skills.name: Solving Inequalities Involving Logarithmic Functions
skills.description: Solve inequalities involving logarithms by respecting the domain and the base's direction, then combining the conditions.

skills.name: Solving Inequalities Involving Geometric Sequences
skills.description: Find which terms or partial sums of a geometric sequence pass a given value, using logarithms and whole-number reasoning.

skills.name: Graphing Strict Two-Variable Linear Inequalities
skills.description: Graph linear inequalities using < or > by drawing a dashed boundary line and shading the correct half-plane.

skills.name: Graphing Non-Strict Two-Variable Linear Inequalities
skills.description: Graph linear inequalities using ≤ or ≥ by drawing a solid boundary line and shading the correct half-plane.

skills.name: Further Graphing of Two-Variable Linear Inequalities
skills.description: Graph trickier linear inequalities, including horizontal and vertical boundaries, boundaries through the origin, and forms that need rearranging.

skills.name: Systems of Linear Inequalities
skills.description: Graph several linear inequalities together and find the overlapping feasible region and its corner points.

skills.name: Solving Two-Variable Nonlinear Inequalities
skills.description: Graph inequalities in x and y with curved boundaries, such as parabolas and circles, using a boundary and test point.

skills.name: Further Solving of Two-Variable Nonlinear Inequalities
skills.description: Solve systems of nonlinear two-variable inequalities by shading overlapping regions and finding where boundary curves intersect.

skills.name: Graphing Curves Defined Parametrically
skills.description: Sketch a parametric curve by tabulating t, plotting (x(t), y(t)), and marking the direction of motion.

skills.name: Cartesian Equations of Parametric Curves
skills.description: Eliminate the parameter from x(t) and y(t) to obtain a single equation relating x and y.

skills.name: Finding Intersections of Parametric Curves and Lines
skills.description: Find where a parametric curve meets a line by substituting x(t) and y(t) into the line's equation and solving for t.

skills.name: Differentiating Parametric Curves
skills.description: Compute dy/dx for a curve defined by x(t) and y(t) and use it to locate horizontal and vertical tangents.

skills.name: Calculating Tangent and Normal Lines with Parametric Equations
skills.description: Find equations of tangent and normal lines to a parametric curve at a given parameter value using dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt).

skills.name: Second Derivatives of Parametric Equations
skills.description: Find d²y/dx² for a parametric curve by differentiating dy/dx with respect to t and dividing by dx/dt.

skills.name: The Arc Length of a Parametric Curve
skills.description: Compute the length of a parametric curve with L = ∫ √((dx/dt)² + (dy/dt)²) dt over the parameter interval.

skills.name: Introduction to Polar Coordinates
skills.description: Describe points by a distance r from the origin and an angle θ from the positive x-axis, and relate them to Cartesian coordinates.

skills.name: Converting from Polar Coordinates to Cartesian Coordinates
skills.description: Convert polar points and equations to Cartesian form using x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ.

skills.name: Polar Equations of Circles Centered at the Origin
skills.description: Recognize that r = a describes a circle of radius |a| centred at the origin, with Cartesian equation x² + y² = a².

skills.name: Polar Equations of Radial Lines
skills.description: Recognize that θ = α describes a straight line through the origin at angle α, or a ray when r is restricted to r ≥ 0.

skills.name: Differentiating Curves Given in Polar Form
skills.description: Find the slope dy/dx of a polar curve r = f(θ) by treating it as a parametric curve in θ.

skills.name: Further Differentiation of Curves Given in Polar Form
skills.description: Use polar derivatives to locate horizontal and vertical tangents, tangent lines at the pole, and tangent line equations.

skills.name: Finding the Area of a Polar Region
skills.description: Compute the area swept out by a polar curve between two angles using A = ½∫ r² dθ.

skills.name: The Arc Length of a Polar Curve
skills.description: Compute the length of a polar curve r = f(θ) using L = ∫ √(r² + (dr/dθ)²) dθ.

skills.name: Circles in the Coordinate Plane
skills.description: Describe a circle as all points a fixed distance from a center and use the distance formula to work with it on a grid.

skills.name: Equations of Circles Centered at the Origin
skills.description: Use x² + y² = r² to describe, graph and test points on a circle whose center is the origin.

skills.name: Equations of Circles
skills.description: Write and interpret the standard equation (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r² for a circle with any center.

skills.name: Determining Circle Properties by Completing the Square
skills.description: Convert a circle from general form x² + y² + Dx + Ey + F = 0 to standard form to find its center and radius.

skills.name: Calculating Circle Intercepts
skills.description: Find where a circle crosses the x- and y-axes by setting one coordinate to zero and solving.

skills.name: Intersections of Circles with Lines
skills.description: Find the points where a line meets a circle by substitution, and tell whether it is a secant, a tangent or a miss.

skills.name: Parametric Equations of Circles
skills.description: Describe a circle with x = h + r cos t, y = k + r sin t and relate the parameter t to position and direction.

skills.name: Upward and Downward Opening Parabolas
skills.description: Tell from its equation whether a parabola opens up or down and how wide it is, including focus-directrix form x² = 4py.

skills.name: Left and Right Opening Parabolas
skills.description: Recognise and graph parabolas that open sideways, written as x = a(y − k)² + h or y² = 4px.

skills.name: The Vertex of a Parabola
skills.description: Find a parabola's vertex, its turning point and maximum or minimum, using vertex form or x = −b/(2a).

skills.name: Calculating the Vertex of a Parabola by Completing the Square
skills.description: Rewrite y = ax² + bx + c in vertex form a(x − h)² + k by completing the square, then read off the vertex (h, k).

skills.name: Calculating Intercepts of Parabolas
skills.description: Find the axis intercepts of a parabola, solving a quadratic for the intercepts that cross its axis of opening.

skills.name: Parametric Equations of Parabolas
skills.description: Write a parabola as a pair of parametric equations, such as x = t, y = t² or x = pt², y = 2pt.

skills.name: Parametric Equations of Parabolas Centered at (h,k)
skills.description: Parametrise a parabola whose vertex is at (h, k), for either an up-down or a sideways opening.

skills.name: Introduction to Ellipses
skills.description: Understand an ellipse as the points whose distances to two foci sum to a constant, and name its axes, vertices and foci.

skills.name: Equations of Ellipses Centered at the Origin
skills.description: Read the axes, intercepts and foci of an ellipse from x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 when its center is the origin.

skills.name: Equations of Ellipses Centered at a General Point
skills.description: Use (x − h)²/a² + (y − k)²/b² = 1 to find the center, vertices, co-vertices and foci of a shifted ellipse.

skills.name: Finding the Center and Axes of Ellipses by Completing the Square
skills.description: Complete the square in x and y to turn an expanded ellipse equation into standard form and read its center and axes.

skills.name: Finding Intercepts of Ellipses
skills.description: Find where an ellipse crosses the coordinate axes, including shifted ellipses whose intercepts are not its vertices.

skills.name: Parametric Equations of Ellipses
skills.description: Trace an ellipse with x = h + a cos t, y = k + b sin t and convert between parametric and standard forms.

skills.name: Equations of Hyperbolas Centered at the Origin
skills.description: Use x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 or y²/a² − x²/b² = 1 to find the vertices and foci of an origin-centered hyperbola.

skills.name: Equations of Hyperbolas Centered at a General Point
skills.description: Interpret the standard equation of a hyperbola centered at (h, k) to find its orientation, vertices and foci.

skills.name: Asymptotes of Hyperbolas Centered at the Origin
skills.description: Find the asymptotes y = ±(b/a)x or y = ±(a/b)x of a hyperbola whose center is the origin.

skills.name: Asymptotes of Hyperbolas Centered at a General Point
skills.description: Write the two asymptote lines of a shifted hyperbola, which pass through its center (h, k) with slopes set by a and b.

skills.name: Finding Intercepts and Intersections of Hyperbolas
skills.description: Find where a hyperbola meets the axes, a line or another conic by substitution or elimination.

skills.name: Parametric Equations of Horizontal Hyperbolas
skills.description: Parametrise a left-right opening hyperbola with x = h + a sec t, y = k + b tan t, and track which branch each t covers.

skills.name: Parametric Equations of Vertical Hyperbolas
skills.description: Parametrise an up-down opening hyperbola using secant for y and tangent for x, and identify each branch.

skills.name: Graphing the Inverse Sine Function
skills.description: Sketch y = arcsin(x) by restricting sine to [−π/2, π/2] and reflecting that piece in the line y = x.

skills.name: Graphing the Inverse Cosine Function
skills.description: Sketch y = arccos(x) by restricting cosine to [0, π] and reflecting its graph in the line y = x.

skills.name: Graphing the Inverse Tangent Function
skills.description: Sketch y = arctan(x), an increasing curve defined for all real x with horizontal asymptotes at y = ±π/2.

skills.name: Evaluating Expressions Containing Inverse Trigonometric Functions
skills.description: Evaluate expressions like arcsin(√3/2), cos(arctan(3/4)), or arcsin(sin 5π/6) using principal ranges and reference triangles.

skills.name: Limits of Inverse Trigonometric Functions
skills.description: Evaluate limits involving arcsin, arccos and arctan using their continuity, endpoints and horizontal asymptotes.

skills.name: Elementary Trigonometric Equations Containing Sine
skills.description: Solve equations such as 2 sin x = 1 by isolating sin x and finding all solutions within a specified interval.

skills.name: Elementary Trigonometric Equations Containing Cosine
skills.description: Solve equations such as 2 cos x − 1 = 0 by isolating cos x and finding all angles in the given interval.

skills.name: Elementary Trigonometric Equations Containing Tangent
skills.description: Solve tangent equations like tan x = −1, using the period π to find every solution in an interval.

skills.name: Elementary Trigonometric Equations Containing Secant
skills.description: Solve equations like sec x = −2 by rewriting them in terms of cosine and locating every solution in the interval.

skills.name: Elementary Trigonometric Equations Containing Cosecant
skills.description: Solve equations like csc x = 2 by converting to sine, checking that solutions exist, and listing every angle in the interval.

skills.name: Elementary Trigonometric Equations Containing Cotangent
skills.description: Solve cotangent equations by converting to tangent or using unit-circle values, remembering that cotangent repeats every π.

skills.name: Solving Trigonometric Equations Using the Sin-Cos-Tan Identity
skills.description: Solve equations mixing sine and cosine, such as sin x = √3 cos x, by rewriting them as a tangent equation.

skills.name: General Solutions of Elementary Trigonometric Equations
skills.description: Express every solution of a basic trigonometric equation using an integer parameter, such as x = π/6 + 2nπ.

skills.name: General Solutions of Trigonometric Equations With Transformed Functions
skills.description: Find all solutions of equations like 2 sin(3x) = 1 by solving for the inner angle first, then undoing the transformation.

skills.name: Trigonometric Equations Containing Transformed Tangent Functions
skills.description: Solve equations such as tan(2x) = 1 or 3 tan(x − π/6) = √3, using the transformed period to list all solutions.

skills.name: Simplifying Expressions Using Basic Trigonometric Identities
skills.description: Rewrite trigonometric expressions with reciprocal and quotient identities, such as tan x = sin x / cos x, to reach simpler equivalent forms.

skills.name: Simplifying Expressions Using the Pythagorean Identity
skills.description: Use sin²x + cos²x = 1 and its rearrangements to simplify trigonometric expressions.

skills.name: Alternate Forms of the Pythagorean Identity
skills.description: Rearrange sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 into forms such as sin²θ = 1 − cos²θ to simplify trigonometric expressions.

skills.name: Simplifying Expressions Using the Secant-Tangent Identity
skills.description: Simplify expressions using the identity 1 + tan²x = sec²x, derived from the Pythagorean identity.

skills.name: Alternate Forms of the Secant-Tangent Identity
skills.description: Use 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ and its rearrangements, such as sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, to simplify and evaluate expressions.

skills.name: Simplifying Trigonometric Expressions Using the Cotangent-Cosecant Identity
skills.description: Simplify expressions using 1 + cot²x = csc²x, the Pythagorean identity divided through by sin²x.

skills.name: The Sum and Difference Formulas for Sine
skills.description: Expand sin(A ± B) as sin A cos B ± cos A sin B to compute exact values and rewrite trigonometric expressions.

skills.name: The Sum and Difference Formulas for Cosine
skills.description: Expand cos(A ± B) as cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B to find exact values and simplify expressions.

skills.name: Writing Sums of Trigonometric Functions in Amplitude-Phase Form
skills.description: Rewrite a sum a sin x + b cos x as a single sinusoid R sin(x + α), revealing its amplitude and phase.

skills.name: The Double-Angle Formula for Sine
skills.description: Apply sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x to evaluate, simplify, or solve trigonometric expressions involving doubled angles.

skills.name: The Double-Angle Formula for Cosine
skills.description: Use cos 2x = cos²x − sin²x and its equivalent forms 2cos²x − 1 and 1 − 2sin²x to evaluate and simplify.

skills.name: The Complex Conjugate
skills.description: Form the conjugate of a complex number by changing the sign of its imaginary part, and use it in basic calculations.

skills.name: Special Properties of the Complex Conjugate
skills.description: Use the rules that conjugation obeys, such as the conjugate of a product and z·z̄ = |z|², to simplify and prove results.

skills.name: The Complex Conjugate and the Roots of a Quadratic Equation
skills.description: Recognize that nonreal roots of a real quadratic form a conjugate pair, and build a quadratic from one complex root.

skills.name: Dividing Complex Numbers
skills.description: Divide complex numbers by multiplying numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator.

skills.name: Solving Equations by Equating Real and Imaginary Parts
skills.description: Solve a complex equation for real unknowns by setting real parts equal and imaginary parts equal.

skills.name: Extending Polynomial Identities to the Complex Numbers
skills.description: Apply familiar polynomial identities over the complex numbers, such as factoring a sum of squares as (x + yi)(x − yi).

skills.name: The Polar Form of a Complex Number
skills.description: Convert a complex number between rectangular form a + bi and polar form r(cos θ + i sin θ).

skills.name: De Moivre's Theorem
skills.description: Raise a complex number in polar form to a power by powering its modulus and multiplying its argument, and reverse this to find roots.

skills.name: Euler's Formula
skills.description: Use e^(iθ) = cos θ + i sin θ to write complex numbers in exponential form and simplify products and powers.

skills.name: The Roots of Unity
skills.description: Find all n complex solutions of z^n = 1 using polar form and list them as equally spaced points on the unit circle.

skills.name: Properties of Roots of Unity
skills.description: Use the structural facts about nth roots of unity: equal spacing on the unit circle, cyclic powers, closure, and a zero sum.

skills.name: The Fundamental Theorem of Algebra for Quadratic Equations
skills.description: Understand that every quadratic has exactly two complex roots counted with multiplicity, and classify them with the discriminant.

skills.name: The Fundamental Theorem of Algebra with Cubic Equations
skills.description: Apply the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra to cubics: three roots with multiplicity, at least one real when coefficients are real.

skills.name: Solving Cubic Equations With Complex Roots
skills.description: Find all three roots of a cubic, including nonreal ones, by dividing out a known root and solving the quadratic left over.

skills.name: The Fundamental Theorem of Algebra with Quartic Equations
skills.description: Apply the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra to quartics and list the possible combinations of real and nonreal roots.

skills.name: Solving Quartic Equations With Complex Roots
skills.description: Find all four roots of a quartic, including complex pairs, by substitution, factoring into quadratics, or dividing out known roots.

skills.name: L'Hopital's Rule
skills.description: Evaluate limits of the indeterminate forms 0/0 or ∞/∞ by taking the limit of the ratio of derivatives instead.

skills.name: Limits of Sequences
skills.description: Determine whether a sequence aₙ converges to a finite limit as n → ∞ or diverges, and find the limit when it exists.

skills.name: Special Limits Involving Sine
skills.description: Use the special limit sin(x)/x → 1 as x → 0, and related forms, to evaluate trigonometric limits that give 0/0.

skills.name: Limits Involving the Exponential Function
skills.description: Evaluate limits built from eˣ, including the definition of e as a limit and forms like (1 + k/x)ˣ and (eˣ − 1)/x.

skills.name: Limits at Infinity and Horizontal Asymptotes of Rational Functions
skills.description: Find a rational function's limit as x → ±∞ by comparing numerator and denominator degrees, giving its horizontal asymptote.

skills.name: Calculating Limits of Radical Functions Using Conjugate Multiplication
skills.description: Resolve 0/0 limits involving square roots by multiplying numerator and denominator by the conjugate to expose a cancelling factor.

skills.name: Evaluating Limits at Infinity by Comparing Relative Magnitudes of Functions
skills.description: Evaluate limits at infinity of quotients by comparing the growth rates of logarithmic, power, and exponential functions.

skills.name: Determining Limits of Sequences Using Relative Magnitudes
skills.description: Find the limit of a sequence by recognising which terms dominate as n grows, using the standard ordering of growth rates.

skills.name: Continuity of Functions
skills.description: Decide whether a function is continuous, meaning its limit equals its value at each point, and classify any discontinuities.

skills.name: The Intermediate Value Theorem
skills.description: Use the Intermediate Value Theorem to show that a continuous function on [a, b] takes every value between f(a) and f(b).

skills.name: Calculating Slopes of Circles, Ellipses, and Parabolas
skills.description: Find the slope of the tangent line at a point on a circle, ellipse, or parabola using implicit differentiation.

skills.name: Calculating dy/dx Using dx/dy
skills.description: Find dy/dx as the reciprocal of dx/dy when x is given as a function of y.

skills.name: Differentiating Inverse Functions
skills.description: Derive and apply the general rule (f⁻¹)'(x) = 1/f'(f⁻¹(x)) for the derivative of an inverse function.

skills.name: Differentiating an Inverse Function at a Point
skills.description: Find the slope of an inverse function at a specific value using (f⁻¹)'(b) = 1/f'(a), where f(a) = b.

skills.name: Differentiating Inverse Trigonometric Functions
skills.description: Differentiate arcsin, arccos, and arctan, and combine these formulas with the chain rule.

skills.name: Differentiating Inverse Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions
skills.description: Differentiate arcsec, arccsc, and arccot, including chain-rule versions and the range conventions they depend on.

skills.name: Integration Using Inverse Trigonometric Functions
skills.description: Evaluate integrals whose antiderivatives are arcsin, arctan, or arcsec, often after substitution or completing the square.

skills.name: Continuity and Differentiability of Functions
skills.description: Decide whether a function is continuous and differentiable at a point, knowing that differentiability implies continuity but not the reverse.

skills.name: The Mean Value Theorem
skills.description: For a function continuous on [a, b] and differentiable on (a, b), some interior point has instantaneous slope equal to the average slope.

skills.name: Global vs. Local Extrema and Critical Points
skills.description: Distinguish local from global maxima and minima, and recognize critical points as the interior candidates for extrema.

skills.name: The Extreme Value Theorem
skills.description: A continuous function on a closed, bounded interval always attains both an absolute maximum and an absolute minimum.

skills.name: Using Differentiation to Calculate Critical Points
skills.description: Differentiate a function and find where the derivative is zero or undefined within the domain to locate its critical points.

skills.name: Determining Intervals on Which a Function Is Increasing or Decreasing
skills.description: Use the sign of the first derivative to find the intervals where a function rises or falls.

skills.name: Using the First Derivative Test to Classify Local Extrema
skills.description: Classify a critical point as a local maximum, local minimum, or neither by checking how the sign of f' changes across it.

skills.name: The Candidates Test
skills.description: Find the absolute maximum and minimum of a continuous function on a closed interval by comparing values at critical points and endpoints.

skills.name: Intervals of Concavity
skills.description: Find where a graph is concave up or concave down by locating zeros of f'' and testing its sign on each interval.

skills.name: Relating Concavity to the Second Derivative
skills.description: Interpret the second derivative as the rate of change of slope and use it to explain why a graph bends up or down.

skills.name: Points of Inflection
skills.description: Locate points where a continuous graph changes concavity by finding where f'' is zero or undefined and confirming a sign change.

skills.name: The Second Derivative Test
skills.description: Classify a critical point where f'(c) = 0 as a local maximum or minimum from the sign of f''(c).

skills.name: Approximating Functions Using Local Linearity and Linearization
skills.description: Approximate a function near a point by its tangent line, L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x − a).

skills.name: Estimating Derivatives Using a Forward Difference Quotient
skills.description: Estimate a derivative from the current point and the next sample: [f(x + h) − f(x)]/h.

skills.name: Estimating Derivatives Using a Backward Difference Quotient
skills.description: Estimate a derivative from the current point and the previous sample: [f(x) − f(x − h)]/h.

skills.name: Estimating Derivatives Using a Central Difference Quotient
skills.description: Estimate a derivative from samples on both sides, [f(x + h) − f(x − h)]/(2h), usually more accurately than one-sided quotients.

skills.name: Second-Degree Taylor Polynomials
skills.description: Build the quadratic approximation f(a) + f'(a)(x − a) + f''(a)(x − a)²/2, matching a function's value, slope, and concavity at a point.

skills.name: Analyzing Second-Degree Taylor Polynomials
skills.description: Read a function's value, slope, concavity, and error bounds from its second-degree Taylor polynomial.

skills.name: Third-Degree Taylor Polynomials
skills.description: Add the cubic term f'''(a)(x − a)³/6 to a quadratic approximation to capture how curvature changes near the center.

skills.name: Higher-Degree Taylor Polynomials
skills.description: Build Taylor polynomials of degree n and use the remainder estimate to choose a degree that meets an accuracy target.

skills.name: Maclaurin Series
skills.description: Represent a function as a power series centred at x = 0, with coefficients built from its derivatives there.

skills.name: Taylor Series
skills.description: Extend Taylor polynomials to an infinite series and determine where that series converges to the function.

skills.name: Representing Functions as Power Series
skills.description: Write functions as power series by adapting known series such as the geometric series, and state where they converge.

skills.name: Recognizing Standard Maclaurin Series
skills.description: Know the common Maclaurin expansions by sight and adapt them by substitution instead of re-deriving each one.

skills.name: Approximating Areas With the Left Riemann Sum
skills.description: Estimate the area under a curve by adding rectangles whose heights come from the left endpoint of each subinterval.

skills.name: Approximating Areas With the Right Riemann Sum
skills.description: Estimate the area under a curve by adding rectangles whose heights come from the right endpoint of each subinterval.

skills.name: Left and Right Riemann Sums in Sigma Notation
skills.description: Write left and right Riemann sums compactly with sigma notation using a general subinterval width and sample points.

skills.name: Approximating Areas With the Trapezoidal Rule
skills.description: Estimate a definite integral by replacing the curve on each subinterval with a straight segment and summing trapezoid areas.

skills.name: Defining Definite Integrals Using Left and Right Riemann Sums
skills.description: Define the definite integral as the limit of left or right Riemann sums as the number of subintervals grows without bound.

skills.name: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
skills.description: Link differentiation and integration: accumulation functions differentiate back to the integrand, and definite integrals are evaluated with antiderivatives.

skills.name: Applying the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus to Exponential and Trigonometric Functions
skills.description: Evaluate definite integrals of exponential and trigonometric functions by finding antiderivatives and applying the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.

skills.name: The Sum and Constant Multiple Rules for Definite Integrals
skills.description: Split definite integrals of sums and pull constant factors outside the integral to simplify evaluation.

skills.name: Properties of Definite Integrals Involving the Limits of Integration
skills.description: Use rules about the limits of integration, including zero-width intervals, reversed limits, and splitting an interval, to evaluate integrals.

skills.name: The Area Bounded by a Curve and the X-Axis
skills.description: Compute the area of a region between a curve and the x-axis over an interval using a definite integral.

skills.name: The Area Bounded by a Curve and the Y-Axis
skills.description: Find the area between a curve and the y-axis by writing x as a function of y and integrating with respect to y.

skills.name: Evaluating Definite Integrals Using Symmetry
skills.description: Simplify definite integrals over intervals symmetric about zero by recognizing even and odd integrands.

skills.name: Finding the Area Between a Curve and the X-Axis When They Intersect
skills.description: Find the total area between a curve and the x-axis when the curve crosses the axis by splitting at its zeros.

skills.name: Calculating the Definite Integral of a Function Given Its Graph
skills.description: Evaluate a definite integral from a graph by adding areas of geometric shapes, counting regions below the axis as negative.

skills.name: Definite Integrals of Piecewise Functions
skills.description: Integrate a function defined by different formulas on different intervals by splitting the integral at each breakpoint.

skills.name: The Integral as an Accumulation Function
skills.description: Treat an integral with a variable upper limit as a function that tracks accumulated quantity as the limit changes.

skills.name: The Second Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
skills.description: Differentiate an integral with a variable limit: the derivative equals the integrand at that limit, times the limit's derivative.

skills.name: The Average Value of a Function
skills.description: Find the average height of a continuous function over an interval by dividing its definite integral by the interval's length.

skills.name: The Area Between Curves Expressed as Functions of X
skills.description: Find the area between two curves y = f(x) and y = g(x) by integrating the top function minus the bottom function.

skills.name: The Arc Length of a Planar Curve
skills.description: Find the length of a curve between two points by integrating the square root of one plus the derivative squared.

skills.name: Integrating Algebraic Functions Using Substitution
skills.description: Integrate algebraic expressions by substituting for an inner expression whose derivative appears as a factor.

skills.name: Integrating Linear Rational Functions Using Substitution
skills.description: Integrate fractions whose denominator is a linear expression ax + b by substituting u = ax + b.

skills.name: Integration Using Substitution
skills.description: Use u-substitution, the reverse of the chain rule, to turn a composite integrand into a simpler integral in a new variable.

skills.name: Calculating Definite Integrals Using Substitution
skills.description: Evaluate definite integrals by substitution, converting the limits to the new variable or returning to the original before evaluating.

skills.name: Further Integration of Algebraic Functions Using Substitution
skills.description: Use substitution on algebraic integrals where the leftover x must be rewritten in terms of the new variable.

skills.name: Integrating Exponential Functions Using Linear Substitution
skills.description: Integrate exponentials with a linear exponent, such as e^(ax + b), by substituting u = ax + b and dividing by a.

skills.name: Integrating Exponential Functions Using Substitution
skills.description: Integrate expressions containing e raised to a function of x by substituting for the exponent.

skills.name: Integrating Trigonometric Functions Using Substitution
skills.description: Use u-substitution on integrals involving sine, cosine and other trig functions of an inner expression or with a matching derivative factor.

skills.name: Integrating Logarithmic Functions Using Substitution
skills.description: Use substitution for integrands involving ln x or of the form f'(x)/f(x), producing logarithmic or power results.

skills.name: Integration by Substitution With Inverse Trigonometric Functions
skills.description: Recognize integrals that produce arcsin or arctan and use substitution to fit them to those standard forms.

skills.name: Integration Using Basic Trigonometric Identities
skills.description: Rewrite trig integrands with reciprocal and quotient identities so they match antiderivatives you already know.

skills.name: Integration Using the Pythagorean Identities
skills.description: Apply sin² x + cos² x = 1 and its variants to rewrite trig powers into integrable forms.

skills.name: Integration Using the Double-Angle Formulas
skills.description: Use double-angle identities to lower powers such as sin² x and cos² x, or to simplify sin x cos x, before integrating.

skills.name: Integrating Functions Using Polynomial Division
skills.description: Divide polynomials first when a rational integrand's numerator degree is at least the denominator's, then integrate the pieces.

skills.name: Integrating Functions by Completing the Square
skills.description: Rewrite a quadratic under a fraction or root as a shifted square so a standard integral such as arctan applies.

skills.name: Introduction to Integration by Parts
skills.description: Integrate products of functions with ∫ u dv = uv − ∫ v du, derived from the product rule.

skills.name: Using Integration by Parts to Calculate Integrals With Logarithms
skills.description: Integrate ln x and products involving logarithms by choosing u = ln x in integration by parts.

skills.name: Applying the Integration By Parts Twice
skills.description: Apply integration by parts a second time when the first application leaves an integral that still needs the same technique.

skills.name: Integration by Parts in Cyclic Cases
skills.description: Apply integration by parts twice until the original integral reappears, then solve for it algebraically.

skills.name: Expressing Rational Functions with Repeated Factors as Sums of Partial Fractions
skills.description: Decompose rational functions with repeated linear factors, giving one partial fraction for each power of the repeated factor.

skills.name: Expressing Rational Functions with Irreducible Quadratic Factors as Sums of Partial Fractions
skills.description: Decompose rational functions whose denominators contain irreducible quadratic factors, using linear numerators over those factors.

skills.name: Integrating Rational Functions Using Partial Fractions
skills.description: Split a proper rational function into simpler fractions over its linear denominator factors and integrate each one.

skills.name: Integrating Rational Functions with Repeated Factors
skills.description: Integrate rational functions with a repeated linear factor, using one partial fraction per power and integrating each to a logarithm or a power.

skills.name: Integrating Rational Functions with Irreducible Quadratic Factors
skills.description: Integrate rational functions whose denominators contain quadratics with no real roots, using partial fractions with linear numerators and log or arctan results.

skills.name: Improper Integrals Involving Exponential Functions
skills.description: Evaluate integrals of exponential functions over infinite intervals by taking limits, checking whether the exponential decays.

skills.name: Improper Integrals Involving Arctangent
skills.description: Evaluate improper integrals whose antiderivative is an arctangent, using its limits of ±π/2 at infinity.

skills.name: Improper Integrals Over the Real Line
skills.description: Evaluate integrals from −∞ to ∞ by splitting at a point and requiring both one-sided improper integrals to converge.

skills.name: Improper Integrals of the Second Kind
skills.description: Evaluate integrals whose integrand becomes unbounded at an endpoint or interior point, by replacing that point with a limit.

skills.name: Calculating Velocity for Straight-Line Motion Using Differentiation
skills.description: Find instantaneous velocity on a line as the derivative of position, and read direction and rest from its sign.

skills.name: Calculating Acceleration for Straight-Line Motion Using Differentiation
skills.description: Find the acceleration of an object on a line by differentiating its velocity, or its position twice.

skills.name: Determining Characteristics of Moving Objects Using Differentiation
skills.description: Use velocity and acceleration found by differentiation to decide when an object is at rest, turns around, speeds up or slows down.

skills.name: Calculating Velocity Using Integration
skills.description: Find velocity from acceleration by integrating, using an initial velocity to fix the constant of integration.

skills.name: Determining Characteristics of Moving Objects Using Integration
skills.description: Use integrals of velocity and acceleration to find an object's position, displacement, and total distance traveled along a line.

skills.name: Calculating the Position Function of a Particle Using Integration
skills.description: Recover a particle's position function by antidifferentiating its velocity and using an initial position to fix the constant.

skills.name: Calculating the Displacement of a Particle Using Integration
skills.description: Compute net change in position by integrating velocity, and separate it from total distance travelled.

skills.name: Velocity and Acceleration for Plane Motion
skills.description: Differentiate a position vector to find velocity, speed, and acceleration for an object moving in a plane.

skills.name: Calculating Displacement for Plane Motion
skills.description: Find the net change in position of an object moving in a plane by integrating each velocity component.

skills.name: Calculating Velocity for Plane Motion Using Differentiation
skills.description: Differentiate position components to get a planar velocity vector, and find speed as its magnitude.

skills.name: Calculating Acceleration for Plane Motion Using Differentiation
skills.description: Differentiate each component of a planar velocity vector to find the acceleration vector of an object moving in 2D.

skills.name: Finding Velocity Vectors in Two Dimensions Using Integration
skills.description: Recover a two-dimensional velocity vector by integrating the acceleration vector component by component and applying the initial velocity.

skills.name: Finding Displacement Vectors in Two Dimensions Using Integration
skills.description: Integrate each component of a two-dimensional velocity vector to find the net change in position over a time interval.

skills.name: Rates of Change in Applied Contexts
skills.description: Interpret derivatives as rates of change with units in real settings such as motion, economics, biology, and physics.

skills.name: Introduction to Related Rates
skills.description: Find how fast one quantity changes by differentiating an equation that links it to another quantity whose rate is known.

skills.name: Related Rates With Implicit Functions
skills.description: Solve related rates problems where the linking equation is implicit, differentiating every variable with respect to time.

skills.name: Calculating Related Rates With Circles and Spheres
skills.description: Relate the changing radius of a circle or sphere to the rate of change of its area, circumference or volume.

skills.name: Calculating Related Rates Using the Pythagorean Theorem
skills.description: Solve related-rates problems in which lengths are tied by a² + b² = c², such as sliding ladders or separating cars.

skills.name: Solving Optimization Problems Using Derivatives
skills.description: Find the largest or smallest value of a quantity in a practical problem by modeling it as a function and using derivatives.

skills.name: Optimizing Distances
skills.description: Minimize or maximize a distance, such as from a point to a line or between two moving objects, using derivatives.

skills.name: Optimizing Distances to Curves
skills.description: Find the point on a curve nearest to or farthest from a given point by minimizing the squared distance.

skills.name: Introduction to Differential Equations
skills.description: Recognize what a differential equation is, its order, and what it means for a function to be a solution.

skills.name: Verifying Solutions of Differential Equations
skills.description: Check whether a given function solves a differential equation by substituting it and its derivatives into the equation.

skills.name: Solving First-Order ODEs Using Direct Integration
skills.description: Solve a differential equation of the form dy/dx = f(x) by integrating the right-hand side directly and adding a constant.

skills.name: Solving First-Order ODEs Using Separation of Variables
