skills.description: Solve first-order equations of the form dy/dx = g(x)h(y) by moving each variable to its own side and integrating.

skills.name: Solving First-Order IVPs Using Separation of Variables
skills.description: Solve a separable first-order equation, then use the given initial condition to determine the constant and the particular solution.

skills.name: Qualitative Analysis of First-Order ODEs
skills.description: Describe how solutions of a first-order ODE behave using slope fields, equilibrium solutions, and sign analysis without solving it.

skills.name: Modeling With First-Order ODEs
skills.description: Translate a verbal description of how a quantity changes into a first-order differential equation and interpret its solution.

skills.name: Euler's Method: Calculating One Step
skills.description: Take a single Euler step, using the slope at the current point to estimate the next value of a solution.

skills.name: Euler's Method: Calculating Multiple Steps
skills.description: Repeat Euler's method step by step to approximate a solution of a differential equation over a longer interval.

skills.name: Three-Dimensional Vectors in Component Form
skills.description: Describe vectors in space by x, y, z components in a right-handed coordinate system, as (x, y, z) or xi + yj + zk.

skills.name: Addition and Scalar Multiplication of Cartesian Vectors in 3D
skills.description: Add, subtract, and scale three-dimensional vectors component by component, and interpret the results geometrically.

skills.name: Calculating the Magnitude of Cartesian Vectors in 3D
skills.description: Find the length of a three-dimensional vector as √(x² + y² + z²), and use it for distances between points.

skills.name: Calculating the Dot Product Using Angle and Magnitude
skills.description: Find a · b as |a||b| cos θ when the lengths of two vectors and the angle between them are known.

skills.name: Calculating the Dot Product Using Components
skills.description: Multiply matching components of two vectors and add the products to get their scalar dot product.

skills.name: The Angle Between Two Vectors
skills.description: Find the angle between two vectors by rearranging the dot product: cos θ = (a · b) / (|a||b|).

skills.name: Calculating a Scalar Projection
skills.description: Find the signed length of one vector along another, comp_b a = (a · b) / |b|.

skills.name: Calculating a Vector Projection
skills.description: Find the vector component of a along b, proj_b a = ((a · b) / |b|²) b, and the perpendicular remainder.

skills.name: The Cross Product of Two Vectors
skills.description: Understand a × b as a vector perpendicular to both inputs, with length |a||b| sin θ and direction given by the right-hand rule.

skills.name: Properties of the Cross Product
skills.description: Use the algebraic rules of the cross product: anticommutativity, distributivity, scalar factoring, and zero for parallel vectors.

skills.name: Calculating the Cross Product Using Determinants
skills.description: Compute a × b by expanding a 3 × 3 determinant with i, j, k in the top row.

skills.name: Finding Areas Using the Cross Product
skills.description: Use |a × b| to find the area of a parallelogram or triangle spanned by two vectors in space.

skills.name: The Scalar Triple Product
skills.description: Compute a · (b × c), a single number that measures signed volume and tests whether three vectors are coplanar.

skills.name: Volumes of Parallelepipeds
skills.description: Find the volume of a parallelepiped spanned by three edge vectors as |a · (b × c)|.

skills.name: Defining Vector-Valued Functions
skills.description: Describe a curve with a function r(t) whose output is a vector, each component being a function of one parameter t.

skills.name: Differentiating Vector-Valued Functions
skills.description: Differentiate a vector-valued function component by component to find tangent vectors and velocity.

skills.name: Integrating Vector-Valued Functions
skills.description: Integrate a vector-valued function component by component, using a constant vector or an initial condition.

skills.name: Introduction to Matrices
skills.description: Recognize a matrix as a rectangular array of numbers, state its order as rows by columns, and read its entries.

skills.name: Index Notation for Matrices
skills.description: Use subscripts such as aij to name individual matrix entries by row and column, and describe matrices by formulas.

skills.name: Adding and Subtracting Matrices
skills.description: Add or subtract two matrices of the same size by combining their corresponding entries.

skills.name: Properties of Matrix Addition
skills.description: Apply the commutative, associative, zero, and inverse properties of matrix addition to simplify matrix expressions.

skills.name: Scalar Multiplication of Matrices
skills.description: Multiply every entry of a matrix by a single number, and use the rules that scalar multiplication follows.

skills.name: Zero, Square, Diagonal and Identity Matrices
skills.description: Identify zero, square, diagonal, and identity matrices and use their special behaviour in matrix calculations.

skills.name: The Transpose of a Matrix
skills.description: Form the transpose of a matrix by turning its rows into columns, and use the transpose's key properties.

skills.name: Multiplying a Matrix by a Column Vector
skills.description: Multiply an m×n matrix by a column vector with n entries to get a new column vector with m entries.

skills.name: Multiplying Square Matrices
skills.description: Multiply two n×n matrices, noting that both orders are defined but AB and BA usually differ.

skills.name: Conformability for Matrix Multiplication
skills.description: Check whether two matrices can be multiplied by comparing inner dimensions, and predict the size of the product.

skills.name: Multiplying Matrices
skills.description: Multiply two matrices by taking row-by-column dot products, after checking that the inner dimensions agree.

skills.name: Powers of Matrices
skills.description: Compute A², A³ and higher powers of a square matrix by repeated matrix multiplication.

skills.name: Multiplying a Matrix by the Identity Matrix
skills.description: Recognize that multiplying by an identity matrix of the right size leaves any matrix or vector unchanged.

skills.name: Properties of Matrix Multiplication
skills.description: Use the associative, distributive and identity laws of matrix multiplication while remembering that it is not commutative.

skills.name: Representing 2x2 Systems of Equations Using a Matrix Product
skills.description: Rewrite a pair of linear equations in two unknowns as a single matrix equation Ax = b.

skills.name: Representing 3x3 Systems of Equations Using a Matrix Product
skills.description: Express three linear equations in three unknowns as a 3×3 coefficient matrix times a variable vector equal to a constant vector.

skills.name: The Determinant of a 2x2 Matrix
skills.description: Compute ad − bc for a 2×2 matrix and use it to decide whether the matrix is invertible.

skills.name: The Geometric Interpretation of the 2x2 Determinant
skills.description: Interpret the 2×2 determinant as the signed factor by which a linear transformation scales areas.

skills.name: The Minors of a 3x3 Matrix
skills.description: Find the minor of each entry in a 3×3 matrix by deleting its row and column and taking the remaining 2×2 determinant.

skills.name: The Determinant of a 3x3 Matrix
skills.description: Evaluate a 3×3 determinant by cofactor expansion along a row or column, using the + − + sign pattern.

skills.name: Introduction to the Inverse of a Matrix
skills.description: Understand the inverse of a square matrix as the matrix that undoes it, so that AA⁻¹ = A⁻¹A = I.

skills.name: Inverses of 2x2 Matrices
skills.description: Invert a 2×2 matrix by swapping the diagonal entries, negating the off-diagonal entries, and dividing by the determinant.

skills.name: Calculating the Inverse of a 3x3 Matrix Using the Cofactor Method
skills.description: Find the inverse of a 3×3 matrix by dividing its adjugate, the transposed cofactor matrix, by the determinant.

skills.name: Solving 2x2 Systems of Equations Using Inverse Matrices
skills.description: Solve two linear equations in two unknowns by writing them as Ax = b and computing x = A⁻¹b.

skills.name: Solving Systems of Equations Using Inverse Matrices
skills.description: Solve square linear systems of any size, typically 3×3, by computing x = A⁻¹b when the coefficient matrix is invertible.

skills.name: Introduction to Linear Transformations
skills.description: Decide whether a transformation of the plane is linear and write a linear transformation as a 2×2 matrix.

skills.name: The Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation
skills.description: Build the matrix of a linear transformation by using the images of the standard basis vectors as its columns.

skills.name: Linear Transformations of Points and Lines in the Plane
skills.description: Find the images of points and straight lines under a 2×2 transformation matrix, including the equation of an image line.

skills.name: Linear Transformations of Objects in the Plane
skills.description: Transform polygons and other shapes in the plane by mapping their vertices with a 2×2 matrix.

skills.name: Dilations and Reflections as Linear Transformations
skills.description: Write and apply 2×2 matrices for dilations about the origin and for reflections in lines through the origin.

skills.name: Shear and Stretch as Linear Transformations
skills.description: Describe stretches along an axis and shears parallel to an axis with 2×2 matrices, and predict their effect on shapes.

skills.name: Right-Angle Rotations as Linear Transformations
skills.description: Represent rotations of 90°, 180° and 270° about the origin with matrices whose entries are 0, 1 and −1.

skills.name: Rotations as Linear Transformations
skills.description: Rotate points about the origin through any angle θ using the matrix with rows (cos θ, −sin θ) and (sin θ, cos θ).

skills.name: Combining Linear Transformations Using 2x2 Matrices
skills.description: Find the single 2×2 matrix for a sequence of transformations by multiplying their matrices in the correct order.

skills.name: Inverting Linear Transformations
skills.description: Undo a linear transformation with the inverse of its matrix, recovering original points from their images.

skills.name: Area Scale Factors of Linear Transformations
skills.description: Use the determinant of a 2×2 transformation matrix to find how much it scales areas and whether it flips orientation.

skills.name: Singular Linear Transformations in the Plane
skills.description: Recognize a plane transformation with zero determinant, which collapses the plane onto a line or a point and cannot be undone.

skills.name: Conditional Probabilities From Venn Diagrams
skills.description: Read conditional probabilities such as P(A | B) from a Venn diagram by restricting attention to the given region.

skills.name: The Multiplication Law for Conditional Probability
skills.description: Find the probability that two events both occur using P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B | A).

skills.name: The Law of Total Probability
skills.description: Find the overall probability of an event by splitting into non-overlapping cases and adding the weighted case probabilities.

skills.name: Independent Events
skills.description: Recognize and test whether two events are independent, meaning one occurring does not change the probability of the other.

skills.name: The Addition Law of Probability
skills.description: Find the probability that at least one of two events occurs using P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B).

skills.name: Applying the Addition Law With Event Complements
skills.description: Combine the addition law with the complement rule to find probabilities of 'or', 'neither', and 'not' events.

skills.name: Mutually Exclusive Events
skills.description: Identify events that cannot happen together and add their probabilities directly with P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B).

skills.name: Probability Mass Functions of Discrete Random Variables
skills.description: Describe a discrete random variable by listing P(X = x) for each value, with probabilities that are nonnegative and sum to 1.

skills.name: Cumulative Distribution Functions for Discrete Random Variables
skills.description: Build and use F(x) = P(X ≤ x), the running total of a discrete distribution's probabilities.

skills.name: Expected Values of Discrete Random Variables
skills.description: Compute the long-run average E(X) of a discrete random variable by weighting each value by its probability.

skills.name: The Binomial Distribution
skills.description: Use B(n, p) and its formula P(X = r) = C(n, r) p^r (1 − p)^(n − r) to count successes in independent trials.

skills.name: Modeling With the Binomial Distribution
skills.description: Decide when a real situation fits the binomial conditions, then use B(n, p) to answer questions about it.

skills.name: The Geometric Distribution
skills.description: Use Geo(p), with P(X = r) = (1 − p)^(r − 1) p, to find the probability that the first success occurs on trial r.

skills.name: Modeling With the Geometric Distribution
skills.description: Apply the geometric distribution to real 'wait until the first success' situations and check that its assumptions hold.

skills.name: The Standard Normal Distribution
skills.description: Work with Z ~ N(0, 1), the reference normal distribution, and its cumulative probabilities Φ(z).

skills.name: Symmetry Properties of the Standard Normal Distribution
skills.description: Use the symmetry of the standard normal curve about 0 to find negative-z, upper-tail, and central-interval probabilities.

skills.name: The Normal Distribution
skills.description: Understand the bell-shaped normal distribution, its symmetry, its parameters μ and σ, and probabilities as areas under the curve.

skills.name: Mean and Variance of the Normal Distribution
skills.description: Interpret the mean μ and variance σ² of a normal distribution and find them from given probabilities.

skills.name: Percentage Points of the Standard Normal Distribution
skills.description: Find the z-value that cuts off a given tail probability of the standard normal, such as 1.96 for the upper 2.5%.

skills.name: Modeling With the Normal Distribution
skills.description: Model a real continuous measurement with N(μ, σ²), use z-scores to answer questions, and judge whether the model fits.

skills.name: Convert SI prefixes in measurements
skills.description: Convert measurements between SI prefixes such as kilo, milli, micro, and nano using powers of ten.

skills.name: Distinguish accuracy from precision
skills.description: Separate how close measurements are to the true value from how closely they agree with each other.

skills.name: Distinguish random and systematic measurement errors
skills.description: Classify measurement errors as unpredictable scatter or as a consistent bias in one direction.

skills.name: Propagate independent uncertainty through a sum
skills.description: Combine independent standard uncertainties in a sum or difference by adding them in quadrature.

skills.name: Propagate uncertainty through products and quotients
skills.description: Combine relative uncertainties of independent inputs in quadrature to find the uncertainty of a product or quotient.

skills.name: Fit a straight-line measurement calibration
skills.description: Fit a slope and offset relating an instrument's output to known reference values, then invert it to convert readings.

skills.name: Test a proposed physical scaling law
skills.description: Check a proposed physical relationship using units and by testing how the output changes when an input is scaled.

skills.name: Make an order-of-magnitude physical estimate
skills.description: Estimate a physical quantity to the nearest power of ten using rounded, clearly stated assumptions.

skills.name: Distinguish path distance from displacement
skills.description: Tell apart the total path length traveled and the signed straight-line change in position.

skills.name: Compute average speed over a multistage trip
skills.description: Divide the total distance traveled by the total elapsed time for a trip with several stages.

skills.name: Find average velocity from two position readings
skills.description: Compute signed displacement divided by elapsed time using position readings at two instants.

skills.name: Read instantaneous velocity from a position graph
skills.description: Estimate an object's velocity at one instant from the slope of the tangent line on a position-time graph.

skills.name: Differentiate position to obtain velocity
skills.description: Differentiate a position function with respect to time to get instantaneous velocity at any moment.

skills.name: Differentiate velocity to obtain acceleration
skills.description: Differentiate a velocity function with respect to time to find acceleration and interpret its sign.

skills.name: Find displacement from velocity-time area
skills.description: Use rectangle and triangle areas on a velocity-time graph to find signed displacement and total distance.

skills.name: Integrate velocity to recover position change
skills.description: Use a definite integral of velocity over time to find displacement, and from it the position or distance traveled.

skills.name: Resolve a projectile launch velocity
skills.description: Split a projectile's launch speed and angle into horizontal and vertical velocity components.

skills.name: Calculate projectile flight time to a specified height
skills.description: Solve the vertical motion equation, usually a quadratic in time, for when a projectile reaches a given height.

skills.name: Calculate horizontal projectile displacement
skills.description: Multiply the constant horizontal velocity by the flight time to find how far a projectile travels sideways.

skills.name: Choose a system boundary for a free-body diagram
skills.description: Decide which object or group of objects is the system before drawing only the external forces acting on it.

skills.name: Identify the two bodies in a Newton third-law pair
skills.description: Match each force with its equal-and-opposite partner, which always acts on the other body in the interaction.

skills.name: Resolve a force vector along chosen axes
skills.description: Project a known force onto two perpendicular axes.

skills.name: Determine the required static-friction force
skills.description: Solve for the static friction needed to prevent slipping and check it against the maximum μs N.

skills.name: Set the direction and magnitude of sliding friction
skills.description: Apply kinetic friction with magnitude μk N, pointing opposite the relative sliding of the two surfaces.

skills.name: Calculate apparent weight in an accelerating elevator
skills.description: Find the scale reading, meaning the normal force, for a person in a vertically accelerating elevator.

skills.name: Identify the net inward force in circular motion
skills.description: Find which real forces combine to supply the net inward force m·v²/r that keeps an object moving in a circle.

skills.name: Find terminal speed under a specified drag law
skills.description: Find the constant speed at which drag exactly balances gravity for a falling object under a given drag model.

skills.name: Determine the sign of mechanical work
skills.description: Distinguish positive, negative, and zero work by the angle between force and displacement.

skills.name: Calculate elastic energy stored in an ideal spring
skills.description: Use U = ½kx² to find the elastic potential energy of an ideal spring stretched or compressed by x.

skills.name: Find variable-force work from a force-position graph
skills.description: Sum signed geometric areas under a force-versus-position graph to find the work done by a varying force.

skills.name: Account for dissipated mechanical energy
skills.description: Include energy lost to friction or drag when kinetic plus potential energy is not conserved.

skills.name: Calculate instantaneous mechanical power from force and velocity
skills.description: Evaluate instantaneous power as the dot product of force and the velocity of its point of application.

skills.name: Calculate impulse from a force-time graph
skills.description: Find impulse as the signed area under a force-versus-time graph and relate it to momentum change.

skills.name: Solve a one-dimensional perfectly inelastic collision
skills.description: Find the common final velocity when two bodies stick together, using momentum conservation.

skills.name: Solve a one-dimensional elastic collision
skills.description: Use momentum and kinetic-energy conservation together to find final velocities in a one-dimensional elastic collision.

skills.name: Calculate center of mass for a set of point masses
skills.description: Form the mass-weighted average of position vectors to locate the center of mass of point masses.

skills.name: Calculate escape speed in a point-mass gravity model
skills.description: Find the minimum speed needed to coast away from a planet or star forever, using v = √(2GM/r).

skills.name: Convert angular velocity to tangential speed
skills.description: Apply v = rω to find the linear speed of a point on a rigid rotating body from its angular velocity.

skills.name: Calculate a planar torque with a signed lever arm
skills.description: Compute a torque in a plane as force times perpendicular lever arm, and give it a clockwise or counterclockwise sign.

skills.name: Calculate rotational inertia for point masses
skills.description: Compute the moment of inertia of a set of point masses as I = Σ m r² about a chosen rotation axis.

skills.name: Apply the no-slip rolling constraint
skills.description: Use v = Rω to relate a rolling wheel's centre speed, spin rate, and distance travelled when it does not slip.

skills.name: Calculate the period of an ideal mass-spring oscillator
skills.description: Use T = 2π√(m/k) to find the oscillation period of an ideal undamped mass on a spring.

skills.name: Calculate the small-angle pendulum period
skills.description: Use T = 2π√(L/g) to find a simple pendulum's period when its swings are small.

skills.name: Classify underdamped, critically damped, and overdamped motion
skills.description: Classify a damped linear oscillator as underdamped, critically damped, or overdamped by comparing b² with 4mk.

skills.name: Explain energy transfer near a driven resonance
skills.description: Explain how a periodic drive transfers energy into an oscillator most effectively near its natural frequency, with damping limiting the response.

skills.name: Convert gauge pressure and absolute pressure
skills.description: Convert between gauge pressure, measured relative to the atmosphere, and absolute pressure, measured relative to vacuum.

skills.name: Infer pressure difference from a static liquid column
skills.description: Use the height difference of a liquid column in a manometer to calculate a pressure difference with ΔP = ρgh.

skills.name: Convert area and mean flow speed to volume flow rate
skills.description: Find volume flow rate by multiplying a cross-sectional area by the mean flow speed through it, Q = A·v_avg.

skills.name: Convert volumetric flow rate to mass flow rate
skills.description: Multiply volume flow rate by fluid density to find how many kilograms pass each second, ṁ = ρQ.

skills.name: Interpret Reynolds number for a stated flow geometry
skills.description: Compute Re = ρvL/μ to judge whether inertia or viscosity dominates a flow, using thresholds suited to the geometry.

skills.name: Calculate pressure loss in ideal laminar pipe flow
skills.description: Use Poiseuille's law to relate pressure drop and flow rate for steady laminar flow in a round pipe.

skills.name: Convert Celsius readings and temperature changes to Kelvin
skills.description: Convert Celsius readings to kelvin by adding 273.15, and recognize that temperature changes are the same size in both scales.

skills.name: Solve a two-body thermal mixing problem
skills.description: Find the final temperature when two bodies exchange heat in an insulated system with no phase change.

skills.name: Calculate energy required for a phase change
skills.description: Use Q = mL to find the heat needed to melt, freeze, boil, or condense a mass at its transition temperature.

skills.name: Solve an ideal-gas state using absolute temperature and pressure
skills.description: Apply PV = nRT with absolute pressure, kelvin temperature, and consistent units to find an unknown gas property.

skills.name: Calculate boundary work from a pressure-volume diagram
skills.description: Find the work done by a gas as the signed area under its path on a pressure-volume diagram.

skills.name: Calculate work for an ideal-gas isothermal expansion
skills.description: Find the work done by an ideal gas expanding reversibly at constant temperature using nRT ln(Vf/Vi).

skills.name: Calculate the reversible heat-engine efficiency bound
skills.description: Find the maximum possible efficiency of a heat engine between two reservoirs using 1 − Tcold/Thot.

skills.name: Calculate entropy transfer with reversible heat
skills.description: Find the entropy change from heat transferred reversibly at constant absolute temperature using ΔS = Qrev/T.

skills.name: Calculate steady one-dimensional heat conduction
skills.description: Find the steady heat flow through a uniform slab using q = kAΔT/L.

skills.name: Calculate net thermal radiation to a large surrounding enclosure
skills.description: Find the net radiant heat flow between a surface and much larger surroundings using εσA(Ts⁴ − Tsur⁴).

skills.name: Convert among wave period, frequency, and wavelength
skills.description: Convert among period, frequency, and wavelength using f = 1/T and v = fλ.

skills.name: Calculate phase difference from separation along a sinusoidal wave
skills.description: Convert a separation along a sinusoidal wave into a phase difference using Δφ = 2πΔx/λ.

skills.name: Identify constructive and destructive two-wave path differences
skills.description: Decide whether two coherent waves reinforce or cancel at a point from their path difference in wavelengths.

skills.name: Calculate standing-wave frequencies on a string fixed at both ends
skills.description: Find the allowed standing-wave wavelengths and frequencies of a string fixed at both ends.

skills.name: Convert an intensity ratio to a sound-level difference
skills.description: Find the decibel difference between two sound intensities using 10 log10(I2/I1).

skills.name: Calculate distance from round-trip echo time
skills.description: Find distance to a reflector as half the wave speed times the measured round-trip echo delay.

skills.name: Calculate the force between two point charges
skills.description: Apply the inverse-square Coulomb force magnitude and determine attraction or repulsion.

skills.name: Add electric fields from several point charges
skills.description: Find the net electric field at a point by calculating each point charge’s field vector and adding components.

skills.name: Calculate electric flux through a flat surface in a uniform field
skills.description: Evaluate electric flux through a flat surface in a uniform field as Φ = E · A = EA cos θ.

skills.name: Use Gauss's law with spherical electrostatic symmetry
skills.description: Use a spherical Gaussian surface and Φ = Q_enc/ε₀ to find the field of spherically symmetric charge.

skills.name: Calculate potential energy change of a test charge
skills.description: Use ΔU = qΔV, keeping the sign of the charge, to find how a charge’s electric potential energy changes.

skills.name: Estimate the capacitance of parallel plates
skills.description: Estimate parallel-plate capacitance with C = κε₀A/d when the gap is small compared with the plate size.

skills.name: Determine magnetic force direction on a moving charge
skills.description: Find which way a magnetic field pushes a moving charge using F = q v × B and the charge's sign.

skills.name: Calculate the radius of a charged-particle orbit in a uniform field
skills.description: Find the circle radius of a charged particle moving perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field using r = mv/(|q|B).

skills.name: Calculate magnetic force on a straight current-carrying wire
skills.description: Use F = I L × B to find the force on a straight current-carrying wire in a uniform magnetic field.

skills.name: Calculate torque on a current loop in a magnetic field
skills.description: Find the twisting effect on a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field using τ = N I A B sin θ.

skills.name: Determine the direction of an induced current
skills.description: Use Lenz's law to decide which way an induced current flows by opposing the change in magnetic flux.

skills.name: Calculate the emf across a rod moving through a magnetic field
skills.description: Calculate the voltage produced across a conducting rod moving through a magnetic field with emf = B L v.

skills.name: Explain speed-dependent back emf in a DC motor
skills.description: Explain why a spinning DC motor generates a voltage opposing its supply, and how that limits current as speed rises.

skills.name: Apply the law of specular reflection
skills.description: Draw or calculate a reflected ray whose angle from the surface normal equals the angle of incidence.

skills.name: Calculate a refraction angle with Snell's law
skills.description: Use Snell's law, n1 sin θ1 = n2 sin θ2, to find how much a ray bends when it crosses from one medium into another.

skills.name: Calculate the critical angle for total internal reflection
skills.description: Find the incidence angle beyond which light in a higher-index medium is totally reflected at a boundary, using sin θc = n2/n1.

skills.name: Calculate image distance with the thin-lens equation
skills.description: Solve 1/f = 1/d_o + 1/d_i for the image distance of a thin lens and decide whether the image is real or virtual.

skills.name: Calculate transverse magnification of a thin lens
skills.description: Find a thin lens's magnification m = −d_i/d_o to get the image's relative size and whether it is upright or inverted.

skills.name: Calculate double-slit fringe spacing
skills.description: Estimate the spacing of bright double-slit interference fringes using Δy ≈ λL/d for a distant screen.

skills.name: Estimate diffraction-limited angular resolution of a circular aperture
skills.description: Estimate the smallest resolvable angle for a circular aperture using the Rayleigh criterion, θ ≈ 1.22 λ/D.

skills.name: Calculate transmission through an ideal linear polarizer
skills.description: Find the intensity passed by an ideal linear polarizer using Malus's law, I = I0 cos²θ.

skills.name: Convert photon wavelength into photon energy
skills.description: Convert a photon's vacuum wavelength into its energy using E = hc/λ, in joules or electronvolts.

skills.name: Determine a photoelectric threshold and maximum electron energy
skills.description: Use K_max = hf − φ to find the threshold frequency or wavelength and the kinetic energy of the fastest ejected electrons.

skills.name: Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of a particle
skills.description: Calculate the wavelength associated with a moving particle using λ = h/p.

skills.name: Interpret the position-momentum uncertainty relation
skills.description: Interpret Δx Δp ≥ ħ/2 as a lower bound on the spreads of position and momentum in any quantum state.

skills.name: Interpret a quantum position probability density
skills.description: Find the probability of locating a particle in an interval by integrating |ψ(x)|² of a normalized wavefunction.

skills.name: Calculate energy levels in a one-dimensional infinite potential well
skills.description: Compute the allowed energies E_n = n²h²/(8mL²) of a particle confined between two impenetrable walls a distance L apart.

skills.name: Calculate time dilation for inertial relative motion
skills.description: Use the Lorentz factor γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²) to compare a proper time interval with the longer interval measured in another inertial frame.

skills.name: Calculate a moving object's longitudinal length
skills.description: Find the length of a moving object along its direction of motion as L = L0/γ, with both endpoints located at the same instant.

skills.name: Calculate mass-energy equivalence
skills.description: Evaluate the rest energy E = mc² of a mass with consistent units, and relate changes in mass to changes in energy.

skills.name: Calculate radioactive decay fractions from half-life
skills.description: Find the fraction of a radioactive sample remaining after a given time using (1/2)^(t / half-life).

skills.name: Calculate nuclear binding energy from a mass defect
skills.description: Convert the mass defect between separate nucleons and a bound nucleus into binding energy using E = Δm c².

skills.name: Values and data types
skills.description: Recognize the type of a value, such as integer, floating-point number, text string, or Boolean, and predict which operations that type allows.

skills.name: Variables and assignment
skills.description: Store a value under a name, reassign it, and trace how each variable changes line by line.

skills.name: Expressions and operators
skills.description: Evaluate arithmetic, comparison, and logical expressions, applying operator precedence, integer division, and remainder correctly.

skills.name: Type conversion and formatted output
skills.description: Convert between text and numbers deliberately, and format numbers as readable text with controlled precision.

skills.name: Text strings and parsing
skills.description: Index, slice, search, split, and join strings to extract fields from lines of text.

skills.name: Conditional branching
skills.description: Choose between paths with if, else-if, and else, ordering the tests so every case reaches exactly one intended branch.

skills.name: Loops and iteration
skills.description: Repeat work with for and while loops, choosing bounds and exit conditions so a loop runs the intended number of times and terminates.

skills.name: Functions, parameters, and return values
skills.description: Define functions that take parameters and return results, and call them with the right arguments in the right order.

skills.name: Variable scope and lifetime
skills.description: Predict which variable a name refers to inside and outside a function, and how long each variable exists.

skills.name: Lists, dictionaries, and sets
skills.description: Store groups of values in ordered lists, key-value dictionaries, and sets, then index, update, test membership, and iterate over them.

skills.name: References, mutation, and aliasing
skills.description: Distinguish changing an object in place from rebinding a name, and predict when two names share one mutable object.

skills.name: Exceptions and error handling
skills.description: Raise, catch, and clean up after errors so a program fails clearly or recovers on purpose, never silently.

skills.name: Classes and objects
skills.description: Group related data and the functions that act on it into classes, create instances, and keep each object's state valid through its methods.

skills.name: Terminal navigation and commands
skills.description: Move around the file system from a command line, run programs with arguments, and read their output.

skills.name: Redirection, pipes, and exit codes
skills.description: Send a program's output to a file or to another program, and use exit codes to tell success from failure.

skills.name: Reading and writing files
skills.description: Open, read, write, and close text and structured data files with correct paths, modes, and encodings.

skills.name: Modules and imports
skills.description: Split a program across files, import names from modules, and understand how the language finds what you import.

skills.name: Package dependencies and environments
skills.description: Install third-party packages into an isolated environment and record exact versions so the project can be rebuilt elsewhere.

skills.name: Compilation, linking, and build tools
skills.description: Explain how source files become an executable through compiling and linking, and drive that process with a build tool.

skills.name: Systematic debugging
skills.description: Find the cause of a bug by reproducing it, narrowing down where it occurs, and testing one hypothesis at a time.

skills.name: Using an interactive debugger
skills.description: Pause a running program at breakpoints, step through it, and inspect variables and the call stack.

skills.name: Unit testing
skills.description: Write automated tests that check a function's results, including edge cases, and run them to catch regressions.

skills.name: Version control with Git commits
skills.description: Record project history as commits, inspect what changed, and restore earlier versions of files.

skills.name: Git branches and merging
skills.description: Develop changes on separate branches, merge them back, and resolve conflicts when two branches edit the same lines.

skills.name: Remote repositories and pull requests
skills.description: Clone, fetch, pull, and push to shared repositories, and propose changes through reviewed pull requests.

skills.name: Documenting code and projects
skills.description: Write comments, docstrings, and README files that let another person, or you later, use and change the code correctly.

skills.name: Remote Linux administration: SSH, permissions, and services
skills.description: Work on a Linux robot computer remotely over SSH, manage file permissions and administrator access, and run software as a service that starts at boot.

skills.name: Arrays and dynamic arrays
skills.description: Use contiguous, indexed storage and predict the cost of indexing, appending, inserting, and removing elements.

skills.name: Linked lists
skills.description: Build sequences from nodes that point to the next node, and compare their insertion and access costs with arrays.

skills.name: Stacks
skills.description: Use a last-in, first-out stack for push and pop, and recognize problems it fits, such as nesting, undo, and backtracking.

skills.name: Queues and ring buffers
skills.description: Use first-in, first-out queues, including fixed-size ring buffers that wrap around, to pass items on in arrival order.

skills.name: Hash tables
skills.description: Explain how hashing gives near-constant-time lookup by key, and what collisions, load factor, and hashable keys mean.

skills.name: Recursion
skills.description: Solve a problem by having a function call itself on smaller inputs, with a base case that ends the recursion.

skills.name: Trees and binary search trees
skills.description: Represent hierarchies as trees of linked nodes, traverse them, and use binary search trees for ordered lookup.

skills.name: Priority queues and heaps
skills.description: Retrieve the smallest or most urgent item efficiently with a binary heap, the usual implementation of a priority queue.

skills.name: Graphs in code: representation and traversal
skills.description: Store a graph as an adjacency list, matrix, or implicit grid, and implement searches that return the actual path, including Dijkstra's algorithm and A* with a priority queue.

skills.name: Linear and binary search
skills.description: Find items by scanning, or by repeatedly halving a sorted range, and implement binary search without off-by-one errors.

skills.name: Sorting algorithms
skills.description: Compare simple and efficient sorting algorithms by running time, memory, and stability, and use library sorts with custom keys.

skills.name: Estimating the running time of code
skills.description: Derive how a piece of code's time and memory grow with input size by counting loop iterations and the cost of the operations inside them.

skills.name: Numerical arrays and vectorized computation
skills.description: Compute on whole arrays at once with NumPy-style vectorized operations, slicing, broadcasting, and axis reductions instead of element-by-element loops.

skills.name: Integer representation and overflow
skills.description: Represent signed integers in two's complement, state the range of a fixed-width integer, and recognize overflow and wraparound.

skills.name: Floating-point numbers and rounding error
skills.description: Explain how floating-point numbers store a sign, exponent, and significand, and handle their rounding error, limited precision, and special values.

skills.name: Character encoding: ASCII and UTF-8
skills.description: Convert between text and bytes with an explicit encoding, and recognize ASCII, UTF-8, and the errors caused by mismatched encodings.

skills.name: Bitwise operations and masks
skills.description: Set, clear, toggle, test, and extract bit fields using AND, OR, XOR, NOT, and shifts.

skills.name: Memory, addresses, and alignment
skills.description: Model memory as numbered bytes, and relate addresses, word size, alignment, and the size of each data type.

skills.name: Byte order and binary data layouts
skills.description: Pack and unpack multi-byte values in a defined byte order and layout when exchanging binary data with files, devices, or networks.

skills.name: Processor registers and status flags
skills.description: Describe the processor's registers, including general-purpose registers, the program counter, the stack pointer, and status flags, and say what each is used for.

skills.name: Machine instructions and assembly language
skills.description: Read short assembly sequences and map loads, stores, arithmetic, comparisons, and branches back to the high-level code they implement.

skills.name: Processor datapath and pipelining
skills.description: Trace how a processor fetches, decodes, and executes instructions through its datapath, and explain why pipelining raises throughput and what stalls it.

skills.name: Caches and memory locality
skills.description: Explain how caches exploit temporal and spatial locality, and write memory access patterns that run faster because of them.

skills.name: Device input and output: polling, interrupts, and DMA
skills.description: Explain how software controls devices through memory-mapped registers, and compare polling, interrupts, and DMA for moving data.

skills.name: C language essentials
skills.description: Write, compile, and run small C programs with declared variables, functions, arrays, strings, and printf, and act on the compiler's warnings.

skills.name: Static types and fixed-width integers
skills.description: Declare variables with static types, choose fixed-width integer types, and predict implicit conversions in languages such as C and C++.

skills.name: Pointers and addresses
skills.description: Use pointers to refer to memory locations, dereference them safely, and relate pointers to arrays and function arguments.

skills.name: Stack, heap, and static memory
skills.description: Place each variable in static storage, the stack, or the heap, and predict its lifetime and the failures each region can cause.

skills.name: Dynamic memory allocation and ownership
skills.description: Allocate and free heap memory correctly, assign clear ownership, and avoid leaks, double frees, and use-after-free errors.

skills.name: Operating system kernel and system calls
skills.description: Explain what an operating system kernel does, how programs request its services through system calls, and why user programs run with restricted privileges.

skills.name: Virtual memory and address spaces
skills.description: Explain how each process gets its own virtual address space mapped to physical memory in pages, and what page faults and segmentation faults mean.

skills.name: Processes and program execution
skills.description: Start, monitor, and stop processes, and use their arguments, environment, exit status, and signals.

skills.name: Threads
skills.description: Run work concurrently in threads that share a process's memory, wait for them with join, and stop them by request rather than by force.

skills.name: CPU scheduling and context switches
skills.description: Explain how an operating system shares processor time among threads through preemption, time slices, and priorities, and what a context switch costs.

skills.name: Race conditions and shared data
skills.description: Recognize concurrent code whose result depends on timing, and identify the shared data and non-atomic operations that cause it.

skills.name: Locks, semaphores, and condition variables
skills.description: Protect shared data with mutexes, wait for conditions without busy-waiting, and coordinate producers and consumers.

skills.name: Deadlock and lock ordering
skills.description: Recognize how threads can block each other forever, and prevent deadlock with lock ordering, timeouts, and simpler designs.

skills.name: Event loops and asynchronous I/O
skills.description: Structure a program around an event loop that runs callbacks or coroutines when data arrives or timers fire, without blocking the loop.

skills.name: Packets, headers, and protocol layers
skills.description: Describe how data travels as packets whose headers carry addressing and control information, and how protocol layers wrap one another.

skills.name: IP addresses, subnets, and ports
skills.description: Read IPv4 and IPv6 addresses with prefix lengths, decide whether two hosts share a subnet, and use port numbers to reach a program on a host.

skills.name: Error detection with checksums and CRCs
skills.description: Detect corrupted data with parity bits, checksums, and cyclic redundancy checks, and know what each can and cannot catch.

skills.name: Reliable delivery over unreliable links
skills.description: Build reliable communication from sequence numbers, acknowledgements, timeouts, and retransmission, and handle the resulting duplicates safely.

skills.name: UDP and TCP transport
skills.description: Choose between UDP datagrams and TCP byte streams by what they guarantee about delivery, order, message boundaries, and delay.

skills.name: Message framing and serialization
skills.description: Turn structured messages into bytes and back, and mark where each message starts and ends in a continuous byte stream.

skills.name: Socket programming
skills.description: Exchange data over TCP and UDP from your own programs, handling blocking calls, partial reads, timeouts, and connections that close or fail.

skills.name: Latency, bandwidth, and jitter
skills.description: Distinguish latency, bandwidth, and jitter, measure them, and estimate how they limit a networked or real-time system.

skills.name: Microcontroller architecture
skills.description: Describe what a microcontroller integrates, including core, flash, RAM, clocks, and peripherals, and choose one against a project's needs.

skills.name: Firmware structure, build, and flashing
skills.description: Build firmware with a cross-toolchain, flash it onto a microcontroller, and structure it as startup code, initialization, and a main loop.

skills.name: GPIO configuration and digital I/O
skills.description: Configure general-purpose pins as inputs or outputs with suitable pull resistors and drive modes, read and write them, and debounce mechanical inputs.

skills.name: Interrupts and interrupt service routines
skills.description: Configure interrupts, write short interrupt service routines, and share data safely between an ISR and the main program.

skills.name: Hardware timers and PWM generation
skills.description: Configure hardware timers from clock, prescaler, and period to produce periodic interrupts and PWM outputs and to measure time precisely.

skills.name: UART, SPI, and I²C in firmware
skills.description: Configure UART, SPI, and I²C peripherals and use them from firmware to exchange data with sensors and other chips.

skills.name: Fixed-point arithmetic
skills.description: Represent fractional values as scaled integers, choose a Q format, and add, multiply, and round them without overflow.

skills.name: Watchdog timers and fail-safe states
skills.description: Use a watchdog timer to recover from hung firmware, and design reset and communication-loss paths so outputs fall to a safe state.

skills.name: Deadlines, jitter, and execution-time budgets
skills.description: State a task's timing requirements as periods and deadlines, measure execution time and jitter, and check that the worst case fits the budget.

skills.name: Real-time scheduling and priority inversion
skills.description: Assign task priorities by rate-monotonic or deadline rules, check whether a task set can meet its deadlines, and prevent priority inversion.

skills.name: RTOS tasks, queues, and timers
skills.description: Structure firmware as prioritized tasks under a real-time operating system, communicating through queues, semaphores, and software timers.

skills.name: Sensor data acquisition in software
skills.description: Read sensors at a known rate, timestamp each sample, convert raw counts to physical units, and detect stale or invalid data.

skills.name: Coordinate transforms in software
skills.description: Represent poses and frames in code, compose and invert transforms in the correct order, and look them up from a time-stamped transform tree.

skills.name: Publish-subscribe messaging and robot middleware
skills.description: Connect robot software components through typed messages on topics, request-response services, and quality-of-service settings.

skills.name: Finite-state machines for robot behaviour
skills.description: Model robot behaviour as explicit states, events, and transitions, and implement the machine so every state handles every relevant event deliberately.

skills.name: Implementing a discrete-time control loop
skills.description: Implement a feedback controller as a fixed-rate read, compute, and write loop with correct time steps, output limits, anti-windup, and safe start and stop behaviour.

skills.name: Robot simulation and simulated time
skills.description: Run robot software against a simulator, handling simulated time, the physics step, and the differences between simulation and the real robot.

skills.name: Logging and recorded data
skills.description: Record time-stamped logs and data streams at a useful level of detail, and replay them to diagnose problems after the fact.

skills.name: Timestamps and clock synchronization
skills.description: Use the right clock for each purpose, timestamp data at its source, and align data from devices whose clocks disagree.

skills.name: Testing with simulation and recorded data
skills.description: Test robot software automatically against simulated scenarios and replayed sensor recordings before it runs on hardware.

skills.name: Robot software integration and bring-up
skills.description: Assemble sensing, control, and communication software into one working robot through launch configuration, parameters, interface checks, and staged bring-up.

skills.name: Datasets, features, and labels
skills.description: Organize data into examples with features and labels, split it into training, validation, and test sets, and spot leakage and bias.

skills.name: Feature scaling and preprocessing
skills.description: Transform raw inputs into model-ready features by scaling, encoding categories, and handling missing values, using statistics from the training set only.

skills.name: Training versus inference
skills.description: Distinguish fitting a model's parameters to data during training from applying the fixed parameters to new inputs during inference, with their different costs and failure modes.

skills.name: Regression models and loss functions
skills.description: Fit a model that predicts a continuous value by minimizing a loss such as mean squared error, and judge it on held-out data.

skills.name: Gradient-descent training
skills.description: Train model parameters by repeatedly stepping against the gradient of the loss, choosing the learning rate, batch size, and number of passes over the data.

skills.name: Classification and decision thresholds
skills.description: Train models that assign inputs to categories, interpret their predicted probabilities, and choose a decision threshold by the cost of each kind of mistake.

skills.name: Evaluating models with metrics and held-out data
skills.description: Measure model performance on data it has not seen with suitable metrics, including confusion matrices, precision and recall, and regression errors.

skills.name: Overfitting, underfitting, and regularization
skills.description: Diagnose overfitting and underfitting from training and validation error, and control model complexity with regularization, more data, and early stopping.

skills.name: Neural-network basics
skills.description: Explain how a neural network computes outputs through layers of weighted sums and nonlinear activations, and how backpropagation trains it.

skills.name: Deploying learned models under robot constraints
skills.description: Fit a trained model into a robot's compute, memory, latency, and power limits, and monitor it for inputs unlike its training data.

skills.name: Identify electrically common points on a DC schematic
skills.description: A circuit node consists of points joined by ideal conductors without a component between them.

skills.name: Calculate average current from charge transferred over time
skills.description: Average current describes net charge passing a cross-section during a stated interval: I = ΔQ/Δt.

skills.name: Interpret a signed current relative to a reference arrow
skills.description: A branch-current arrow defines the direction counted as positive.

skills.name: Calculate signed voltage between two labeled nodes
skills.description: Voltage between nodes A and B is V_AB = V_A − V_B when both node values use the same reference.

skills.name: Decide whether a constant-resistance model fits a stated DC case
skills.description: A fixed resistor model assumes voltage is proportional to current over the operating conditions being considered.

skills.name: Solve for voltage, current, or resistance in one ohmic element
skills.description: Use V = IR to find one unknown from two known quantities for the same ohmic component.

skills.name: Recognize resistors that form an unbranched series path
skills.description: Resistors form a simple series path when the intermediate connections have no other conducting branches.

skills.name: Calculate the equivalent resistance of a series group
skills.description: Replace a valid series group by one resistance equal to the sum of its resistor values.

skills.name: Recognize resistors connected across the same two nodes
skills.description: Resistors are in parallel when each terminal pair connects to the same two circuit nodes.

skills.name: Calculate equivalent resistance using parallel conductances
skills.description: For positive finite parallel resistors, add their reciprocal resistances and invert the result: 1/R_eq = Σ(1/R_i).

skills.name: Determine current and individual drops in a one-source series circuit
skills.description: For a fixed DC voltage source driving a series resistor chain, first obtain total resistance, then the shared current, and finally each component’s voltage drop.

skills.name: Determine branch and supply currents in a one-source parallel circuit
skills.description: In a resistor network connected directly across an ideal fixed-voltage DC source, each branch sees the source voltage.

skills.name: Reduce a resistor network by successive series and parallel replacements
skills.description: Simplify a reducible resistor network one valid group at a time, redrawing its node connections after each replacement.

skills.name: Calculate the output of an unloaded two-resistor divider
skills.description: For two positive resistors in series across a source, calculate the junction voltage relative to the lower terminal using V_out = V_in R_lower/(R_upper + R_lower).

skills.name: Choose a resistor ratio for a specified unloaded divider output
skills.description: Work backward from a desired output fraction between zero and one to a resistor ratio.

skills.name: Calculate divider output with a specified resistive load
skills.description: When a resistive load is connected from a divider output to its lower reference terminal, combine that load in parallel with the lower divider resistor.

skills.name: Calculate steady DC power dissipated in a resistor
skills.description: Calculate heat dissipation in a passive resistor using P = VI, I²R, or V²/R with quantities belonging to that resistor.

skills.name: Compare resistor dissipation with a stated derated power limit
skills.description: Compare calculated resistor dissipation with the permitted power under the datasheet’s stated mounting and temperature conditions.

skills.name: Measure DC voltage between specified points in a low-energy circuit
skills.description: Select the meter’s DC-voltage function and appropriate terminals and range for a low-voltage, current-limited teaching circuit.

skills.name: Measure branch DC current by inserting a meter in series
skills.description: In a low-energy, current-limited teaching circuit, select a suitable fused current input and range, then insert the meter into the intended branch with power removed while changing connections.

skills.name: Measure an isolated resistor in a de-energized circuit
skills.description: A resistance meter applies its own test stimulus.

skills.name: Estimate divider measurement error from finite voltmeter input resistance
skills.description: Represent a DC voltmeter’s specified input resistance as an additional load across the measurement points.

skills.name: Estimate the current change caused by a meter’s series resistance
skills.description: A real ammeter introduces resistance and therefore a voltage drop into the branch it measures.

skills.name: Predict the effect of one open resistor in a simple DC network
skills.description: Model one failed resistor as an open circuit and determine which current paths remain.

skills.name: Predict the effect of a bypass short in a simple DC network
skills.description: Model a specified bypass fault as a near-zero-resistance connection and determine which nodes become effectively joined.

skills.name: Choose a voltage test point that distinguishes two stated DC fault hypotheses
skills.description: Given a simple resistive circuit and two proposed faults, predict a voltage reading for each and select a test point where the predictions differ.

skills.name: Choose and consistently apply a one-dimensional coordinate convention
skills.description: Define an origin, positive direction, and reference frame before assigning signed positions and displacements.

skills.name: Calculate average acceleration from two signed velocity readings
skills.description: Calculate average acceleration as the final velocity minus the initial velocity, divided by elapsed time.

skills.name: Determine speeding up or slowing down from velocity and acceleration signs
skills.description: In one dimension, a nonzero velocity and acceleration with the same sign increase speed; opposite signs decrease speed.

skills.name: Read acceleration from a straight segment of a velocity-time graph
skills.description: For a straight segment on a velocity-time graph, use change in velocity divided by change in time to obtain its constant slope and acceleration.

skills.name: Recover velocity change from piecewise-constant acceleration areas
skills.description: For a piecewise-constant acceleration-time graph, multiply each acceleration by its interval duration and add the signed areas.

skills.name: Check whether a constant-acceleration model is justified over an interval
skills.description: Before applying constant-acceleration equations, identify the interval over which the assumption is stated or supported.

skills.name: Calculate final position and velocity over a known constant-acceleration interval
skills.description: Given initial position, initial velocity, constant acceleration, and elapsed time, calculate the final velocity and position using v = v0 + aΔt and x = x0 + v0Δt + aΔt²/2.

skills.name: Carry position and velocity between successive motion intervals
skills.description: Use the final position and velocity of one motion interval as the initial conditions of the next.

skills.name: Explain velocity and acceleration at the top of an ideal vertical throw
skills.description: For a vertical throw under gravity alone near Earth, vertical velocity is momentarily zero at the highest point while acceleration remains downward.

skills.name: Distinguish mass from gravitational weight and calculate weight using a stated g
skills.description: Mass is measured in kilograms; gravitational weight is a force measured in newtons with magnitude mg in the stated local gravitational field.

skills.name: Identify the direction of a normal contact force
skills.description: For an ordinary nonadhesive contact, the normal force acts perpendicular to the local surface and pushes the chosen body away from it.

skills.name: Identify the force direction exerted by a taut flexible cable
skills.description: A taut flexible cable pulls an attached body along the cable away from the attachment point.

skills.name: Check when equal tension may be assumed in an ideal cable model
skills.description: Equal tension along a cable segment requires an appropriate idealization, such as negligible cable mass and no distributed tangential loading.

skills.name: Infer constant velocity from zero net force in an inertial frame
skills.description: For a constant-mass body in an inertial frame, zero net external force implies zero acceleration and therefore constant velocity.

skills.name: Audit a free-body diagram for missing and double-counted interactions
skills.description: Check a proposed diagram against the isolated body and its actual interactions.

skills.name: Translate a supplied collinear force diagram into a signed Newton equation
skills.description: Choose a positive axis and translate a correct diagram of collinear forces into ΣF = ma for a constant-mass body in an inertial frame.

skills.name: Determine a normal force from a supplied perpendicular force balance
skills.description: Given a correct force diagram with components already resolved perpendicular to a support, use Newton’s second law in that direction to determine the normal reaction.

skills.name: Check whether a predicted normal reaction is compatible with nonadhesive contact
skills.description: An ordinary nonadhesive support can push on a body but cannot pull it toward the surface.

skills.name: Identify which interaction forces cancel when two bodies form one system
skills.description: When two interacting bodies are included in one system, their mutual Newton third-law forces are internal and cancel in the vector sum for that combined system.

skills.name: Calculate engineering tensile stress using the original specimen area
skills.description: Convert a tensile force measurement into engineering stress by dividing it by the original cross-sectional area.

skills.name: Calculate engineering strain from a stated gauge length
skills.description: Calculate engineering strain as the change in gauge length divided by its original length.

skills.name: Extract Young’s modulus from a specified linear stress-strain interval
skills.description: Find Young’s modulus from the stress change divided by the strain change over a stated linear elastic interval.

skills.name: Compare axial part stiffness after changing length, area, or modulus
skills.description: For a uniform straight bar under small, linear elastic axial deformation, use k=EA/L to compare force-per-extension stiffness.

skills.name: Distinguish recoverable deformation from linear stress-strain response
skills.description: Elastic response concerns recovery after unloading, while linear response concerns the shape of a stress-strain relationship.

skills.name: Determine 0.2 percent offset proof stress from a tensile curve
skills.description: Draw a line with the measured elastic slope starting at strain 0.002, and read the stress where it intersects the tensile curve.

skills.name: Estimate residual strain using a stated linear elastic unloading model
skills.description: For a specified uniaxial state with total strain epsilon and tensile stress sigma, subtract the recoverable strain sigma/E to estimate residual strain.

skills.name: Find ultimate tensile strength from peak load and original area
skills.description: Locate the maximum recorded tensile load and divide it by the original specimen area to obtain ultimate tensile strength.

skills.name: Compare nominal and current-area average stress using measured areas
skills.description: At a given tensile load, calculate nominal stress with the original area and current-area average stress with the measured current section.

skills.name: Distinguish modulus, yield strength, and tensile strength in property data
skills.description: Choose the property column that answers the question being asked: modulus describes elastic stress-to-strain response, yield strength describes a stated yielding criterion, and tensile strength identifies a peak engineering tensile stress..

skills.name: Replace ideal planar supports with their allowed reaction components
skills.description: Choose reaction unknowns from the motion an ideal support restrains.

skills.name: Replace an equal-and-opposite force couple with its signed moment
skills.description: Two equal, opposite, parallel forces on distinct lines have zero resultant force but a nonzero couple moment.

skills.name: Move a force to another point using an equivalent force-and-couple system
skills.description: To represent a force applied at A by the same force at B, add a couple equal to the original force moment about B.

skills.name: Solve reactions of a stable pin-and-roller beam under point loads
skills.description: For a straight horizontal beam with an ideal pin at one end and a vertical roller reaction at the other, calculate reactions from planar equilibrium.

skills.name: Solve the force and moment reactions of a planar cantilever
skills.description: An ideal fixed end can supply two force components and a moment reaction.

skills.name: Audit a proposed planar reaction solution using force and moment residuals
skills.description: Substitute proposed reactions into horizontal force balance, vertical force balance, and a moment balance.

skills.name: Detect unrestrained planar rigid-body motion from support geometry
skills.description: Inspect whether ideal support directions restrain both translations and rotation of a planar rigid body.

skills.name: Recognize when support reactions require deformation compatibility
skills.description: For a stable single planar rigid body, compare independent reaction unknowns with the available independent equilibrium equations.

skills.name: Recognize the conditions for an ideal two-force member
skills.description: An isolated member in static equilibrium with only two nonzero applied forces and no applied couple must have equal, opposite, collinear forces.

skills.name: Transfer a known joint force between separate member diagrams
skills.description: When two members interact through an ideal joint, represent the force on one member as equal and opposite to the force on the other.

skills.name: Calculate internal normal force, shear, and bending moment at one beam cut
skills.description: Cut a planar beam at a specified section away from a concentrated load or applied couple, and isolate either side.

skills.name: Label the reference frame of a robot position or direction
skills.description: Attach a frame label to coordinate values before combining them.

skills.name: Construct a rotation matrix from one frame’s axes expressed in another
skills.description: Form R_AB by placing the three unit axes of frame B, expressed in frame A, into its columns.

skills.name: Check whether a supplied matrix represents a proper 3D rotation
skills.description: Check that R transpose times R equals the identity and that the determinant is positive one.

skills.name: Apply translation to a point but not to a free displacement vector
skills.description: For a rigid coordinate conversion use p_A=R_AB p_B+t_AB for a point and d_A=R_AB d_B for a free displacement vector.

skills.name: Compose a chain of labeled rigid transforms in the correct order
skills.description: With T_AB mapping B coordinates into A coordinates, combine successive mappings as T_AC=T_AB T_BC.

skills.name: Invert a rigid transform while rotating its translation correctly
skills.description: For T_AB with rotation R and translation t, form T_BA using R transpose and translation minus R transpose times t.

skills.name: Count independent coordinates of an unconstrained serial joint chain
skills.description: For a fixed-base open chain of independent one-degree-of-freedom revolute or prismatic joints, count one configuration coordinate per joint.

skills.name: Specify joint order, zero references, signs, and units for a configuration
skills.description: Define a configuration vector by listing joint coordinates in a fixed order with their units, positive directions, and zero references.

skills.name: Distinguish joint configuration, task coordinates, and reachable workspace
skills.description: Joint coordinates describe the robot arrangement, while task coordinates describe the output specified for a job.

skills.name: Calculate position and orientation of an ideal two-revolute-link planar arm
skills.description: For link lengths L1 and L2, shoulder angle q1, and relative elbow angle q2, compute x=L1 cos(q1)+L2 cos(q1+q2) and y=L1 sin(q1)+L2 sin(q1+q2).

skills.name: Include a fixed tool offset after the final link transform
skills.description: When the tool frame is displaced from the last link frame, append the fixed link-to-tool transform to the chain.

skills.name: Check the geometric position reach of an unrestricted planar two-link arm
skills.description: For positive link lengths and unrestricted revolute angles, a target distance r from the base is reachable in position when abs(L1-L2) is at most r and r is at most L1+L2..

skills.name: Calculate both regular inverse-kinematic branches of a planar two-link arm
skills.description: For a reachable position, compute c2=(x*x+y*y-L1*L1-L2*L2)/(2*L1*L2) and q2=plus or minus acos(c2).

skills.name: Verify an inverse-kinematic candidate by forward substitution and joint limits
skills.description: Substitute a candidate configuration into the forward model and compare the output with the requested target using stated tolerances.

skills.name: Derive the Cartesian position Jacobian of a planar two-link arm
skills.description: Differentiate the two planar tip-position equations with respect to q1 and q2.

skills.name: Calculate instantaneous planar tip velocity from joint rates
skills.description: Evaluate the position Jacobian at the current configuration and multiply it by the joint-rate vector.

skills.name: Identify lost instantaneous motion directions at a planar arm singularity
skills.description: For the two-link position task, the Jacobian determinant is L1*L2*sin(q2).

skills.name: Choose the system for an energy balance
skills.description: Decide which objects are inside the system before an energy balance, so each interaction is counted once, either as work or as stored potential energy.

skills.name: Test when momentum conservation applies
skills.description: Decide whether a system's total momentum, or one component of it, is conserved during an event by checking the net external impulse.

skills.name: Check assumptions before a Bernoulli calculation
skills.description: Decide whether a flow is steady, incompressible, effectively frictionless and free of pumps or turbines along the chosen streamline before using Bernoulli's equation.

skills.name: Track sign conventions in a thermal energy balance
skills.description: Carry one stated heat and work sign convention through a multi-step thermal balance, and convert results between the two common conventions.

skills.name: Compare flux change mechanisms
skills.description: Identify whether an induced emf comes from a changing field, a changing area or a changing orientation, and estimate each contribution.

skills.name: Convert between time delay and phase shift
skills.description: Convert a time delay into a phase shift at a given frequency, and recognize that a fixed delay gives a phase shift that grows with frequency.

skills.name: Separate optical resolution and pixel sampling
skills.description: Decide whether a camera's smallest resolvable detail is set by its optics (diffraction blur) or by its pixel spacing.

skills.name: Find a Thevenin equivalent with a dependent source
skills.description: Find Vth and Rth when the network contains a dependent source, which cannot be switched off.

skills.name: Check superposition limits for power calculations
skills.description: Recognize that power cannot be found by adding the power from each source acting alone, and add currents or voltages first.

skills.name: Verify a circuit solution using independent balances
skills.description: Check a solved circuit with a balance not used to solve it: a loop's voltages, another node's currents, or the power supplied against the power absorbed.

skills.name: Determine a capacitor's initial and final voltage
skills.description: Find a capacitor's voltage just after a switching event and once the circuit has settled, before solving the transient between them.

skills.name: Interpret poles, damping and resonance from a second-order model
skills.description: Read the natural frequency, damping ratio and response type from a second-order model, and relate them to an RLC circuit's components.

skills.name: Choose a valid diode approximation
skills.description: Pick the simplest diode model, ideal switch, constant drop, drop plus resistance, or exponential, that is accurate enough for the circuit at hand.

skills.name: Check a switch's voltage and current limits
skills.description: Compare the worst-case voltage across and current through a transistor switch with its ratings, with margin, including spikes and temperature.

skills.name: Distinguish conduction loss and switching loss
skills.description: Separate the loss a switch dissipates while fully on from the loss during each transition, and see which dominates as frequency rises.

skills.name: Check an op-amp's input and output range
skills.description: Confirm that a circuit's input voltages stay within the op-amp's common-mode range and that its required output stays within the achievable swing.

skills.name: Convert ADC codes with a stated reference
skills.description: Convert between an ADC code and the input voltage using the converter's stated reference and code convention, and estimate the effect of reference error.

skills.name: Trace a high-current return loop
skills.description: Follow the path a high or fast current takes back to its source, and find the loop's area and which other circuits share it.

skills.name: Plan test points for diagnosing a board
skills.description: Choose and place a board's test points so the supplies, references and key signals needed to separate likely faults can be measured safely.

skills.name: Replace a distributed load with an equivalent resultant
skills.description: Replace a load spread along a beam with a single force equal to its total, acting at its centroid, for use in external equilibrium.

skills.name: Solve selected truss joints
skills.description: Find the forces in the members meeting at a truss joint by applying equilibrium at a joint with no more than two unknown member forces.

skills.name: Identify the limits of a uniaxial material model
skills.description: Decide whether properties from a uniaxial tensile test apply to a part, given its stress state, loading rate, temperature and material direction.

skills.name: Check effective-length assumptions in a buckling model
skills.description: Choose the effective-length factor from how a column's ends are really held, and check how much the buckling load depends on that choice.

skills.name: Distinguish nominal and peak stress
skills.description: Compute both the nominal stress on a net section and the peak stress at a notch, and decide which one a given check should use.

skills.name: Distinguish yielding from crack-driven failure
skills.description: For a part with a known crack, compare the stress that would cause yielding with the stress that would cause fast fracture, and say which comes first.

skills.name: Distinguish fibre-direction effects from isotropic response
skills.description: Compute a fibre composite's stiffness along and across its fibres and recognize when an isotropic formula would mislead.

skills.name: Relate processing choices to dimensional change
skills.description: Predict how a manufacturing process will change a part's dimensions, such as shrinkage, warping, quench distortion or stress-relief movement, and plan an allowance for it.

skills.name: Build a functional datum scheme
skills.description: Choose a part's primary, secondary and tertiary datums from how it mounts and works, and dimension its critical features from them.

skills.name: Calculate differential expansion between joined parts
skills.description: Calculate how much two joined parts of different materials change length relative to each other over a temperature range, and its effect on a fit or a fastened joint.

skills.name: Write a function with a clear input-output contract
skills.description: State what a function accepts, what it returns, its units and what it does with invalid input, and make the code keep that promise.

skills.name: Design a boundary-case test
skills.description: Pick test inputs at, just inside and just outside each boundary a function's specification states, and derive the expected results independently.

skills.name: Identify numerical cancellation
skills.description: Recognize when subtracting nearly equal floating-point numbers destroys significant digits, and rewrite the calculation to avoid it.

skills.name: Explain object ownership across a task boundary
skills.description: Decide which task owns data passed between threads or tasks, and whether it is copied, handed over or shared under a lock, so it is never freed or changed while another task uses it.

skills.name: Prevent train-test leakage
skills.description: Split data so no information from the test set reaches training, including through preprocessing, related samples or time order.
